quotes.race: Pontefract Castle Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

Ralph's been aiming her at this and it's worked out lovely. She had a lot to turn around - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: She's consistent and I'm sure something will fall her way again this year. She won the Bronte Cup at York last season and that is the obvious race for her in May. She likes the track and also ran well in last season's Lonsdale Cup. She'll need to improve again to step up in grade, which is possible given she's from a late-developing family. She's training well and is versatile. 15-04-24

quotes.race: Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Dubai Honour has run a huge race in defeat and was beaten by a good mare. He had a horrible run round but whether it would have been enough to turn it around, I don't know - Tom Marquand, jockey.

quotes.race: Longines Hong Kong Vase (Group 1) (3yo+) (Course A) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Dubai Honour was just a little bit keen early and Tom [Marquand] was keen to get him to settle, so he was well back. He has run a hell of a race on ground faster than he really likes, so you've got to be thrilled - Maureen Haggas, trainer's wife.

quotes.race: Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud (Group 1) (4yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: The two Group 1s in Australia were fantastic but to win a Group 1 in Europe was important. Dubai Honour seemed to really enjoy himself today and looked to be travelling well all the way. The ground was probably a bit quick for him but maybe the trip [1m4f] on this ground is more suitable. He seemed to stay the trip really well which gives us another option. On the faster ground he gets this trip really well. William [Haggas] will decide where he goes but he's in lots of Group 1s all over the place. He's just a star of a horse and every time he gives his all. He's so good in his mind - assistant trainer Maureen Haggas.

quotes.race: Grand Prix de Chantilly (Group 2) (4yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Dubai Honour got rushed over ten furlongs in Hong Kong where there's a short run to the first bend. Now he's shown he can go a mile and a half we might look at going back to Hong Kong for the Vase, a race in which they have the whole straight before the turn - Philip Robinson, owner's racing manager.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Every Saturday Money Back Magnolia Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Dubai Honour was a bit fresh and I think the run will have done him the world of good. He's such a grand horse, a sweet one, and that was good. It's nice to get his head back in front. He won a Group 1 only a year ago, but when you do those foreign trips, it takes time to get them back in the groove again. He needs to go after the money and is a slow-ground horse, but did win on faster last year. I think the plan is a Group 1 in Hong Kong on April 28 - Maureen Haggas, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Longines Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Dubai Honour relaxed very well, and I knew when he relaxed well, he would pick up and he picked up well. Anamoe is a great horse, take nothing away from him, but this horse has come forward for being here and he's won well. I think Tom was keen to track Anamoe. The horse was prominent in the Ranvet which is not normally his style of running. He likes to come off the pace - William Haggas, trainer, speaking to Racing.com.

quotes.race: Ranvet Stakes (Group 1) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: I was very much worried about the track, but they assured me it was on the five side of a good four and Chris Waller told me it was fantastic, so we decided to gamble and run, and that was a great result. Dubai Honour had a great year in 2021 but he wasn't quite himself last year. However, he had a very, very good winter and I've been really happy with him - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.race: Longines Hong Kong Cup (Group 1) (3yo+) (Course A) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Dubai Honour ran a really good race and he was just a bit unfortunate with how the race unfolded, which often happens there. When he got out and hit his stride he really came home well. This trip will have taught him a lot and hopefully we'll have a smart international performer on our hands next year - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.race: Qipco Champion Stakes (British Champions Middle Distance) (Group 1)
quotes.quote: Dubai Honour ran a fantastic race. The draw didn't help and then he got a bit set alight. He came from quite a way back with a winning chance but the French horse was just too strong. We might now have a dart at Hong Kong - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Dubai Honour did that well off a gallop which was a bit stop start. He's going the right way and toughed it out - James Doyle, jockey.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (Plus 10 Race) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Dubai Honour has probably been a bit of a slow learner and he did well to finish second at Chester, which is a tight track. He's improving all the time and is a nice horse for the future - Danny Tudhope, jockey.

The Grand Prix de Paris could be next, but we would not want to run him on firm ground on a hot day, so we will play it by ear. There are some important races coming up in the autumn and we want to have him ready for that. He is a very, very good one and we are blessed to have him- Jean-Claude Rouget, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Undefeated star. Too strong George Ryder Stakes at Rosehill. Previous winner in wet here. Suited by the longer assignment now.

quotes.race: The Agency George Ryder Stakes (Group 1) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Autumn Glow is important. Let's not beat around the bush. She's 11 from 11. People are here to come out and see her, and she's got such an amazing fanfare now - it's growing. It's incredible - the feeling you get off these horses, and it's special to witness people pin their eyeballs on her. I thought Anamoe was a big deal. This horse has taken it to a new level. It was evident in the week when Chris said you'll see something special. So when he says that I take notice, because her work's been phenomenal. I truly believe she loves fast ground, because there's not a horse that could come with her. It doesn't matter what is in the race. She's just got an amazing sustained speed, it's quite incredible what we're witnessing. She's the jockey's dream. You get nervous on horses, certain horses throughout your life, and she's one you don't - James McDonald, jockey.

runners.breeder: Nearco Stud Ltd & Rich Hill Thoroughbreds Ltd
runners.owner: Star Thoroughbreds Pty Ltd, Boeara Holdings Et Al
runners.spotlight: Elite performer. Won the Ranvet Stakes at Rosehill two back 21 Mar. On pace and stuck on grittily for narrow Kia Tancred Stakes win at Rosehill. Coming back in distance should suit.

racecards.verdict: If there's a time to try and get Autumn Glow beaten, it seems this race is the one. DUBAI HONOUR is taken as a win and place bet

stable_tour.quote: She is from the crop of Hungerford Stakes winner Massaat and is already in full work. I would say she is about three weeks off a run but is going very nicely. She is not the biggest but what she lacks in size she makes up for in strength. Massaat was good over 7f, and she will be best between that trip and a mile. She is showing us so much speed and we will possibly start off over 6f and then see where we go. I have been pleased with all she has shown me. 25-05-22

prev_owners.owner: Mrs A Williams and Mr A Badri

runners.comment: Well adrift of No Questions Asked and Be Aware at Windsor; hard to recommend
runners.spotlight: Front-runner who made it 2-2 over fences when winning at Cheltenham (2m, good to soft) in October; however, his limitations seem to have been exposed since and he finished well adrift of No Questions Asked and Be Aware at Windsor last time; has had wind surgery but still hard to recommend.

quotes.race: Holland Cooper 'Chasing Excellence' Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We might go straight to Sandown and I think Alnilam will be a better horse on slower ground. If you get into a good rhythm around there it can be hard to peg them back. He's a tough horse and he was brilliant there - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet 'Chasing Excellence' Beginners' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Alnilam jumped well. I wasn't sure he'd take to it as well as he did, which is great. He won a big handicap last season and was second in the Morebattle, so he's not a slouch, and hopefully he can go on to bigger and better things over fences. I'm not sure where we'll go next. There are a few options at Sandown, Aintree or the Grade 2 [Arkle Trial] at Cheltenham. We want him to get plenty of experience and hopefully he might make up into a Graded novice chaser - Olly Murphy, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was very good on his chase debut at Uttoxeter and we have declared him to run at the Showcase meeting on Friday. He was a good handicap hurdler and we'll be looking at all those good novice chases over two miles throughout the season. Hopefully he'll carry on improving. 23-10-25

runners.breeder: S C E A Pa Ouvry & E A R L Ecurie Des
runners.comment: Too free at Cheltenham Festival but consistent prior to that; each-way possibilities
runners.spotlight: Smart form but has won only twice (runner-up seven times); rallied when beaten 1l by No Questions Asked in Grade 2 novice at Windsor (2m, soft; handles good) in January; raced freely and faded in Grand Annual Handicap at Cheltenham last time; the hood is back on today, a tongue-strap is fitted and he may well bounce back to form; if so, he has each-way possibilities.

quotes.race: Get Best Odds Guaranteed At BetVictor Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: We've always thought Be Aware was a nice horse and we know the family well as we've got his older brother Lac De Constance. He was capable of winning so it's not a surprise, but it was just whether he was up to it mentally. Lac De Constance has had a setback and is out for the season, so it's nice this lad has come out and can take over ? he's probably one of the nicer novice hurdlers we've got - Tom Messenger, assistant to Dan Skelton.

stable_tour.quote: He has some high-class novice form and this will be his first time in a handicap over fences, which I think will be interesting in the Grand Annual. 17-02-96

runners.comment: Won three of first five chases but disappointing twice since; lots to find on the figures
runners.spotlight: Won three of first five races over fences, including a Grade 3 novice at Punchestown (2m2f, good to yielding) in October, but has made mistakes and run poorly at Cheltenham and Newbury since; perhaps he'll be revived by a break and cheekpieces, but he has plenty to find on the figures.

quotes.race: BetVictor Novice Chase (Grade 3) (Registered as the Carvill's Hill Chase)
quotes.quote: Jack [Kennedy, jockey] said King Of Kingsfield is relaxing a lot more. He was very keen as a young horse and Jack said he might have won snug if he hadn't nodded at the back of the second-last. I thought it was a good enough performance. As soon as the ground goes soft, you won't see him until the spring. He's won three races now over fences so we can't complain. He had to do the donkey work for the mare last season and it wasn't really fair on him - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Latin Quarter Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: King Of Kingsfield had a couple of hard races last season, but I was delighted with the ground and Jack [Kennedy] gave him a beautiful ride. It was probably a bit unfair he had to do the donkey work for Brighterdaysahead last season, but he'll jump fences now and we'll have fun with him.  I don't think he wants winter-heavy ground, but there's plenty of nice races for him - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Thorntons Recycling Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: We were riding King Of Kingsfield all wrong and the last day we changed our minds. He's been disappointing up until now as I always thought he was a proper horse but he might just come good now. The ground is key to him - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Bar One Racing Royal Bond Novice Hurdle (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Jordan (Gainford)was kicking himself and said he got there too soon. King Of Kingsfield will be a short price in a maiden hurdle the next time! - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: King Of Kingsfield is a good horse and will be a lovely horse with a summer's grass - Gordon Elliott, trainer

stable_tour.quote: There's the option of three races ? the Plate, the Grand Annual and the novice handicap chase. He has plenty of experience, with seven runs over fences, and we'll see what race might suit him best closer to the time.  09-02-26

runners.comment: Doncaster win completed his hat-trick in handicap chases; earns his chance in this Grade 1
runners.spotlight: Flat and hurdles winner but already a far superior chaser; jumped well in front (although sometimes to the right) when completing a handicap hat-trick at Doncaster (2m, soft) six weeks ago by 17l; firmly on the up and deserves his chance in this higher grade.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: After that, Mighty Bandit is going to be rated 150 or more. I didn't realise he had won by 17 lengths, and you have every right to run in a Grade 1 then. He's progressing well and is just high on confidence. We'll be going to Aintree very hopeful and he'll be fresh. It's very exciting - Warren Greatrex, trainer.

quotes.race: Remembering Paul "Stan" Stansfield Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted for Mighty Bandit, he tries very hard. He came with a big price tag and I think he could go for some big handicaps in the future - Eddy Greatrex, jockey.

quotes.race: John Lynch Carpets 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Mighty Bandit looks a nice horse. He did two bits of work and got light, so we've done very little with him since. We didn't really know what to expect but you would have to be impressed with that - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was a €420,000 purchase two years ago and raced mainly on the Flat until we sent him chasing this season. He started over 2m at Newbury, where he came second to Mambonumberfive, who subsequently won the Grade 2 Wayward Lad at Kempton over Christmas. He went back to Newbury last month and won a similar race off a mark of 129. He's a young horse with time on his side, so I'm not too worried about his 4lb rise. He's a strong-travelling sort with lots of scope and might well go for a Cheltenham Festival handicap such as the Kim Muir. 07-01-26

runners.comment: Beaten at 1-4 last time; bottom of the pile on ratings and difficult to fancy
runners.spotlight: Made all in beginners' chase at Exeter (2m1f, good to soft) in December; has run creditably in two 2m Grade 2 events since but he was beaten at 1-4 at Bangor on his latest outing; bottom of the pile on ratings and hard to fancy.

quotes.race: JCB Hydrogen "Chasing Excellence" Beginners' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Mirabad jumped particularly well. It was his first time over fences and I wanted to pop him out and get into a nice rhythm. He can race quite keenly but the hood helped, and the fences backed him off a bit, so it was a good performance. On the rising ground he just relaxed on me. Joyeuse came by me but he's tough and he picked up again - Tristran Durrell, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He's made a great start to his chasing career and is one of those horses who will always give his running, so we'll leave him in the Arkle until the 11th hour to see if it cuts up a little, but at this stage it looks as though there are five or six strong contenders in there and we wouldn't want to turn up hoping to be fifth or sixth. If a few came out, we'd go there looking for the best place we could get, but otherwise he'd be more likely to go to Aintree. 17-02-26

runners.comment: Beat Be Aware at Windsor in January and had a possible excuse at Cheltenham; not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Useful over hurdles and even better over fences; found a bit more improvement when coming from behind to beat Be Aware 1l in three-runner Grade 2 novice at Windsor (2m, soft; handles good) in January; well beaten next time in 2m4f handicap at the Cheltenham Festival, lack of stamina probably a factor; this drop back in trip looks a plus and he wears cheekpieces for the first time (has won when hooded); not ruled out.

quotes.race: Fitzdares Your Personal Bookmaker Lightning Novices' Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: There's loads of improvement to come and I'm delighted to have won a nice prize. At halfway I thought No Questions Asked might get second, but we were helped by Be Aware's jumping. We're a fortunate winner, but jumping is the name of the game and he's run well. He might not end up going to Cheltenham and could end up at Aintree over two and a half miles - Ben Pauling, trainer.

quotes.race: Ascot Underwriting Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: No Questions Asked didn't miss a beat, bar just going down at the last a little bit. I didn't think he'd be that good over his jumps. He's always been a bit haphazard with his hurdles. They're big fences at the moment and he jumped impeccably and put the race to bed relatively easily. It was a good performance. That's probably put him up around the 140-mark and whether or not he goes for the John Francome or not, I'm not sure, but the way he jumped gives me confidence he could acquit himself in a better class of race - Ben Pauling, trainer.

quotes.race: Racing TV Members Day EBF 'National Hunt' Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I wouldn't have necessarily chosen to come out this quick after what was a proper ding-dong at Huntingdon, but No Questions Asked came out of it incredibly well. It was a bit different for him today making the running, so he took a bit of time to work it out, but he won quite nicely. That was his fifth run, so he qualifies for the handicaps at the festival, which it looks like he'll go to, and we've now got four options come March. I think the Huntingdon race will work out very well, it's probably a very strong bit of British novice form from this season. I've always held him in high regard and I think he's very decent - Ben Pauling, trainer.

quotes.race: Sidney Banks Memorial Novices' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: No Questions Asked ran a great race but he didn't jump well enough on the whole. He stayed very well and has two entries at Cheltenham but those races look a bit hot, so we could look at the two-and-a-half-miler at Aintree - Ben Pauling, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's rated 149 over fences now, which is quite high to be winning a handicap, and he might finish with a wet sail in the Arkle. I know how I'd ride him; you'd drop him in and just hunt away, picking up the pieces because he'd finish well. We'll see. He's in very good order and all his preparation is done. He could be one for the two-and-a-half-mile novice at Aintree too, and races like the Plate and the Grand Annual are also options if we need them. 10-02-26

prev_owners.owner: Genetique Obstacle, Haras Du Saubouas & Mme Marine Pineda

runners.comment: Grade 1 hurdle winner here last spring; back on track over fences last time; major player
runners.spotlight: Enjoyed his finest hour over hurdles when winning the Grade 1 Top Novices on this course (2m, good) 12 months ago; beaten at 1-7 on chasing debut in November and again underwhelmed at Leopardstown over Christmas, but a bloodless win at Thurles (2m2f, soft) in February was much more like it; open to further improvement over fences, comes here fresh after missing Cheltenham and has strong claims.

quotes.race: TrustATrader Top Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Salvator Mundi's work at home has been very good. I was disappointed that it had taken him this long to win a Grade 1, but we changed tactics a little bit today and decided to let him get at it, and I think it worked finally. They went a really good pace and Paul got him settled. He jumped well - just a little bit to the right up the straight, but Paul felt that he was correcting himself. That's a good sign that he was able to think about that when galloping at speed. He thinks he's faster than he is - that's what goes on in his head - but he's learning to settle and with more racing he'll settle and he'll be better - Willie Mullins, trainer.I won't lie, over the first and around the bend I was a bit worried - I'd set out to make more use of Salvator Mundi, but when he was settled where he was I stayed there. Cheltenham probably didn't suit him as much as here. We know he has a big engine - he disappointed us at Cheltenham, to be honest, and I wanted to disprove that he wasn't good enough. He was back to himself here, fast ground suited him - Paul Townend, jockey.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Club Moscow Flyer Novice Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Salvator Mundi was fresh and it was messy so I would say it was going to be hard to be impressive. We know he can jump but he didn't jump well today because I couldn't let him. He had to dig in then off the bend on tacky ground in the straight. He had to find plenty. It's hard to be impressive on that ground but at least he won. He'll have to build on it but I think he will. He has gears and on that ground it's hard to use them to the best effect. I'd say a stronger run race on looser ground, wetter ground even, would help him - Paul Townend, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: After his race the other day, you'd be thinking he should go to Cheltenham. However, he's had two disappointing runs at Cheltenham and he won at Aintree last year. We'll have to think more on him. 12-02-26

runners.comment: Beat subsequent Arkle winner Kargese at Cork; top on RPRs with her mares' allowance
runners.spotlight: Useful hurdler and she made a smooth transition to chasing towards the end of 2025, winning two mares' races at Cork (2m5f/2m1f) and beating subsequent Arkle winner Kargese by 16l in the second of them; could not maintain her progress in Grade 1 novice at Sandown in January but nor was she disgraced; top on RPRs with her mares' allowance and should go well.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Scilly Isles Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Kala Conti just struggled on the ground. Everything was a bit of an effort to her and she just wants nicer conditions. It's dead ground and she's not the biggest, so it was hard work - Jack Kennedy, jockey.

quotes.race: Coolmore N.H. Sires Order Of St George Irish EBF Mares Novice Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: She's good mare, got a lot stronger over the summer. Kala Conti is not the biggest but she jumped great. We didn't get to do a whole lot of schooling before she ran here the last day as the ground was so quick. She stays well, we were nervous today back at 2m so we said we would make plenty of use of her. I'd imagine the mares' chase at Cheltenham will be the target. Christmas may come soon, she deserves a little break- Gordon Elliott, trainer, speaking to Racing TV

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Kala Conti was a little bit in my hands early on, but we weren't going much of a gallop. We got going early into the straight and it probably took her a while to get into top gear. She jumped the last three fences very slick and did it well. I was always in or around the same area as Danny, so I had a good eye on him, but I was riding my own race. She was a lovely, consistent mare over hurdles, but the way she jumps a fence, there could be more to come over fences - Jack Kennedy, jockey.

quotes.race: Eventsec Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Kala Conti is not a bad filly and had graded form last year. I thought she might need the run today. She's a good filly - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Mercedes-Benz South Dublin Juvenile Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Kala Conti didn't lose much in defeat at Fairyhouse. It was a good performance and she enjoys a good gallop as she stays very well - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Bar One Racing "Price Boosts Across All Channels" 3-Y-O Hurdle
quotes.quote: Kala Conti is a nice filly. We'll look at the graded race at Fairyhouse in two weeks time. She's pretty straightforward - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She's been a revelation this season. She was brilliant on her first two runs over fences at Cork and probably bumped into a very good horse in the Scilly Isles at Sandown. She's in the Mares' Chase and she could go there, but there are plenty of options for her at home as well.  09-02-26

racecards.verdict: Last year's Top Novices' Hurdle resulted in a smooth success for SALVATOR MUNDI and he now looks to be coming to the boil over fences.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/5 Salvator Mundi, 4/1 Kala Conti, 9/2 Mighty Bandit, 10/1 Be Aware, 12/1 No Questions Asked, 33/1 Alnilam, 40/1 King Of Kingsfield,  Mirabad

racecards.race_name: William Hill Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Hasn't looked a natural over fences but could revive back hurdling (did well last spring)
runners.spotlight: Hasn't looked a natural in his five chases (beaten favourite in Kim Muir last time) but he did very well over hurdles in cheekpieces last spring, finishing second to stablemate Doddiethegreat in the Pertemps at Cheltenham before getting the better of him at Punchestown (2m7f, yielding); could stage a revival back over hurdles.

quotes.race: Conway Piling Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Jeriko Du Reponet has to go back over fences because he's good at it - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Boodles Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jeriko Du Reponet is a very good horse and I really believed he'd canter round today and we'd be talking about coming back here the Henry VIII but I don't think we'll do that for the time being. We've got to go away and regroup. We can always get surprised and fooled, and I'm afraid the horse has done that to us today in every sense. He's 100 per cent and pulled up completely sound. I just think it's a bizarre chapter of circumstances that have contributed to this. I'm sorry, but no one is going to be more disappointed than our team. We've got to correct it and we will - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: SBK Supreme Trial Rossington Main Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The race wasn't run to suit Jeriko Du Reponet. We went too slow and it turned into a sprint. He didn't jump great early - they were going too slow. He was a bit sloppy. I think that's because he thought he was just going for a school round. But when we picked it up into the straight he was electric over the last three - Mark Walsh, jockey.

quotes.race: Coral Committed To Safer Gambling 'Introductory' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jeriko Du Reponet is obviously very smart. We don't know what he's beat, but he's done it as good as he can. I wouldn't like to say about his trip but today he felt speedy enough and he was fine on that ground - James Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: Coral Get Closer To The Action "National Hunt" Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We all know that wasn't the greatest novice hurdle run at Newbury, but Jeriko Du Reponet is the most beautiful horse - he's stunning. His attitude to life is very good and he's a lovely, lovely horse and I'm very lucky to have him - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was a very good novice hurdler and he looked a natural novice chaser -  Nico thought he was our best one to start with -  but we went to Sandown and he just lost it before the race. We had to go back over hurdles, but at least he finished on a good note, finishing second at Cheltenham and then going one better at Punchestown. Chasing really has to be the name of the game, and he's still only a six-year-old, so I think we have to start this season by going down the chasing road again -  I'm pretty confident he'll be top class. If it didn't work, we'd have to look at the three-mile hurdle division. Whichever way he goes, he's still got loads of potential. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Landed gamble in the Pertemps at Cheltenham; raised 9lb but probably even better to come
runners.spotlight: Provided yet another example of his yard's prowess in top handicaps when quite comfortably justifying strong market support in the Pertemps at Cheltenham (3m, good) last month, with seven of today's rivals in behind; raised 9lb but could be capable of even better.

quotes.race: Pertemps Network Final Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: After running Supremely West over two and a half at Aintree, which was a disaster, we said look, we're all in, we're gambling, we're qualified for the race. I said to Jimmy [Fyffe, owner], 'Look, this might happen if you're really patient', and to be fair to the man, he has been. If you have got one you think it can happen with, you've got to be patient. There was a bit going on in the race and he was a bit fresh the whole way, but it was great. Our job is to win, and to win with with ones which can win, and you can win any one, and we're very proud of that. The whole team work hard to get it all to happen. It's not ever as simple as it looks, but it's been an idea since he qualified. I toyed with the idea that he didn't stay and dropped him back in trip last time so see if he didn't stay, but that was obviously the wrong thing and we've built back up to that. I'm very proud of the horse. He had a big chance today and sometimes when the light shines on you, you can crack under the heat, but he didn't - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfred Merry Christmas Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Stayers' Hurdle Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: We've always thought a lot of Supremely West. He's got good form but was too keen last time at Hexham. He loves this ground and although he has the blinkers on, he's so game and honest - Charlie Hammond, jockey.

quotes.race: Racing TV Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Supremely West is a good prospect. We gave him a squeeze along the back and he won well. He's schooled well at home and that was a good performance under a penalty - Charlie Hammond, jockey.

quotes.race: Garrarus Beach (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: It's unreal. I've four point-to-point winners but that's my first on the track so it's great. To be honest, Supremely West hung a bit that's why he raced wide. The lads said he'd stay so I made plenty of use of him and it worked out in the end. I wasn't hard on him, in fairness he picked up well, I'd say he still had a lot more left in the tank - Emily Cody, jockey, talking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: I was wondering if he didn't stay, so I ran him over 2m4f last time, which probably wasn't the right thing to do, and 3m will be more like it. His first run was his best run for us, so we've taken the advice he's offered us, we've got him really fresh, and I'd say he's got a solid each-way chance. 17-02-26

runners.comment: Not obviously well treated back hurdling, so first-time visor needs to make a difference
runners.spotlight: Dual hurdle winner; made a bright start to chasing career when winning a 2m6f beginners' chase at Thurles in November but hasn't built on that in his two runs since and is not obviously well treated now back hurdling in a first-time visor; probably stays 3m.

quotes.race: A.M. Transport Supporting Kill GAA Rated Hurdle
quotes.quote: Eagle Fang has bumped into some smart horses. He would want it soft and I would like to see some rain but the Boodles has been the plan for some time - Gary Bannon, assistant trainer

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late Trevor Hemmings

runners.comment: C&D winner who also scored at Haydock last May; fair fourth at Cheltenham latest
runners.spotlight: Won a good prize at Haydock (3m, good) last May; pulled up on return to action there in November but better when fourth of seven to Ma Shantou at Cheltenham (3m, good) on New Year's Day; being eased another 2lb can only help this C&D scorer but he requires a big career best as a 10yo.

quotes.race: Pertemps Network Long Distance Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I felt off 12st Harbour Lake was maybe a few pounds too high but that was a good, tough performance - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Pertemps Network Handicap Hurdle (Pertemps Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We have a lovely clear run with Harbour Lake this autumn. We thought he would run well today and he has. The Pertemps Final at the Cheltenham Festival has to be an option for him. He is in the Betfair race at Haydock but that is only two weeks away so I imagine that would come too quick so we could work back from Cheltenham - it's a nice problem to have. He wouldn't want a lot of racing and I'd say he would have a couple of runs before the final as that's a nice target - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Lengthen #yourodds Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Harbour Lake is a grand horse, a typical big, fine Trevor Hemmings horse. Whether or not he wants the ground that soft I'm not sure but he has to run on it to get experience. This is only the second run of his life, he's two from two and he's not done a lot wrong - Brian Hughes, jockey.

quotes.race: bet365 Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Harbour Lake is a smashing horse, we've always liked him. If he'd finished in the first four or five we'd have been happy. He'll stay further and he'll learn from the experience - Mick Meagher, racing manager to the executors of the late Trevor Hemmings.

stable_tour.quote: He'll stay hurdling for the time being. Despite the fact he schooled very well at home, he didn't enjoy chasing. He ran some good races back over hurdles in the spring and will start back soon either at two and a half or three miles. We could also try to qualify him for the Pertemps Final. 25-10-24

Although he schooled very well over fences at home, he didn't enjoy chasing so he'll stick to hurdles for the time being. He ran some good races back over hurdles in the spring and will head to Aintree this Saturday for a Pertemps qualifier. 07-11-24

runners.owner: Aisling Byrne & Paul Raleigh & Matthew Cunningham

prev_owners.owner: Aisling Byrne & Paul Raleigh & Matthew Cunningham

runners.comment: Well held at Cheltenham but promising before that and still not fully exposed
runners.spotlight: Third in a Listed handicap over 2m6f at Galway (good) last summer; didn't enjoy much luck on next two starts (still in the lead when falling two out at Haydock in February) but he was well held in a big-field 2m5f handicap at Cheltenham last month; the cheekpieces worn on that occasion are discarded; still not fully exposed, particularly at 3m.

quotes.race: William Hill Betting Done Properly EBF "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Chart Topper is a fantastic jumper, he's so measured. Once upon a time we thought he might be a Cheltenham horse. He got a setback and took a while to get the hang of it again but going jumping seems to have unlocked the potential we always thought he had.   As a bumper horse we thought he'd be a 140-plus horse, his first hurdles performance could have been that and that looks like it could have been that. He could go to the spring festivals but we'll probably keep him going in the summer and he could be a Galway and Listowel horse - Patrick Mullins, jockey.

quotes.race: A J C Group Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: He popped away lovely. Chart Topper's more inclined to pop them rather than have a crack at them, he's clever rather than brave. Jumping has improved him, these Walk In The Park's are natural jumpers. I think he'll go up in trip no problem. - Patrick Mullins, rider, taking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Two wins this term, including here, but only midfield behind Supremely West at Cheltenham
runners.spotlight: Successful over 2m4f on reappearance here (good to soft) in October and has shown better form at around 3m since, including a win at Huntingdon (good to soft) in January; only midfield behind reopposing stablemate Supremely West in the Pertemps at Cheltenham, though.

quotes.race: Sue Ryder Leckhampton Court Hospice Maiden Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: The key move was not committing from three out. It's disappointing for everyone that it's a four-runner race but Ace Of Spades will be progressive. Last season he just improved and hopefully he can this season - Dan Skelton, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won at the start of the season at Aintree over 2m 4f but has definitely appreciated the step up to 3m and won a qualifier at Huntingdon last time. I'm very happy with him and he could be an each-way player. 17-02-26

He progressed nicely last season, having got off the mark over hurdles at Cheltenham's November meeting. We feel there's a little more room for improvement in him over hurdles and we'll look at the longer-distance races with him. The £100,000 stayers' handicap hurdle on Betfair Chase day at Haydock on November 22 is on his radar. There's a good programme for him over hurdles this season and then he'll probably go chasing next term. 22-10-25

runners.comment: Has struggled in both outings since a break but was second in C&D Grade 1 a year ago
runners.spotlight: Second in the C&D Grade 1 novice at this meeting last year; went on to finish first and second in handicaps over the extended 2m7f at Uttoxeter at the start of the summer but well below par both starts since a break, latterly at the Cheltenham Festival; combination of first-time cheekpieces and a return to this C&D needs to spark a revival.

quotes.race: Oddschecker Sefton Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Minella Rescue was a little unlucky last time. We came here thinking that if everything went well for us, he may be top six. We thought 100/1 was a bit embarrassing, so the owners helped themselves to a bit of that. He wants good ground. Now it's out in the open - everyone knows about him. He's got three weeks left as a novice, so it's very tempting to go in a 0-120 novice, but Sean [Bowen] said he had a hard race today, so if he's ok, we'll run him again, and if he isn't, he'll have to wait and run in a handicap. We've got a little race mapped out for him at Galway, at the festival. His jumping's a bit sloppy to go chasing so that might be a bit of a slow burner. He's got a big engine, and that normally counts for most things - Gary Hanmer, trainer.

quotes.race: Grace & Dotty Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Minella Rescue looks exceptional. He was recommended to me by some good scouts and Terence was also very complimentary. I think he's everything they've said he'd be. I've got my eye on the bumper at Aintree but we'll take it day by day so we'll see. We've schooled him and he jumps well but I don't want to run over hurdles until we've exhausted the bumper route. It's very exciting - Gary Hanmer, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A lovely horse who ran at the Cheltenham Festival last time [in the BetMGM Cup]. It was a bit underwhelming, but I don't think the track suits him. He went to Bangor last week to gallop after racing and he's been primed for Aintree again. He ran a super race there last year when second in the Grade 1 Sefton Novices' Hurdle and he'll go for the 3m½f handicap hurdle this time. It's been a stop-start season and the handicapper has had a say, but he wants quicker ground so we've been quite restricted. He's ready to go now. Aintree is his next target and we're toying with Galway after that. 08-04-26

runners.comment: Listed novice chase win despite not impressing with his jumping; lower mark back hurdling
runners.spotlight: Switched to chasing with two wins in the autumn, the latter in a Cheltenham Listed race (3m1f, soft) despite not jumping that well; his fencing once again lacked fluency when sixth in the National Hunt Chase back at Cheltenham (3m6f, good) in first-time cheekpieces (blinkered now) last month; has a lower mark back hurdling, so no surprise were he to go well despite the fact Sean Bowen looks elsewhere.

quotes.race: Sun's "Save Our Bets" Novices' Chase (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Wade Out is lazy, but to be fair he kept finding and that's what you need over these trips. I only think he jumped the way he did because he wasn't going forward. He was going nowhere and that's why he was getting under fences - Sean Bowen, rider.

quotes.race: Richard Davis Memorial Beginners' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Wade Out is a bit slow and a bit lazy but, to give him credit, he keeps finding. He went on from the back of the last and got the job done. He'll probably go up in trip and by the spring he'll be running over three miles or further - Sean Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: Racing TV 100% Profits Returned To Racing Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: You can put a line through Wade Out's last run and he's picked up where he left off. There was probably something wrong with him last time, I don't know what. He ran too bad to say he's not good enough for that grade - James Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: Download The At The Races App Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I think Wade Out is a good horse. I've run him over 2m three times and he's crying out for a trip. We are just trying to sharpen him up for the spring for when he does go up in trip and you'll see a different horse. It's nice to get a third run into him and plot where we're going to go, originally we were thinking of trials day for the 2m4f Grade 2 at Cheltenham in late January - Olly Murphy, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: British EBF "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: Wade Out is a likeable horse who doesn't wow you at home, but he saves his best for the track. He's very laid-back but has a great attitude and hopefully this is the start of a nice hurdles campaign for him. We could certainly look at Cheltenham's November meeting as he's very professional now ? nothing is going to faze him. I'm chuffed with how things are going - Olly Murphy, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: He's one of my better chances of the week. It was too sharp for him around Windsor last time, when he actually ran okay. He'll be fitted with headgear, whether it's cheekpieces or blinkers, and the National Hunt Chase trip will suit him fantastically well. If he can stay in touch and get into a rhythm, I can see him coming home strongly and running very well. He's a bit of an enigma with the way he goes through his races, but he ended up bolting up at Cheltenham in November. He's got plenty of ability and hopefully he can sharp up in the mid-part of the race. 12-02-26

runners.comment: Won first five starts for this yard; fair eighth of 24 to Supremely West at Cheltenham
runners.spotlight: Successful on his first five starts for Paul Nicholls; winning run ended when eighth of 24 to Supremely West in the Pertemps but he did stay on again after getting outpaced; likely to be competitive.

quotes.race: Remix Dry Mortar Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Physically, Absolutely Doyen is improving, but more than anything, mentally he's improving. He's settled into a routine now, is jumping better and I think he'll keep improving. He'll make a nice chaser in time - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I didn't know much about him before he arrived in the summer but he's settled down, learned to jump and going up in trip has really helped. He keeps improving and won very nicely at Musselburgh recently for his five-timer. He's rated 135 and I'm not sure where that leaves him ? we could be sitting here in a year saying he was very well handicapped ? but I could see him running very well. 15-02-26

runners.owner: The 8 Amigos, Readers & Wiggy, N Skinner
runners.comment: Good start over fences but mistakes crept in; now back hurdling (sixth in this last year)
runners.spotlight: Made a good start over fences for new connections, winning at Carlisle (2m, good) in October and second in a Grade 2 novice at Ascot (2m3f, soft); mistakes crept in when below that level twice since and he now reverts to hurdling; sixth of 17 in this last year off an identical mark.

quotes.race: Olly Murphy Racing Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: To see your homebred win is just fantastic. I've bred some nice horses from his dam Tara Rose, but Push The Button is by far the best. He just keeps improving and has achieved plenty for a four-year-old - Jimmy Wenman, owner-breeder.

stable_tour.quote: He was a bit disappointing at Exeter recently after a great run at Windsor. We probably ran him too soon, but two and a half miles on the New track for the Martin Pipe will suit him well. 17-2-25

runners.breeder: Mrs M Pallot & Mr J C Pallot
runners.comment: Progressive on soft this winter but well beaten on quicker ground at Cheltenham since
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 6yo who has made a big splash on his switch back to hurdling this season, winning soft-ground handicaps over about 3m at Cheltenham and Sandown; the form of the Sandown win is particularly strong but he couldn't reproduce it back on good ground in the Pertemps at Cheltenham and conditions may once again not be as soft as he prefers.

quotes.race: From The Horses Mouth Podcast Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's much more nerve-racking than riding. I'm not a good spectator. Kikijo travelled and jumped great and Sean gave him a great ride. I sold him as a chaser but just how the races have worked, we went over hurdles at Aintree and then there was this here, so we'll wait and see what to do next - Richard Johnson, syndicate manager.

quotes.race: BetVictor Cheltenham Non-Runner No Bet Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Kikijo disappointed me over hurdles and I wasn't really sure what trip he wanted, but fences have slowed him down. Now we've got it under the belt we can look to go a bit further in trip - Johnson White, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was very good indeed at Cheltenham last weekend. The plan now is to go to Sandown in a few weeks for a Pertemps qualifier, then just see how we go after that. It would be good to get him qualified just as another option. He could go over fences, although he's lost his novice status as he won at Newbury in February. 20-11-25

runners.owner: Middleham Park Racing & Mrs D J Brown

prev_owners.owner: P Detre, J Detre Et Al

runners.comment: In good form, including third in Pertemps latest, but Sean Bowen still jumps off him
runners.spotlight: Regular winner, including at Lingfield (2m7f, good to soft) and Ayr (3m, soft) this season; very good third of 24 to Supremely West in the Pertemps at Cheltenham (3m, good) last month but Sean Bowen still deserts him in favour of Hold The Serve.

quotes.race: Pertemps Network Final Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Our lad ran a cracker. He'd won two out of three this season and Ikarak qualified for the race. Now he's finished third in a Pertemps at 40-1 - a career best - Ger Tumelty, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Living North Christmas Fair Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was always confident. Ikarak was looking for a bit of company, but as soon as we turned in and they came upsides me I gave him a squeeze and he just lengthened all the way to the line - Bradley Harris, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Sean Bowen looks elsewhere but this 5yo has made steady progress; up in trip
runners.spotlight: Notched a first win for current yard when asserting late on at Plumpton (2m4f, soft) in January and backed that up when second of eight at Kelso (2m5f, good) six weeks ago; Sean Bowen prefers Hold The Serve but this 5yo brings unexposed potential now he's stepping up in trip under Jack Kennedy.

runners.comment: Won two good handicaps in Ireland this term and sixth to Supremely West in Pertemps latest
runners.spotlight: Winner of handicaps at around 3m at Listowel (yielding) in September and Leopardstown (18 runners; good to yielding) in December; bounced back from a lesser effort at the Dublin Racing Festival when sixth of 24 to Supremely West at Cheltenham (3m, good); same mark today.

runners.comment: Staying on when hampered in 2m5f Grade 1 novice at Cheltenham; player on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Useful novice hurdler, including Fontwell wins over 2m3f and an extended 2m1f (both good to soft); also third in a Grade 2 novice at Cheltenham in January before performing with credit in the Grade 1 Turners at the Festival there (2m5f), staying on again when hampered at the last; that suggests this step up in trip could suit now he's handicapping; interesting.

stable_tour.quote: We got him from the Cheltenham sales. He didn't get on the track last season because the ground dried up very rapidly. He came out this season and won his maiden really nicely at Fontwell and he was third at Kempton on Monday.I want to get him qualified for the EBF Final at Sandown in the spring. 01-12-25

runners.comment: Largely progressive, including second in EBF Final at Sandown latest; enters calculations
runners.spotlight: Pair of novice wins over an extended 2m3f (soft/good); flopped in a 3m Grade 2 novice at Doncaster in January but quickly back on the up with an excellent staying-on second of 17 in the EBF Final at Sandown (2m4f, soft; Kaka's Cousin fourth) five weeks ago; well worth another attempt at 3m and has to enter calculations.

quotes.race: Get The Boyle Sports App Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Get On George is a lovely horse. He ran a very good race at Carlisle and he's definitely going to be a chaser - Joel Parkinson, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a lovely horse who's definitely one to watch. He could be the one to go chasing and do something similar to what Grand Geste has done this season - and better. He's got everything - he's fast, he stays, he jumps and he's got a good attitude - and this is his first season in training. It was a very good race at Doncaster last Saturday and it wasn't our day. He's going to be better over a fence. 28-01-26

runners.owner: McNeill Family & The Late Mavis Warren
runners.comment: Progressive; won going away on 2m5f handicap debut, so 3m should suit; major player
runners.spotlight: Flopped on hurdle debut but hasn't looked back since wind surgery, landing a pair of novices before bringing up the hat-trick on 2m5f Kempton handicap debut (good to soft) seven weeks ago; won that going away in a style which suggests he's capable of better again and is likely to be suited by today's longer trip (3m Irish point winner); major player.

runners.comment: Has shown he still retains a good portion of his ability back with Nicky Henderson
runners.spotlight: Back with Nicky Henderson after last season with Laura Morgan; had marks in the 140s at his peak and has shown he still retains a good chunk of that ability in his two outings after a year off, latterly finishing seventh of 24 to Supremely West in the Pertemps at Cheltenham (3m, good).

quotes.race: Sky Bet Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Bold Endeavour wants better ground and he's probably better going the other way, I was pleased that he knuckled down to it like he did - Nico De Boinville, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He was a good old soldier and we had a lot of fun with him, but the handicapper absolutely hit him two seasons ago. He kept running in all those big staying handicaps and he kept running fantastically. They couldn't let his mark down, but he's had time away and he's returned. He wants good ground and, although he's won over fences, he wasn't madly in love with it, so I think we'll stick to hurdles. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Steady progress since upped to 3m; may do better again back from a break.
runners.spotlight: Readily made all in Kilbeggan maiden when upped to 3m1f in August and followed up on handicap debut at Roscommon (3m, good to yielding) in September; even better form in defeat later in the autumn, including fifth of 17 in a notably strong 3m Cheltenham handicap on good; returns from a four-month break as a 6yo who could easily have more to offer.

stable_tour.quote: He put in a good run in the Pertemps qualifier at Cheltenham last time. finishing fifth. He's a real chaser in the making, but he'll have a go in another handicap or novice hurdle in the next few weeks. 11-11-25

runners.comment: Another who ran well in the Pertemps but looks summed up by his mark
runners.spotlight: Another in this field who took in the Pertemps at Cheltenham, finishing a good fifth of 24 to Supremely West; should be competitive again but nothing in his record suggests he has enough in hand to win a race as hot as this.

stable_tour.quote: He's got plenty of ability, but is also very quirky. We'd love to jump a fence with him one day. Whether his mind would let us do that we don't know, but he's a good staying hurdler. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Positive start to handicap career when fourth in EBF Final at Sandown; likely more to come
runners.spotlight: Maiden/novice winner who couldn't justify favouritism but still made a positive start to his handicap career when fourth of 17 in the EBF Final at Sandown (2m4f, heavy; Get On George second) five weeks ago, faring best of those who raced close to the pace; up in trip; remains open to improvement.

stable_tour.quote: He was just touched off in his second point-to-point and the winner has gone on to win a bumper at Cork for Emmet Mullins and Paul Byrne. He's a nice type who we like at home and he'll be running over two and a half miles when we get some soft ground. 18-11-25

runners.comment: Won in small field at Newbury latest but this looks much harder
runners.spotlight: Ridden last ten starts by William Maggs; seventh hurdle win when seeing off five rivals at Newbury (3m, good to soft) three weeks ago but even a 2lb nudge seems likely to stop him in this much more competitive scenario.

quotes.race: Sign Up To Our Newsletter Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Lihyan is not overly big but is well put together and came on leaps and bounds from the last day. He jumped far better today which was one of the goals we got right - Josh Halley, trainer

stable_tour.quote: The change to waiting tactics and a step up in trip have been the key to him. He's won three races over hurdles for us this season. If the ground is decent he could go for the conditional jockeys' race at Aintree, a 0-130 hurdle over 3m on October 27. He should get the strong gallop he needs there and he's certainly capable of winning a better pot than he's been playing for. Now we know he stays, the 3m races at Musselburgh will be ideal for him when the ground goes soft elsewhere. 16-10-24

racecards.verdict: There are several progressive sorts in the bottom half of this field, none more so than HOLD THE SERVE, who can make it four in a row.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 Supremely West, 11/2 Hold The Serve, 6/1 Fortune Timmy, 9/1 Kaka's Cousin, 12/1 Jeriko Du Reponet,  Absolutely Doyen, 14/1 Duke Silver, 16/1 Quantum Quest,  Bold Endeavour,  Get On George,  Good To Be Alive, 20/1 Ikarak,  Kikijo,  Ace Of Spades, 22/1 Wade Out, 25/1 Push The Button,  Idem,  Lihyan, 28/1 Chart Topper,  Harbour Lake, 40/1 Minella Rescue,  Eagle Fang

runners.comment: May well be capable of better than he showed at Cheltenham; stable has won last 4 runnings
runners.spotlight: 11-1 and beaten just over 7l when tenth of 21 in the Turners at Cheltenham (2m5f, good to soft) last month; however, he was kicked at the start that day and may well be capable of better, having finished ahead of the Turners winner King Rasko Grey when short-headed in Leopardstown Grade 1 in February; respected for top Irish trainer who has won the last four runnings.

quotes.race: Tattersalls Ireland Novice Hurdle (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Ballyfad ran a great race. There were no excuses. He did everything right and just got caught on the line. I loved the way he battled to beat King Rasko Grey and just got nutted by Talk The Talk. I was a little bit worried about the ground for him and think on a bit better ground he could be even better. He and [stablemate] El Cairos will go to the Supreme now - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: TRI Equestrian Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: He showed a good attitude. We were a bit worried in his bumpers that Ballyfad looked like he was a bit sluggish in soft ground. Jack said he showed plenty of pace there and was delighted with him. We were worried that he might not be quick enough on it but it was a good performance. We'll get him home and have a chat with Michael and Eddie [O'Leary] and see where we go, maybe the DRF - Gordon Elliott, trainer

quotes.race: Eventsec (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: Ballyfad is probably a horse who will be better with a jump in front of him, but these are all horses for the future. I'll speak to Michael and Eddie [O'Leary, owners] and we will make a plan - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He'll run in the Supreme or the Turners. We haven't made a final decision on which one yet, but you could see him running a big race in the Turners, couldn't you? He's improving all the time and has some rock-solid form against classy horses. Wherever he shows up, he'll make his presence felt. He's a very nice horse and is going to make a smashing chaser. I'm already looking forward to that. 09-02-26

runners.owner: M W Lake & Exors Of The Late N W Lake
runners.comment: Keeping on well in share of third when making bad mistake at final flight at the Festival
runners.spotlight: Three wins from first four starts and he was keeping on well and disputing third when making a bad mistake at the final flight in the Turners at Cheltenham (2m5f, good to soft) last month, ultimately finishing sixth; leading claims on the back of that very promising performance.

stable_tour.quote: He could be a bit of a dark horse, having stepped forward massively on his first run of the season when winning nicely at Ffos Las, and then again at Chepstow. He's always looked very promising and there could be plenty to come. Everything at home has been very positive and I've always held him in high regard. He handles soft ground very well and is a probable runner. 17-02-26

runners.comment: Smooth-travelling sort who could have more left in the tank; each-way shout
runners.spotlight: Improved in this tongue-tie in the winter, winning two handicaps (2m3f, soft), and he may well have completed a hat-trick but for a final-flight mistake in a novice at Newbury (2m4f, good to soft) three weeks ago; this smooth-travelling sort could have more left in the tank; each-way shout.

quotes.race: bettingsites.co.uk New Betting Sites Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Came From Nowhere picked up an injury after his second run over hurdles, so it's been a bit of a long road back. He's been running well without winning, so it's nice to bump into a race we can pick up. We might now look for a nice target for him in January - Jeremy Scott, trainer.

runners.comment: Runner-up in Grade 2 at Kelso in February but work to do with Montemares on that form
runners.spotlight: Point, bumper and dual novice hurdle winner who was second in a Grade 2 at Kelso (2m2f, good to soft) in February; however, he was just over 6l behind Montemares at Kelso, so has work to do today.

quotes.race: Go Racing In Yorkshire Season Ticket Novices' Hurdle (Go North Night Nurse Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: I really enjoyed that, he jumped brilliantly, he was foot-perfect. It was a good performance. He's a solid horse, getting better and better. - Gavin Sheehan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: A point-to-point winner, he stayed on well to finish fifth on his debut for us at Newton Abbot last week. He's good enough to win a bumper before going hurdling. 06-11-24

runners.breeder: E A R L Haras Des Marronniers, D Boin-
runners.comment: Sole defeat over hurdles came when second in Grade 2; others have more substance to form
runners.spotlight: 2-3 over hurdles, with those novice wins (2m/2m3f, good/good to soft) sandwiching a creditable Grade 2 second at Haydock (1m7f, good to soft) in November; this bright prospect is open to further improvement but others have more substance to their form; first run since December.

quotes.race: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com EBF 'National Hunt' Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Masked Man is a very nice horse and this was a bit of a last-minute plan. I was speaking to Simon Munir and Isaac Souede's [owners] racing manager Anthony Bromley and we said this looked a weak-enough contest. It's got him qualified for the EBF Novice Handicap Hurdle Final. We didn't want to go for the Formby Novices' Hurdle, so it'll tee him up nicely to go back into graded company next year. It's nice to have him qualified, but he has a few nice options. We've always held him in high regard and think he'll be the real deal - Willy Twiston-Davies, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Wasdell Group Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: He showed a very high level of ability in his point-to-point and he's done nothing but please us since we've got him. He seems straightforward and we think he's very nice. He'll definitely get two and a half miles but he's shown a very good turn of foot. I'm not sure where we'll go now, whether we'll just want another novice and then look at something else. - Willy Twiston-Davies, co-trainer,

runners.comment: Impressive in 2m2f Grade 2 at Kelso in February and he's one to consider
runners.spotlight: Lost his unbeaten record when fourth of six, beaten about 8l, in the Grade 1 Challow at Newbury (2m4f, good) in December; returned to winning ways in fine style in the Grade 2 Premier Novices' Hurdle at Kelso (2m2f, good to soft) in February; steps back up in trip and in grade this afternoon but he's one to consider after that impressive latest performance.

quotes.race: bet365 Premier Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Montemares is a lovely horse. He's got a great mind and a great attitude and nothing fazes him. Stan Sheppard said 'I made a big mistake in the Challow, I gave him a slap and he took off with me'. I wasn't too worried he was racing behind the bridle today. That's one of the joys of having Stan, he knows the horses inside out and I think he's as good as anyone over an obstacle. He's done a really good job here today - Tom Lacey, trainer.

quotes.race: PricedUp Daily Racing Boosts Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Montemares is still a work in progress, so he appears to have a big engine. He's always shown plenty at home and impressed us away from home. He appears to stay and he's got a bit of boot at the end of his races, as well as a good attitude, so he's got all the right attributes to be a good racehorse. The first race that sprung to my mind for him was the Challow [at Newbury on December 29], but we'll have a look at the calendar. Physically he'll do some filling out, and by default he has to strengthen up, but I don't see any reason to step up in trip at the moment. He should get further in time. I bought him as an unbroken store to go point-to-pointing. He's got a poor scope at rest with his larynx - when he's working he's got open airways, but at rest it's lazy - so I asked Mr Chinn to take a punt on what I thought was potentially a good horse as he wouldn't pass the vet at any auction. It's a nice story - Tom Lacey, trainer.

runners.comment: Beaten 22l in Grade 2 at Kempton but should be better than that; not a forlorn hope e-w
runners.spotlight: Soundly beaten sixth of 12 in Grade 2 at Kempton (2m, good to soft) in February and hard to fancy on the back of that; however, he easily won a maiden at Taunton (2m, good) in January and followed up in a warm small-field novice at Musselburgh (1m7f, good to soft) and his pedigree suggests this step up in trip will suit; might not be a forlorn hope each-way.

quotes.race: 3 February Sporting Clubs Day Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: Onlyforfrankie is a very nice horse who's going to be lovely next year. He's one of the most exciting novices we have. He's got smart bumper form and he's going the right way. I think he's a proper horse and he couldn't have done this any better - Alastair Ralph, trainer, talking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He's won his last two at Taunton and Musselburgh and he'll go to the Dovecote at Kempton in a couple of weeks' time. That's the plan. He was the outsider when winning the Scottish Supreme Novices' Hurdle at Musselburgh, but I wasn't shying away from it. I think he's a very nice horse. I know Captain Hugo, who was the second favourite, fell and some will say the race panned out for us, but he was bang there turning down the back and he won it quite nicely in the end. He's got a big future. 12-02-26

runners.comment: His recent Grade 2 third at Auteuil reads well; this French raider is not ruled out
runners.spotlight: 5yo who is trained in France and has won four of his 17 hurdle starts there; better than ever when close third of six in Grade 2 at Auteuil (2m3f, very soft) three weeks ago behind two previous Grade 1 winners and he's not ruled out; has won on good to soft ground on the Flat.

runners.comment: Cruised into the lead when winning the EBF Final at Sandown; could play a leading role
runners.spotlight: Completed a four-timer (soft/good to soft) and made it three handicap wins in a row when cruising into the lead in the 2m4f EBF Final at Sandown last month; highly progressive and could play a leading role up in grade.

quotes.race: European Breeders' Fund Betfair "National Hunt" Novices' Handicap Hurdle Final (Premier Hcap) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Scorpio Rising goes on that ground very well but he didn't jump that well. It was his first run in a real good handicap where he had no room so he'll only get better. He'll be exciting when he goes chasing next season - Sean Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: Royal Windsor Horse Show Cup Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I knew Harry [Skelton] was going best and I wanted to get past him fast. I got past him before he realised I was coming and then he's tried to edge out when I'm already there and there's not much I can do about that. It was race riding and Scorpio Rising was best on the day - Sean Bowen, jockey.

runners.comment: Flew home for 4th at the Festival; doesn't have the Cheltenham hill but still a contender
runners.spotlight: Improved for the step up to 2m5f when storming home for fourth at 150-1 in the Turners at Cheltenham (good to soft) last month; he doesn't have the Cheltenham hill this time and his stablemate Bossman Jack would probably have beaten him at the Festival had he jumped the final flight proficiently, but this 5yo is unexposed at this sort of distance and could be a contender.

stable_tour.quote: He's had a great season, winning a maiden hurdle at Cheltenham by staying and then staying on well again last time behind Old Park Star. He doesn't come into the race with big numbers behind him but I'm very happy with him, I think he's progressive, will be better for the step up in trip and will outrun himself. There's lots to like. 17-02-26

runners.breeder: His Highness The Aga Khan's Studs S C
runners.comment: Useful on the Flat and things have clicked over hurdles, but further improvement is needed
runners.spotlight: Won four-runner handicap at Sedgefield (2m4f, good) last October and followed up in a warm Newcastle novice (2m6f, good to soft), again with plenty in hand; he's useful on the Flat and could have more to offer in this code now things have started to click, but such improvement is necessary.

quotes.race: Weatherbys And Birdie Calendars 'The French Furze' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Things didn't fall the right way for Zanndabad but hopefully this year they will.  He has the experience, he has been around for a while and hopefully now it's beginning to go right for him- Tony Martin, trainer.

quotes.race: Duke Of Westminster Supporting The Chester Cup (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: It was just bad luck. Zanndabad missed the break and we were always on the back foot. But we're all still here and we live to fight another day - Tony Martin, trainer.

runners.comment: Won big-field mares' handicap at Newbury in good style; needs something extra today
runners.spotlight: Listed bumper winner who built upon previous promise over hurdles when sent up in trip for her handicap debut and winning that 15-runner mares' novice handicap at Newbury in good style; has the 7lb mares' allowance but she still needs to find something extra and can make the odd mistake.

quotes.race: BetVictor British EBF "National Hunt" Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Limited Handicap) (Grade 2) (GBB)
quotes.quote: I thought the step up in trip helped. She was entered at Cheltenham, but Robert [Waley-Cohen, owner] and I felt she wasn't ready, even though she'd run well. This looked a good option. Charisma Cat was a very good bumper filly, but it was her jumping that was the issue earlier in the season. The cheekpieces have sharpened her and it was a good performance - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Mares' Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Charisma Cat didn't seem to handle the bends very well, but she has come back on the bridle. She wouldn't want this ground as it is hard work on the hurdle track. We all felt the one at Market Rasen was one that got away, but she didn't handle the track at all. She got shuffled well back, but she would have won in another couple of strides. We made up for it today, and we got a win, and some black type. If we are happy she will go to Aintree - Alan King, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She's a homebred of the Waley-Cohen family, by Nathaniel, who's one of the most exciting stallions out there, and she won well at Southwell in the summer. She had a break but has come back into strong work and will have another run in a bumper, but we definitely think she's above average. 25-10-24

She's a homebred of the Waley-Cohen family, by Nathaniel who's one of the most exciting stallions out there, and won well at Southwell in the summer. She had a break but has come back into strong work and will have another run in a bumper but we definitely think she's above average. 07-11-24

prev_owners.owner: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier

runners.comment: Kept on well for Triumph fifth and this trip could suit; needs to back up that promise
runners.spotlight: Kept on well for 80-1 fifth in the Triumph Hurdle at Cheltenham (2m1f, soft) and this step up in trip could prompt further improvement; however, two starts ago this 4yo was soundly beaten by Montemares and Kosac d'Oudairies at Kelso (2m2f, good to soft) and he needs to back up his latest promise.

racecards.verdict: Running a big race in the Turners at Cheltenham only to blunder at the final flight, BOSSMAN JACK earns the vote.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Bossman Jack, 7/2 Ballyfad, 13/2 Montemares,  Scorpio Rising, 15/2 Soldier Reeves, 14/1 Charisma Cat, 16/1 Masked Man,  Rooster Crowing,  Lord Byron, 20/1 Kosac d'Oudairies,  Zanndabad, 25/1 Came From Nowhere, 40/1 Onlyforfrankie

racecards.race_name: William Hill Handicap Chase (Registered As The Freebooter Handicap Chase) (Premier Handicap) (GBB)

runners.breeder: Jean-Pierre Dubois & Scea Haras Du Ma
runners.comment: Made mistakes last time but may resume his progress when jumping errors are avoided
runners.spotlight: Good third to Lookaway in the bumper on this card four years ago; spoiled his chance with a couple of mistakes in the Cheltenham Festival handicap won by Grand National contender Johnnywho; however, he split that rival and Deep Cave for useful effort at Ascot (3m, good to soft) in December and may resume his progress when jumping errors are avoided.

quotes.race: William Hill Extra Places With Bog 'Chasing Excellence' Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a lovely performance. Leave Of Absence was really well balanced and handled the undulations of Cheltenham. We thought of going for something like the Badger Beer but he is still a novice until the end of November so we thought it would be nice to run him in a 6- or 7-runner novice chase with a nice value and let him have another go. We have until November if we want to run him in another novice although the way he jumped today, we could also look at the Coral Gold Cup. I loved the way he went about it today and he has a nice profile for the race - Anthony Honeyball, trainer.

quotes.race: Gl Events Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Leave Of Absence wants a trip. He's a relentless galloper. We had to do it the hard way, which is what he had to do in bumpers. We'll gently step him up in trip but for now we'll keep him at two miles - Chris Gordon, trainer.

quotes.race: Run For Your Money At BetVictor Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Leave Of Absence had to go out there and do it the hard way - do the donkey work - but he's a relentless galloper. Making it all the way here with a penalty is really good going. I'll get him jumping over hurdles at home in the next month and then we'll start over two miles next season and step up when we have to. He's a lovely, big three-mile chasing type - Chris Gordon, trainer

stable_tour.quote: He flopped at Cheltenham last time out, so we've got to run some tests on him. I don't think the ground entirely suited and maybe something about making the running in that wind didn't work either, but he's quite an odd character and something wasn't quite right on the day. If he checks out okay we could go back to Newbury for a Grade 2 novice chase as he's eligible for those races only until the end of the month. If he's back on song he could give them a bit to worry about. We could look for a conditions race or some big handicaps after that. 23-11-25

runners.comment: Won the bumper on this card in 2022 and major handicap chase at Kempton last time
runners.spotlight: Landed the bumper on this card in 2022; justified market support in major handicap at Kempton (good to soft; first attempt at 3m under rules) most recently, taking chase record to 3-5 and overall strike-rate to 9-20; remains particularly unexposed over this sort of distance and commands respect returned to Aintree, with further progress plausible.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Trophy Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I live for Lookaway. I can't say that loudly enough. I ride him every day and he's the first one I talk to in the mornings. It's such a shame he missed his novice chase year because he came back with a breathing problem and he had complications with that. Well done to our veterinary surgeon Ben Brain for getting him back to this form, because at one time it looked like he would never be a racehorse again. He had an epiglottic entrapment and needed two procedures to try and correct it, both failed and then we had a third try and fortunately Ben has worked the magic on him and got him back. I've always thought of him from his early hurdling days as a King George-type horse - this isn't a King George but it's three miles around Kempton. We strongly believed that stepping up to three would bring out the necessary improvement and it's worked. He's so gutsy, so game. Jack knows him inside out and has given him a smashing ride. We normally try and make the running with him but we don't have to, as you saw there. He's got three entries at Cheltenham, but it's quite close and today was probably his Cheltenham. I wouldn't be against going up in trip again and the race that would be very interesting at the end of the season would be the bet365 Gold Cup - Neil King, trainer.I am very, very lucky to get to ride Lookaway. He has been around a few years now and has a great will to win - he never really lets us down. He is so used to getting into a war at the front end, so if you change tactics, it can upset the applecart a little bit. Watching The Opening Show this morning, Oli Bell said get to the front and try and slow them down. I couldn't quite manage that but, luckily, I was able to take a nice tow in from the leader all the way. I was always in my comfort zone and then he galloped on strongly and saw it out really well. We had Storming George in the Dovecote before this who ran a bit below par, so we were a bit flat, but this fella has lifted us right back up again. We've been lucky to have this horse for a number of years now. He's won a Grade Two bumper, a Grade Two hurdle and now a big handicap chase on a Saturday - Jack Quinlan, jockey.

quotes.race: Coral "Daily Rewards Shaker" Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's wonderful for Lookaway. As tough and as hard as he is, he deserves it as he's the most genuine horse. Last season we were looking forward to his novice chase season but he had a breathing problem. He might be the best horse in the yard. I hope he's not, but he's very good. In fairness, he's probably been crying out for this trip. I'd rather be sensible and keep him winning rather than going to the festival for a nice lunch. We'll see where we go with him now, there's the Ladbrokes Trophy Chase [at Kempton on February 21] which is possible. I wouldn't be frightened of stepping up in trip again. I think three miles around here would be pretty exciting - Neil King, trainer.

quotes.race: Kalahari King Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was thrilled with Lookaway. I know it's only a two-horse race but it was better than they can be as Personal Ambition is a useful animal. He did everything right there, he did it the hard way from the front and he jumped great. He was always a better horse last year in fast-run races so I'm sure the same will apply now he's chasing. He's such a great jumper, I think we'll see him to better effect over fences. We're lucky that he's very versatile. I wouldn't mind if we went two miles or two miles four with him next time and most ground comes the same to him. He may go to Cheltenham for the Arkle Trial and we have the Henry VIII at Sandown on our radar, but we'll take him home and have a think - Neil King, trainer.

quotes.race: TrustATrader Top Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Lookaway had an off-day for whatever reason at Newbury and we missed Cheltenham. Fortunately he's bounced back to form. Jack gave him a great ride from the front and his jumping was fantastic. You wait until he gets over a fence here next season - Neil King, trainer.

quotes.race: Unibet Greatwood Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Lookaway has done nothing wrong and Jack (Quinlan) has given him a cracking ride from the front. We have won our Grade Two here and he went up 10lb for that, and maybe without that we would have won today, but we will take the Grade Two and finish second today. We might now go to Ascot for the Betfair Exchange Trophy at Christmas and that is what I have got on my mind at the moment. I must admit I thought we would take a lot of catching today, but there was just one who turned out to get past us unfortunately - Neil King, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (Registered As The Sharp Novices' Hurdle) (GBB Race)
