quotes.quote: The only reason Lookaway is not unbeaten is because the yard was so out of form at the start of last season and things just never clicked. He showed again at Uttoxeter he's a serious horse and I'm over the moon. It's just fantastic. It's funny how things swing around, if he'd won a little novice hurdle he wouldn't have been here. But we waited for the new season to start to retain his novice status and all options are open. If was a tough decision coming as he's such a well handicapped horse we felt we should be running in handicaps. It's nice to take on novices. He's got so much class and speed, Jack (Quinlan) couldn't pull him up at the finish - Neil King, trainer.

quotes.race: Weatherbys nhstallions.co.uk Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Lookaway is potentially the best I've ever had, and that's no disrespect to Lil Rockerfeller. Lil Rockerfeller was great and did us proud for years, but he was a three-mile hurdler and I feel this horse will have a bit more speed. When he went to Newbury I'd hardly touched him, but when I gave him a gallop a week before he wowed me. We went straight to Newbury and away he went and won. I knew he'd come on a bundle, but when you come to Aintree for a race like this you don't know what you are taking on. There were a lot of nice horses from big stables who have won their races, and we are a small stable, but he's going to be a serious horse. I'm sure he'll go straight over hurdles next season, and he'll start at two miles, although he'll stay further. He's already won a point-to-point, in which he jumped great. He jumps for fun, and I think he's everything, I really do. He's a point-to-point winner but he has speed. He's a lovely size too - Neil King, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's come out of the Greatwood very well and I thought it was a terrific run from him. We went there thinking we would win but he was beaten by what could be a very progressive horse. I think he'll either go to the Betfair Exchange Trophy or the Tolworth on Boxing Day. We'll see how he gets reassessed on Tuesday but the Tolworth would be quite appealing. 27-11-23

runners.comment: Faller last time; progressive otherwise and has won two notable handicaps this term
runners.spotlight: Faller in the Cheltenham Festival contest won by Grand National runner Johnnywho; progressive otherwise and his record of 5-11 over fences features wins in notable handicaps at Newcastle (2m7f, good to soft) and Wetherby (3m, soft) this term; likely to go well barring mishaps.

quotes.race: William Hill Rowland Meyrick Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Konfusion is a good horse. He's on the up and it's nice to have a good winner for Anne, who's been a long-standing owner of ours and been with us through thick and thin and had no luck for a couple of years. The Ultima could be his target. We'll look at the options but we're going to have to give him a run around Cheltenham to see if he likes the track. He seems to like these flat, galloping courses and that's my only worry with him. And the way you've got to ride him, round Cheltenham he'd be there to be shot at.  We could possibly enter him in the National. If he keeps improving we'll see how good we are - he'd be borderline to get in after that - Joel Parkinson, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: BetMGM Rehearsal Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Konfusion is a lovely horse and the soft ground has helped him. It was a bit of a freak at Haydock last week but it's kept him fresh and if he'd won that he wouldn't have run today so it's worked out - Joel Parkinson, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Entertain In Style At Wetherby Racecourse Handicap Chase (Go North Monet's Garden Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Konfusion got a slight strain, nothing serious, which was why he's been off since Sedgefield and we hoped he'd be fit enough. He's a nice horse - Joel Parkinson, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: The ground in the Peter Marsh went against us and it wasn't a true staying test. He was giving weight to the two horses who finished in front of him and on soft ground it would have been a completely different result. We were still impressed with him and we've come away knowing we've probably still got a little bit in hand granted the right conditions. The way he won the Rehearsal at Newcastle surprised us as he did it so easily against good horses. Then the Rowland Meyrick was a strong enough race with the right horses in it. He's got a Cheltenham Gold Cup entry, but we haven't made any concrete plans. He's come out of Haydock well and he'll have two more easy weeks and then we'll discuss it. The weather and likely competition could dictate things and we're not closing any doors. The Ultima has to be an option and there's Aintree. 28-01-26

runners.comment: 3 wins over conventional fences here; 3m1f win this January but this trip is a big unknown
runners.spotlight: Novice campaign last season went well, notably over the conventional fences here where he registered three handicap wins (2m/2m4f) and was second at this meeting (3m1f); resumed progress with a win at Haydock (3m1f) this January but badly hampered at the Cheltenham Festival; this trip is a big step into the unknown but he needs a second look.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Peter Marsh Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Imperial Saint has got form on the ground and I thought it would play to our advantage, and possibly disadvantage one of two of the others. I had no worries about the trip on that ground. I thought we'd potentially have more of a turn of foot than some of the opposition. I think there's still improvement to come. He's run four fantastic races at Aintree and I'd certainly be heading that way rather than Cheltenham. I think he'd definitely be worth an entry in the National - Johnson White, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Handicap Chase (Registered As The Freebooter Handicap Chase) (Premier Handicap) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Imperial Saint has been progressive all year, winning three here, and that was another step in the right direction. Hopefully there will be more to come again next season. He has to go left handed and he might start in the Paddy Power, as he's effective over two and a half - Philip Hobbs, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Betting Done Properly Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Imperial Saint definitely seems to enjoy it round here and it was the obvious race for him. We knew he'd get further and he's bounced back. We were a little bit disappointed at Newbury but maybe two miles round there was a bit too sharp for him. He's jumped, travelled and done it really well. He's going to go up in the handicap again and it's not going to be easy for him, but it's lovely to have a horse of his quality for our syndicate - Richard Johnson, syndicate manager.

quotes.race: Jason Salleh Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I didn't see what happened to the other horse, but I felt I was just getting back on top coming to the last. I was very comfortable the whole way and Imperial Saint jumped really well. He's had the point-to-point experience and he's a forward-going type, so we used that experience. He stays really well - Micheal Nolan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He ran okay the other day in the Old Roan at Aintree. They went off pretty quick and he just never really got into a rhythm. We've put it down to the fact it was his first run of the season and he might have just needed it. I think two and a half miles is his right trip, although he'll get further, as he proved at the Grand National meeting. We're looking at the December Gold Cup next. 20-11-25

He did well for us over hurdles last season, winning twice, at Ludlow and Ffos Llas, and finished in the first three in all of his five runs.  We were over the moon with his win at Aintree on Sunday in his first run over fences when he jumped very well throughout. He's owned by the Richard Johnson Racing Club and he gave his owners a great day. We think he'll get further in time but we'll stick with 2m with him at the moment and try and find another race for him in a couple of weeks' time. He's one we're looking forward to. 30-10-24

runners.comment: A fluent fourth in the Topham over these fences last April; ran creditably once at 3m4f
runners.spotlight: A fluent fourth in the 2m5f Topham over these fences was the first of three big runs in good handicaps last April-July; ran creditably in one (Sandown in April 2024) of his three attempts at 3m4f-3m5f and excuses might be made for his latest two outings (first cross-country, then the mud) but other candidates are more persuasive.

quotes.race: KilbegganRaces.com Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: I expected Amrite to win last time but I'm not convinced he loves real heavy ground. We waited for better ground after giving him a break. He looked really well today. The plan was to leave him in the field but we may look to a novice hurdle.

stable_tour.quote: He won the Midlands National at Kilbeggan and was fourth in the Galway Plate this summer. He was meant to go for the cross-country chase at Cheltenham this week but that has been cancelled, so he'll probably now go for the one in December. The aim is to run in the Cross Country Chase at the festival and then hopefully on to the Aintree Grand National. He's in great form. 11-11-25

He made a winning debut over fences at Fairyhouse this season from stablemate Secret She Keeps before making the frame in two Graded races. He has entries in the Brown Advisory Novices' Chase and the Kim Muir Handicap Chase and will go for one of those. 01-03-23

runners.comment: Looks worth a crack at this new trip but quirky and comes with risk
runners.spotlight: Useful handicap chaser at up to 2m5f, albeit quirky and having saved his winning in this sphere for Kempton; admittedly right up to best in Ascot contest on penultimate start; last two efforts suggest this new trip is worth exploring but he comes with some risk, especially in such a competitive field.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Daily Extra Places Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Bad didn't miss a beat today, he's always been very economical with his jumping. He was very unfortunate to fall at Ascot when he was going very well, but today was deeper race than the last day. We went a good gallop from the start and it probably worked out better for him, because I had a lead for longer. Once I got upsides Tristan [Durrell on Flegamatik] coming down to the last, I didn't know how much my lad wanted it, but he had a good jump and I just held on. It was do or die at the last. If I missed it and Tristain winged it, he was going to win, and vice versa. That's what won it for us in the end but he has loads of ability. He's one of the yard favourites and a hell of a character at home, so for him to get his head in front twice now, it's brilliant. If he gets out of bed on the right side then he's got loads and loads in hand - the days he doesn't want to do it then he won't - Ben Jones, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: I was delighted with his seasonal reappearance at Kempton. We took the headgear off and we weren't overly fussed with how he ran - we wanted him fit and ready for the Paddy Power. But he was great and he's showing a more willing side to himself these days. 07-11-25

runners.comment: Needs to prove he retains ability in this second run back from long layoff
runners.spotlight: Shaped as if in need of the run, en route to taking a late fall, at Kelso six weeks ago on debut for new stable and first start since finishing sixth in the 2024 Grand National; landed a major Irish handicap that year but needs to prove he retains peak ability.

quotes.race: Goffs Thyestes Handicap Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: The stewards have just asked me for the reason for Ain't That A Shame's improvement in form, but we genuinely we didn't know (at Navan) and were very disappointed - Henry de Bromhead, trainer.

quotes.race: Holden Fleet Management Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Ain't That A Shame deserved to win. It was a good performance and I couldn't be happier. He handles those conditions and it was a perfect race for him - Rachael Blackmore, rider.

quotes.race: I.N.H. Stallion Owners EBF Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Ain't That A Shame jumps and stays well, is a scopey big horse who has taken time but it is nice to see him come to himself. We'll look at the festivals and the three mile options, maybe the handicap hurdle at Fairyhouse. I'm looking forward to getting him over a fence next year - Henry de Bromhead, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was a bit disappointing in the Troytown for whatever reason. We'll get him checked out and see if anything shows up. That wasn't his true form. 20-11-23

He has run two big races in defeat this season with a head second in the Munster National and a good fourth to Real Steel in a big handicap at the Leopardstown's Christmas meeting. His big target this season is the Grand National, which I think should suit him as he stays 3m well and gives the impression he'll get further. He could have a run beforehand but it wouldn't be a problem if he went straight to Aintree. 01-03-23

runners.comment: Possibilities provided he taps back into the progress that culminated in 2025 Ultima win
runners.spotlight: Four falls in 15 career starts reflect that he's sometimes an iffy jumper; broadly disappointing this season, most recently at the Cheltenham Festival when bidding to repeat a 2025 Ultima success (3m1f) that was impressive and promised even bigger things to come; needs a turnaround but he has clear possibilities provided earlier progress is resuscitated.

quotes.race: Ultima Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We knew that if Myretown jumped round, he was phenomenally well-handicapped; I just didn't know if he was going to be man enough, and it's very exciting that he is. He's a novice horse, his jumping has been a bit hit and miss, he turned upside down at Windsor, but since then we ran him at Kelso and he's got his confidence back. He's a bit different to Corach Rambler - he jumps so exuberantly. Corach is just a different sort of horse, but this is a phenomenal horse - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

quotes.race: Every Horse, Every Race, At timeform.com Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Myretown was much more grown up today and that opens options up for us. I'd like to keep Derek [Fox] on him so we wouldn't go for the Kim Muir or anything and we'll look at a novice chase at Uttoxeter after Cheltenham - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He flew the flag for us last season by winning at Cheltenham. He'll start off in the Coral Gold Cup, but he'll have a couple of racecourse gallops before Newbury. He's got to take another step forward, but he's got the profile to do so. He couldn't have been any more impressive in the Ultima, albeit off a mark that in a normal year wouldn't have got him into the race. He's got a long way to go and perhaps Grand Nationals are more realistic than Gold Cups, but he's very lightly raced. With Corach Rambler, the Ultima was a good Grand National trial and that's in the back of our minds. 29-10-25

runners.comment: 2-2 over fences at Aintree, namely wins in this race for the last two years; respected
runners.spotlight: Has failed to show his form in both outings this term but a revival looks highly likely back at Aintree on return from four-month break; 2-2 over fences at this venue, namely wins in this race for the last two years (good/good to soft); had a similar prep when winning by 5l off just 1lb lower 12 months ago; commands respect in the hat-trick attempt.

quotes.race: William Hill Handicap Chase (Registered As The Freebooter Handicap Chase) (Premier Handicap) (GBB)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted to be able to get Cruz Control back on track - he'd completely lost his way. He ran ok in Punchestown, and Stan [Sheppard, jockey] just said to me afterwards, 'He's proper tired', and it's taken until now to get him really back on song. We mixed it up at home - took him to the beach, jumped the Aintree fences at Lambourn with him, and I'm so delighted for the owners, who are great supporters of mine. We've sweetened him up - did more slow work, gave him some away days, and the sun on his back - Tom Lacey, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Handicap Chase (Registered As The Freebooter Handicap Chase) (Premier Handicap) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Cruz Control missed the ditch in the home straight the second time but otherwise he jumped pretty economically, fast and effectively. It was a good performance. He was unlucky to lose at Doncaster and he got chinned at Newcastle on another occasion but otherwise he's not done a lot wrong this season. He appears to be slow but he's such a big, long-striding horse he's covering ground - he's taking one stride to other horses' two. I've been reluctant to step him up to three miles because although he's seven he's still a frame. We've given him time to mature and I think he'll just get better and better, hopefully - Tom Lacey, trainer.

quotes.race: Sportvision Stadia & Event Branding Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought Cruz Control jumped much better compared to how he jumped at Ascot, where he was just running into fences. We did a load of schooling with him at home over some poles and he's tucking his front end up so much better. He's a horse that's still to do some maturing - he's got such a big frame and has been such a hollow horse - and hopefully he can go on from here. If he can jump with accuracy he could go up in trip - Tom Lacey, trainer, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: racingtv.com Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Cruz Control is a fine horse. Two-and-a-half miles around Cheltenham just didn't suit him and he jumped okay today, but I got a free lead. It's a cliche but we'll see the best of him over a fence - Stan Sheppard, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He's a big, tall, angular type who has done nothing wrong, winning his bumper and scoring twice over hurdles. However, he's always been a real chaser in the making and got off the mark on his third attempt over fences at Newcastle, where I was much happier with his jumping following plenty of schooling. He followed that up with a good second at Doncaster on Saturday and the result might have been different had he been a little bit quicker over the last few fences. He'll get better in time, is constantly filling his frame and seems to handle most ground. I think he's progressive. 20-12-23

prev_owners.owner: C B Woods & Mr N Doolin

runners.comment: Possibly best to forgive latest effort; won over hurdles on this card 12 months ago
runners.spotlight: 3m hat-trick in 2025 started with a success over hurdles on this card (good) and ended with nabbing Leave Of Absence on the line in notable handicap chase at Ascot (good to soft); couple of backward steps since but a bad early error, and perhaps losing a shoe, contributed to a poor effort last time; may well rebound on a significant day in his calendar.

quotes.race: William Hill Top Price Guarantee Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's very special to have winners at these meetings, but we didn't have anything for Cheltenham and we've come here with just the one runner, so for Deep Cave to go and win is great. The owner [Caolan Woods] has been patient all year. He had a break to freshen him up and then we targeted this meeting. It's probably taken us a long time to figure him out, but we thought he'd be better on nice ground and he's going to be very special over fences next year. He won a novice chase in France, so he's not a novice, but he'll hopefully be a Saturday horse - Christian Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Savills Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Deep Cave is a lovely horse who we always liked. Rachael gave him a super ride. In fairness to Ciaran Murphy, he recommended him to us after winning his point-to-point. Davy Russell felt he went a bit soon the last day so we said we'd take our time here. We'll look to the spring and see what's there - Henry de Bromhead, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A nice young horse that I like. He's been doing things nicely at home and we'll find him a suitable maiden hurdle over the next few weeks. 14-11-22

Having been a good second of 22 on his debut at Punchestown, he opened his account at Leopardstown over Christmas and that form has been franked since. We raised his sights last time for a Grade 1 at the Dublin Racing Festival and he ran another promising race. He's likely to be saved for Punchestown. 01-03-23

runners.comment: Irish 7yo who is still reasonably unexposed and looks interesting back up in trip
runners.spotlight: Irish 7yo whose broadly progressive form switched to chasing this season features a comfortable win at Roscommon (sole attempt over 3m1f; good) in the summer and good second in Thurles handicap (2m5f, yielding) last time; still reasonably unexposed and looks interesting back up in distance.

quotes.race: Horse & Jockey Hotel Rated Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Brave Fortune won his point to point and has done everything well but it has really taken until now to come to himself. We have a high opinion of him - Pat Doyle, trainer

quotes.race: I.N.H. Stallion Owners EBF Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: I thought Brave Fortune was capable of doing that but he has been disappointing. He appreciates the ground and if the ground stays the way it is, we'll look for the 2m4f winners' of one race at Thurles in the coming weeks. He is a lovely big horse who cost a lot of money and we were always hoping he'd do something like that - Pat Doyle, trainer.

runners.comment: Ideally needs assistance from the weather, having gained all wins on soft ground
runners.spotlight: 1-6 over fences, the success at Aintree (2m4f) on seasonal debut; seemed a non-stayer in the Welsh National before eventually falling, then ran below form at Cheltenham (2m4f); return to this venue may have a positive effect but he ideally needs assistance from the weather, having gained all wins on soft ground.

quotes.race: William Hill Racing Winnings Boost Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a pretty good performance. Uncle Bert needs three miles and the soft ground helps. His jumping wasn't quite right last season but he's matured and it's definitely back now. He's got an entry in the Welsh National and we'll go away and have a think -  Nigel Twiston-Davies, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Cheltenham Non-Runner No Bet Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Stayers Hurdle Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I've got a good strike-rate on Uncle Bert. He's done it nicely, over three miles he just keeps going. It's easy on him, bounce him out and he just keeps going. He was tough - James Turner, rider.

quotes.race: Dragonbet Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was a lovely pot to win. Uncle Bert is a very consistent horse and never seems to let us down. We're very pleased for owners James and Jean Potter, who support us a lot and also bred him, as well as standing his sire Pether's Moon - Willy Twiston-Davies, trainer's assistant.

runners.owner: Andrew Peake, Simon Macauley & Bryant Family

prev_owners.owner: Andrew Peake, Simon Macauley & Bryant Family
Exors Of The Late Magalen O Bryant & Mlle Muriel Caslant

runners.comment: French jumper; ran well in top race in 2024; not in the same form since
runners.spotlight: French jumper who bagged Grade 3 honours and finished a good fourth in the Grand Steeple-Chase de Paris in 2024; however, has failed to match that form since and, judged on recent RPRs, has something to prove off his mark in this very warm handicap; first British attempt.

prev_owners.owner: Walters Plant Hire & James & Jean Potter

runners.comment: Formerly useful but looks far from solid on his form this season
runners.spotlight: Formerly useful but looks far from solid on his form this term, latterly switched back to chasing (from hurdles) for another new yard; beaten long way, behind some of today's opponents, in Cheltenham Festival handicap most recently.

quotes.race: Matt Hampson Foundation Silver Trophy Handicap Chase (Grade 2) (A Limited Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We're pleased with that. Stolen Silver was fourth here at the festival and has come back and finished the season on a high note. He'll go out to grass now and we'll see what Sam [Thomas] and Dai [Walters] say but we could look at the October meeting, but certainly November - James Potter, part-owner.

quotes.race: Urbano By Symphony Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Stolen Silver didn't miss a beat with his jumping. He's very free-going and the ground helped him, he bounced off it - Charlie Deutch, jockey.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Supreme Trial Rossington Main Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: I was worried about getting third place at the last with Stolen Silver but Sam got another gear out of him. He's a nice horse and the Betfair Hurdle might be his next race - Nigel Twiston-Davies, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's lost his way since the Coral Gold Cup last season but the ground has been quick both times he's run since, which he wouldn't have enjoyed. We're on a bit of a recovery mission with him at the moment, but he's sound and well and we may just have a spin over hurdles in the next two or three weeks on some softer ground. He's got lots of ability, we just need to recapture some form. 25-11-24

He's been a dude for the yard. We stepped him up in trip this season and he won the Native River Handicap Chase on his first start at Chepstow. He then ran well in the Coral Gold Cup and just found it all a bit too much pace wise. He needs to be in his comfort zone. He came back a little bit sore. He's a lovely horse to aim at some of the big handicaps this campaign. 05-01-24

runners.comment: Seemed non-stayer in a 3m attempt; stamina to prove back up from 2m4f
runners.spotlight: Novice chaser who has several pieces of sound form at up to 2m4f this season, including a second at Aintree; however, below that level in major handicaps in two of his last three starts, seeming a non-stayer at Doncaster (soft) in the sole 3m attempt; stamina to prove back up in trip.

quotes.race: Wasdell Group Silver Trophy Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was very insulting to see Josh The Boss priced up initially at 33-1 but a few people saw sense. He was very well handicapped on his form and we targeted this thinking he was very well in. He could go chasing but we'll see what to do -  Willy Twiston-Davies, assistant to trainer Nigel Twiston-Davies.

quotes.race: BoyleSports Supports Safer Gambling Week EBF "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm absolutely over the moon. I was moaning when they took the hurdles out because that's John The Boss's strength. He's a proper National Hunt horse. I think we'll take it steady - we'll go and win the Challow and then we'll come back here in April for the Mersey Novices' Hurdle. It will be ten years since Splash Of Ginge got chinned in the Mersey by a length and we'd like to right that wrong - John Neild, owner.

quotes.race: Hazelton Mountford Insurance Brokers Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Ever since Willy (Twiston-Davies) broke Josh The Boss in we thought he might be the one to bring us back to the big days. This is only a fraction of what he is capable of. It is hard to get back to where we were, but this could be the one that helps us cling on to that dream. We will give him another small run in a novice with a penalty to give both him and Jamie some more experience - John Neild, owner.

runners.comment: Well treated on best chase effort and looks open to improvement back up in distance
runners.spotlight: Four-time hurdles winner, including in one of only two attempts at 3m; campaigned over 2m4f/2m5f switched to fences this term, best effort when third behind very notable rivals in graduation chase at Haydock; well handicapped on that bare form and could be open to any amount of improvement back up in distance; a typically interesting runner of his type for the Skeltons.

quotes.race: 'Rasen Rocks' Featuring Ella Henderson Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: The extra distance helped Mr Hope Street. He's a big, backward horse and is still pretty raw. He's very much a work in progress and I think he'll improve nicely to go again. The penny still hasn't dropped yet - Harry Skelton, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He was very consistent over hurdles and ran satisfactorily on his first run over fences in a hot 2m5f novice handicap chase at Carlisle. They went very fast that day and he was taken off his feet early on, but there's a lot more to come from him, especially when we go up to three miles. 10-11-25

He's a good, solid horse and has given us some great days out when climbing the handicap ranks over hurdles. He's going chasing this season and it looks like that's what he's made to do. He's a big lad and I'm looking forward to seeing him over fences. 22-10-25

runners.comment: Made all at Cheltenham in December; unable to dominate in the same way since
runners.spotlight: Has form at 3m1f; made all in major handicap at Cheltenham (2m4f) in December; unable to dominate in the same manner and eventually pulled up in all three outings since; had wind surgery (his second) since latest; wears new headgear; again far from certain to have his own way.

quotes.race: Support The Hunt Family Fund December Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Glengouly is a star and I couldn't have been any happier with where Sean [Bowen] had him and the speed he was going. I know this horse inside-out and could tell he was loving it - Faye Bramley, trainer.Glengouly was out of the handicap but Faye [Bramley] and AP [McCoy] obviously know what they're doing. Faye is a very good trainer and AP said to my agent that he had a massive chance. When someone like that is telling you he's got a big chance, you trust in it. Hopefully AP will think I'm better from the front now as well! He had some good form here and stepping up to two and a half miles has really suited him. He got in a really good rhythm - Sean Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: Richard Brennan Fencing Services Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Glengouly jumps well at home and I think he can jump better than he did today but he got a good start and kept it up. When the mare came at him he picked up again which was nice to see - Willie Mullins, trainer

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction Novice Hurdle (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Glengouly got a lovely ride from Jack. He got him settled going down the back and produced him nicely. I thought this trip might be a bit short for him. I love the way he jumped and he'll be prepared for the final of this series at Punchestown - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Ladies Auction Maiden Hurdle (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Glengouly was a bit idle in front, he was looking all around him. I wouldn't be afraid of going out in trip with him, he will go 2m6f or 3m next time - Willie Mullins, trainer.

runners.comment: Posted duck eggs on last two starts but is in excellent hands and may yet resume progress
runners.spotlight: Irish 7yo who was successful last August/November in first two chase attempts, including at Kempton (3m, good); something to prove in this scenario, having posted duck eggs in competitive handicaps on last two starts, but in excellent hands and may yet resume improvement; not written off.

racecards.verdict: Being fresher than most and still unexposed over fences, BRAVE FORTUNE may be the answer. Mr Hope Street is second choice.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Mr Hope Street, 11/2 Cruz Control, 6/1 Deep Cave,  Brave Fortune, 13/2 Lookaway, 11/1 Leave Of Absence,  Konfusion, 16/1 Josh The Boss,  Chance Another One, 20/1 Bad,  Uncle Bert, 28/1 In Love, 40/1 Glengouly, 66/1 Ain't That A Shame, 100/1 Stolen Silver

runners.comment: Some respectable runs in Grade 2s this term but pulled up in the Stayers' Hurdle last time
runners.spotlight: Won the Pertemps Final at Cheltenham (3m, good to soft) last March and some respectable runs in Grade 2s this term; wore blinkers when pulled up in the Stayers' Hurdle at Cheltenham last month and is back in his usual cheekpieces this afternoon, but he still has something to find.

quotes.race: Conway Piling Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Doddiethegreat ought to go up into the Graded races now - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Pertemps Network Final Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Nico [De Boinville, jockey] said make sure Doddiethegreat has loads of light, which is a little bit alien to me as I like to be glued to the inner. He got in a good old rhythm, I was just following Sean Flanagan everywhere. I missed the second last and I was getting there sooner than I wanted, but I had a willing partner - Brian Hughes, jockey.

quotes.race: Give The Gift Of Ascot Membership "Introductory" Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a horrible injury at Kempton when Doddiethegreat won his only hurdle race. He severed a tendon. This race has been on the horizon since the spring, because of the conditions. It's satisfying for everyone. He runs for the Doddie Weir foundation, which is terrific. Kenny 'Honeysuckle' Alexander is a great character and I can tell you where he's being aimed because I got a text from him last night. We're preparing him for the Scottish Champion Hurdle - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Racing TV Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: All prize-money won today between myself and the guv'nor, and my riding fee as well, all goes to the Doddie Weir's foundation in support of motor neurone disease. It's a great cause and Kenny Alexander has named Doddiethegreat after a great man and I think he's a fantastic advert for it. The more awareness he can raise the better and he's a fantastic horse as well. It's not easy to win a bumper with a penalty. He'll go hurdling next season - Nico de Boinville, jockey.

quotes.race: Ludlow BCD "Newcomers" Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It looked a good race, we didn't go much of a gallop. It was good to be front-end, Doddiethegreat is a nice horse and he knuckled down all the way to the line. He's a bit of a frame at the moment but he's coming on nicely and is definitely one for the future - Nico de Boinville, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: This campaign has all been about winning as much prize-money as possible for the Doddie Weir Foundation. Our objective has been hard, because he's very hard to place over hurdles. He was great at Cheltenham last year, winning the Pertemps, and he ran a brilliant race at Punchestown. He's not quite a Grade 1 horse, but you never know. When he's right, he's very good. 18-02-26

runners.comment: 12yo who won his last two hurdle starts last summer but is very much up against it today
runners.spotlight: 12yo who won his last two hurdle starts last summer (3m, good/good to firm), looking as good as ever; however, he's very much up against it in today's company; down the field on the Flat last September when last seen.

quotes.race: RBC Brewin Dolphin Hurdle
quotes.quote: Happy Jacky is as tough as boots and I thought he was beaten three times. He battled back well to the line and Peter was brilliant on him - Mark Fahey, trainer.

quotes.race: Grant Thornton Ulster Cesarewitch Handicap
quotes.quote: Happy Jacky kept on finding and he gives it to you when you need it. I got him rolling up the hill, which probably isn't the best thing to do, but one thing Mark said was don't give them a chance to quicken by you. So I was happy enough to go earlier and get beat rather than go later - Ronan Whelan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Beaufort Golf Club Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We fancied Happy Jacky today, we thought he would take a bit of stopping. I got a lovely split through, the horse in front kept jumping to his right, so I got a lovely gap. It was nice to get it - Bryan Cooper, jockey.

quotes.race: Giantsgrave Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Happy Jacky toughed it out well on his last chance in that grade. I would say that trip is the shortest he would want. I might give him a pop over a fence before the ground turns heavy - Ray Hackett, trainer

quotes.race: David Heneghan Memorial Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was worried that the ground might have gone for him but he's a hardy little lad and got through it alright. He wouldn't be in love with it, but is tough. It didn't work out when he got boxed in at Killarney and got no run but he finished out his race really well. After two quick runs we'll give him a little rest, although he could go to Listowel - Ray Hackett, trainer of Happy Jacky

runners.comment: Gave it a very good go from the front when 7th in Stayers' Hurdle; again looks vulnerable
runners.spotlight: Career highlight when winning the King George over fences at Kempton in December 2023; won two conditions hurdles last year; gave it a very good go from the front when seventh in the Stayers' Hurdle at Cheltenham (3m, good) last month following wind surgery but this 11yo is probably vulnerable once more.

quotes.race: www.thurlesraces.ie Hurdle
quotes.quote: It's great to get Hewick back in the winner's enclosure again, and it was a great first run for the season. I can't thank TJ [McDonald, owner] enough for letting me up on him again; he's been some servant for us. He loves jumping, and that has only really come in the past year and a half with him; he's really attacking his fences and hurdles. In the Grand National, he didn't miss one bar the Canal Turn; it's like he's getting better. He's some horse - Shark Hanlon, trainer.

quotes.race: Randox Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I couldn't have had a better ride off Hewick. He travelled great but it probably took him a circuit to figure out the fences and on the second circuit I got a much better ride from him. He'd figured them out and was clever. I was getting excited after the Canal Turn. I thought I could get the job done and it was just conserve, conserve. I thought we might relive that moment in the King George and just outgrind them, but I kind of knew my fate going to the third-last and it wasn't to be. He's come back safe and sound though and just needed a sprinkle of water - Gavin Sheehan, jockey.

quotes.race: Jimmy Neville Memorial Hurdle
quotes.quote: Hewick was brilliant. He'll go for the National now and this was a lovely set-up for it. Every time I asked him he was there for me and he travelled great. Hopefully he'll go to Aintree with a great chance - Paddy Hanlon, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Racing TV Grande Course de Haies d'Auteuil (Hurdle) (Grade 1) (5yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Hewick jumped well, did everything and a better horse beat us. I know we're better over fences but that shows what I have, he's a great horse - Shark Hanlon, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes King George VI Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Turning out of the back I said we will still be in the first three. It was some ride. I thought the game was up, but Hewick has such a heart. He is a small horse. Probably the race for him in the future is the Grand National, but now when you are here you have to go for a Gold Cup. I said he was getting one run (before the Gold Cup) and he was coming here for that. Cheltenham will suit this horse a lot better as it is a tougher three and a quarter miles there. There was a lot of the other horses that had problems, and we came here fresh and we had a great man on board and that was it - Shark Hanlon, trainer.  Put it this way - if it wasn't the King George I probably would have pulled up! I knew that he stays and stays and I just wasn't able to get going. There are only so many questions you can ask them and if they are not responding you can't ask. Shark said before I got on him he is  is the smallest horse here but he has got the biggest heart and that perfectly sums him up - Gavin Sheehan, speaking to ITV Racing.

quotes.race: bet365 Oaksey Chase (Grade 2) (For The Menorah Challenge Trophy) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I wanted to go for the Bet365, but with the fall Hewick got at Cheltenham I thought it was the right thing to do for the horse to give him a confidence boost. His season's only just starting because he's a summer horse. I just wanted him to get around safe and Rachael's ridden him beautifully, as she always does. I have something planned but I'm not going to say it yet. You'll see it in time, but I have a plan for him in six weeks' time and it won't be in England or Ireland. He'll also go back to America, but we might go somewhere else with him, have horse, will travel - Shark Hanlon, trainer.

quotes.race: Tote Galway Plate (Handicap Chase) (Grade A)
quotes.quote: It's been a dream run with Hewick - this is unreal. We bought him for just 800euros.  Jordan gave him a super ride and knows the horse well. In the closing stages I was nearly afraid to look because the loose horses were doing harm. Everyone told me during the week he wasn't fast enough for this. At Sandown they were going a strong pace from the first furlong, and I knew they wouldn't be going that pace here. I knew he'd have the pace for this race. You need to be ridden prominently here because you stay out of trouble. I knew he'd stay all day. I told Jordan that if he was four lengths behind them at the dip he'd win by five [lengths] - John 'Shark' Hanlon, trainer

quotes.race: Vickers Independent Family Run Bookmaker Durham National Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Hewick stays the trip and was very good. This opens up a lot of doors and he'll probably go on a break now as he's a good ground horse. Next year, there's a lot of Nationals for him and we'll be spending a lot of time over here. He's only a young horse at six and I think he'll keep improving - Shark Hanlon, trainer.

quotes.race: Devon Inn Hotel Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Hewick is very consistent and I was disappointed he didn't get into the Kerry National. I also had him entered in this race so we said we'd come here. He loves the trip, and the ground dried up which is a big help. He loves good ground  - Shark Hanlon, trainer.

quotes.race: Camida Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Hewick is a lovely horse and needs that fast ground. He's a summer horse and maybe we will go for a winners somewhere. He likes that trip and that ground.

stable_tour.quote: He's back in and did his first piece of work last week. There are a few different races we have in our mind for him, one coming up at Thurles, but his main aim is most definitely the Gold Cup. We can't wait to have another crack at it. We ran him here, there and everywhere last season, and he picked up a huge amount of prize-money, but we will be more selective this season. Jordan [Gainford] thought he was about to get his second wind in the Gold Cup when he came down. We're looking forward to getting back there again. 27-11-23

runners.comment: Return to form is needed but he was third and first in the last two runnings of this race
runners.spotlight: Well beaten at Punchestown last May and at Navan in February on sole start since; however, this race has brought out the best in him in the last two seasons, as he finished third in 2024 (good to soft) and first last year (good); could bounce back and play another leading role.

quotes.race: Ivy Liverpool Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Hiddenvalley Lake is a lovely horse. It's worked out really well for us. He really stuck at it. I always thought he wanted softer ground and I was a bit nervous about the ground, but you could say he's improved for it - Henry De Bromhead, trainer.I must say that Henry had a big deal to do with this. There was no pace looking at the race and we were toying with the idea of making the running on Hiddenvalley Lake. Henry came back in and said ride him the way you normally do. He handled the ground brilliantly and travelled so well. He stays really well - Darragh O'Keefe, jockey.

quotes.race: William Hill Boyne Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Hiddenvalley Lake loves heavy ground and Darragh  (O'Keefe, jockey) said the further he went the better he jumped. When they stepped on the pace he jumped better up the straight. We knew he'd stay well over that trip and that ground probably suited him. It's great to get that and we'll see where we go next. He stays three miles and we'll have a look at all the big festivals coming up and see what the options are. He's a fresh horse, he's only had two runs and that's his first completed run this season - Robbie Power, trainer's assistant.

quotes.race: Singletons Supervalu Stayers Novice Hurdle (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: I thought Hiddenvalley Lake was struggling turning in and then he picked up really well - I'd say he quickened after the second-last. He could run at Clonmel in February, in the race which Monalee won for us, and Minella Indo finished second to Allaho - Henry De Bromhead, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Hiddenvalley Lake is a lovely horse and had been working well. He was green and he stays well; he is a horse we will keep finding out about - Henry de Bromhead, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: It was a brilliant run at Aintree last season when he won the Grade 1 Liverpool Hurdle, and he's tipping away now. He's being aimed at the Long Walk at Ascot or the Christmas Hurdle at Leopardstown. We'll sort of flip-flop him and Bob Olinger as to which one goes where. 11-11-25

He's a lovely young horse who made a flying start to his hurdling career with wins at Naas and Cork before Christmas. His latest start in the Grade 3 Mercedes-Benz Novice Hurdle was another fine effort when he was collared late on by stablemate Monty's Star on ground that was softer than ideal for him. I was very happy with that effort and the plan is to go for the Albert Bartlett Novices' Hurdle. 01-03-23

runners.comment: 33-1 winner of Stayers' Hurdle; unproven here but the one to beat on that Cheltenham form
runners.spotlight: 11yo who was running in the Stayers' Hurdle for the fifth time when making the breakthrough in that Cheltenham Grade 1 last month (3m, good); pulled up in this race on both visits to Aintree and 33-1 when winning at the Festival, but it was certainly no fluke judged on the pick of his career exploits and he's the one to beat if repeating that latest form.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Stayers' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were just hoping for a good run. It was a fantastic ride by JJ and I'm so delighted for Sean O'Driscoll and his family as they bred Home By The Lee and he's an 11-year-old and they've been with him all the way. He's as tough as nails. It was a huge team effort by everyone at home. We've raced him a bit more often than we usually do. We thought we'd get him running but we normally keep him very fresh. He's all stamina and JJ[Slevin] gave him a fantastic ride. He made all the right moves at every stage. Of all the horses I've ever trained he's the winning-most in number of wins. We've had him since maybe he just turned four, so he's been there a long time. He trains every day with enthusiasm and when he's off he gets bored. He loves his work, loves his job, loves his racing and has never had a lame step in his life. He's a superstar - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.Home By The Lee has been a great horse and he's tough as nails. Down to the last he started looking around a bit and I thought we were in a bit of bother but he put down his head and away he went again. He keeps loads in reserve for himself and I'd say he'd stay any trip - JJ Slevin, jockey. We came here with confidence, but the odds were stacked against us in that Home By The Lee is 11 years of age, it was his fifth attempt at the race, I don't think any horse has won it after running in it five times - the moral of the story is that there's always a first time! He has the heart of a lion. He's a very sound horse. He lost his way chasing. Joseph rang me one day and said, 'I think maybe you should send him to another yard, they can freshen him up'. I said, 'Are you politely telling me that I should take him away from the yard?' To which he replied, 'No, I'm not'. So I said, 'Well, he's not going anywhere'. Joseph is an amazing trainer -  Sean O'Driscoll, owner-breeder.

quotes.race: John Mulhern Galmoy Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Home By The Lee has bundles of stamina and a great will to win. They were the two things he was going to need today to win in these tough conditions. He got a lovely ride from JJ. He's been a high-level staying hurdler for a number of seasons and I think on the figures he's run right up to his best today. I think he'll go back to Cheltenham again. It'll be the fifth time he goes over there and he got brought down when he had his best shot, but you never know - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Savills Hurdle (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: I'd say that was close to a career-best from him. He's been around for a number of years now and will go back to Cheltenham for the Stayers' with an each-way chance - Joseph O'Brien, trainer of Home By The Lee

quotes.race: Railway Bar Lismullen Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Home By The Lee was a bit better off at the weights this year. He went through the race well and jumped well, Danny was impressed with him. He'll go to Leopardstown now and then to Cheltenham, his programme really plots itself - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Stayers' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: JJ [Slevin] gave Home By The Lee a lovely ride and he galloped on well to the line. I was very proud of his performance. We won't make any plans yet as to what we will do next, but I'm delighted with the performance - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Jack de Bromhead Christmas Hurdle (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: I'd say Home By The Lee will probably go straight to Cheltenham now for the Stayers. He likes getting into a nice rhythm and wasn't beaten a million miles in it last year. He looks a better horse this year - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Railway Bar Lismullen Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Home By The Lee was a bit wild when he was younger, he went chasing and he didn't take to it. But he's a very decent horse on his day. Staying will be his job. He is lazy but this track suited him and I told JJ if he was on their tails turning in he wouldn't be far away - Brendan Powell, assistant trainer

quotes.race: Paddy Power "From The Horse's Mouth" Podcast Novice Handicap Chase (Grade B)
quotes.quote: Home By The Lee is a horse that can be very excitable, but JJ managed to get him switched off today and did a lovely job. He jumps and stays and who knows what he'll be in time - Brendan Powell, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Paddy Power From The Horses Mouth Podcast EBF Novice Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: He's a hardy horse. It was a big ask having had just one run over fences to step in to Grade 3 company He jumped fairly well but got under one or two. He stays very well and is a lovely horse going forward - JJ Slevin, rider of Home By The Lee

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: It was a good, tough performance and he's done quite well for his first day over fences. He's a young, hardy horse. I felt he'd went to sleep on me jumping the third last and thought we were in trouble, but once I got stuck into him he took off. He galloped out to the line well. He could be a nice stayer going forward - JJ Slevin, rider of Home By The Lee

quotes.race: Happy New Year From All At Fairyhouse Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: He's done nothing wrong all the way along and ran a lovely race last time at Naas, which he's come forward from. JJ [Slevin] said he jumped the third last very well and got to the front sooner than he wanted and was waiting a little bit then. At the back of the last he caught a hold of him and he galloped out to the line well. A confined novice could be an option for him, or some kind of Graded race, but we'll take baby steps with him. He's a staying horse for the future and has only just turned five - Joseph O'Brien, trainer of Home By The Lee

stable_tour.quote: It was a good performance in the Galmoy at Gowran and, at this stage of his career, stamina is his forte. He was giving weight away to a good horse in Staffordshire Knot, who has franked the form since, so it's fair to say he was at least as good as he's been in the past when winning Grade 1s. He hasn't had a real slog at Cheltenham to be seen to best effect. He'll go to the Stayers' with a top four or five chance again. He unseated his rider last season and that was probably his best chance to win it, but it's a horse race and anything can happen. 19-02-26

He knocked on the door a couple of times last season but this term he has really got his act together winning back-to-back races at Navan and Leopardstown. I had him in grand order for the Stayers' Hurdle last month, but he made a very bad mistake on the first circuit which put paid to his chances, and the fact he was still less than four lengths behind the winner is a testament to his battling qualities. He goes for the 3m hurdle on Saturday at Aintree and I'm very happy with how he is right now. 12-04-23

runners.breeder: H Fowler, A Frost & C Longsdon
runners.comment: Grade 1 novice win here 12 months ago; remains lightly raced and could have more to offer
runners.spotlight: Won the Grade 1 Mersey Novices' Hurdle here 12 months ago (2m4f, good); just two runs in current campaign and they've been positive performances in Grade 1s, finishing third in the Long Walk at Ascot (3m, good to soft) and fifth in the Stayers' Hurdle at Cheltenham (3m, good); this lightly raced 6yo could have more to offer back here in a first-time tongue-tie; chance.

quotes.race: Turners Mersey Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Honesty Policy is very well named - he's as honest as the day is long. It's only his fourth run over hurdles and he's still inexperienced, and, in fairness to him, when he got going after the third-last he never raised his head off the ground and galloped all the way to the line. I was hopeful going to the last - he jumped and picked up well, but he wasn't going as quickly after the last as I'd have liked, but I knew he had enough left in the tank. He'll have no problem going over fences last year - Mark Walsh, rider.

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction Novice Hurdle (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: I suppose we were all sweating coming down the home straight because Honesty Policy was stuck in a bit of a pocket for a while, but he got himself out of trouble and has actually won snug enough at the winning post. The softer the ground the better for him. It's lovely to get that win on the board and I'm sure Gordon will be aiming for the Final at the Punchestown Festival - Lisa O'Neill, stable representative of Gordon Elliot.

quotes.race: Navan Ford & Opel Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Honesty Policy is a nice horse. The further he goes the better. He's going in the right direction and he should make a nice chaser - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I'd say he'll go straight to the Stayers' Hurdle now. I was keen to run him in the Boyne Hurdle, but the ground was too heavy and he's not the biggest horse in the world. We'll get a racecourse gallop into him somewhere. He was a very good novice last season and we went over to Ascot for the Long Walk before Christmas to find out where we stood with him. Needless to say, we were thrilled with the way he ran. He stays well and has a touch of class to go along with it.  09-02-26

runners.comment: Pulled up in Stayers' Hurdle but in the picture on his winning form in the Long Walk
runners.spotlight: Relished step up in trip when winning C&D handicap (good to soft) in November and won the Grade 2 Long Distance Hurdle at Newbury (3m, soft) and Grade 1 Long Walk at Ascot (3m, good to soft) on his next two starts, with Strong Leader in second on both occasions; below par at Cheltenham on last two runs (good record there previously) and it was disconcerting that he was pulled up in the Stayers', but he's in the picture if back to his best.

quotes.race: Howden Long Walk Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Impose Toi has loved this step up to three miles and it's made a big difference. You can ride him like that, with a bit of confidence. He doesn't do much in front, so the timing has to be perfect, and it was. He's the most honest person, and if you saw him at home you wouldn't give me a sixpence for him. But everyone loves him and he's progressing all along, so hopefully we can keep it going. He'd probably want one more run before Cheltenham. He can afford to have some time off in January, but he does so little at home that you can't afford to give him too much holiday - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Long Distance Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a funny race as it looked as though they were crawling round. We knew Impose Toi would get three miles but I'd have thought a stronger test over that trip would suit him. He didn't jump quite as well as he can do but he's a tough little devil. That's taken him from handicaps into Graded races, but where do we go next? The Long Walk comes quite quickly but last season he went Cheltenham, Aintree and Punchestown, so he can do quick turnarounds. We'll just have to see. You've got to think about the Stayers' Hurdle. It's an open division, one that chops and changes throughout every season. There are some good horses and Strong Leader is probably the best of the British team, so he's a good yardstick. After that, you'd say we're towards the top of the home defenders - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Pertemps Network Handicap Hurdle (Pertemps Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's hard to tell how good Impose Toi is because he doesn't do anything at home. He's nearly as slow as we have in the whole place and then he can come and do that. It's surprising he's even got himself fit because he just does so little. It was a great performance under top weight and we'll have to see what the handicapper says, but it was a bit of a messy race with some of the hurdles out. I'd be surprised if he's a Graded horse but we'll have to see - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Cup Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The lack of a recent run wasn't an issue. Impose Toi is a funny character as he does absolutely nothing at home at all. Suddenly out there three quarters of the way through the race he carted Nico [de Boinville] into the race and if anything he got there too soon. It didn't matter that happened as the other horse was always going to win. I would have thought that is his trip. We didn't think he would get this at first, but he wouldn't want to go over three miles - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral 'Daily Rewards Shaker' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We ran Impose Toi in the Lanzarote last season and didn't think he stayed but I actually think he wants to go up to three miles now. He keeps popping up and will stay over hurdles. I did school him over fences and he wasn't the best - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Valda Energy Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a tidy race to aim at and start the season but Impose Toi will need to play with the grown-ups now. He's got the experience and everything was in his favour. He's a very likable character and a straightforward horse. He'll jump a fence and will be a nice horse for the future. He's progressing - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's been in very good order and has done nothing wrong. He was brilliant when winning the Long Walk Hurdle at Ascot. He got beaten at Cheltenham the other day, but Nico said to put a line through that run because it was tough ground and we were giving 6lb away to the winner [Ma Shantou]. He loves to get on some decent ground. His progression has been great, and even last season over two and a half miles, he ran fantastic races at Cheltenham, Aintree and Punchestown. He was knocking on the door, but he's another year older, and pushing him up to three miles has been key.  18-02-26

runners.breeder: Mrs J Rainer, Mr F Jereczek & Mr Rainer
runners.comment: Convincing winner of the BetMGM Cup and this unexposed 7yo could have a part to play
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in Grade 2 Relkeel Hurdle at Cheltenham in January (2m4f, good; no match for Kabral Du Mathan) when his jumping lacked fluency, then convincing winner of the BetMGM Cup (Handicap) at Cheltenham (2m5f, good to soft) last month; he should be fine now back up in trip, having won a 3m Grade 2 novice chase last season, and this unexposed 7yo could have a part to play.

quotes.race: BetMGM Cup Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought James [Bowen] was interesting - it wasn't exactly the plan to make the running, but he did it exceptionally well, didn't he? It was great. Jingko Blue is not the easiest horse to keep on the right side of - when he's good, he's very talented, but he's not the easiest. His jumping has never been? We tried him over fences and he won over fences, but? This was the obvious race to come for. He's not a slow horse, but he got an easy lead there - normally the pace is flat out. Great pace-making by James! At least the owner [Tony Barney] has got a day to calm down before Jango Baie in the Gold Cup - he might need it ! - Nicky Henderson, trainer. Plan A went completely out of the window, then B and C! I never intended to make the running but I winged the first and the next thing I was there, doing nothing. It felt good when I winged the last because he doesn't always come for you, but he did today. He got in a great rhythm and I was able to take him back the whole way, then when we got between four out and three out I was able to roll on into it. I jumped that one well and from the top of the hill to turning in it just worked out well. It's quick ground and I feel like we went slower today than yesterday when I won the National Hunt Chase. It was always going to suit the ones on the front end and I'm just glad it was me - James Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: Hampton Novices' Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were hoping Jingko Blue would stay three miles so I think he'll continue down that road. This was never the plan but then they put this race on and it's a great effort. We weren't really prepared for this because we were waiting for the Reynoldstown. I think there's every chance he'll still go there and then onto Cheltenham. I was chatting with Nico [de Boinville, jockey] and he's very happy that we do that. I think he's going the right way and he's a talented horse - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: 2025 Uttoxeter Annual Membership Now Available Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jingko Blue was great. He jumped really slickly; he's not very big but he certainly respects those fences a lot more than he did hurdles. He's gone through that ground easy enough. I thought it was the perfect start - Nicky Henderson, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That caught me unaware. I thought it was quite a big test off top weight in a competitive race. I've had the odd issue with Jingko Blue at home and not been unable to run him but that was a good performance. You'd love to mind him a bit this season. He's a nice big horse who will jump a fence - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Committed To Safer Gambling Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I think Jingko Blue did well to get back up. It deserved to be a dead-heat and I think the first two are both smart horses. It's a juggling game at the moment with the novices because they are a good bunch and spreading them out is important. I think he is good but he's only young and let's go one step at a time. He's growing up all the time - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won at Uttoxeter and then in a Grade 2 Windsor last season. We were thinking about the Brown Advisory at the festival, so we went to the Reynoldstown at Ascot, but his jumping got a bit muddled. He made a shocking mistake going down the hill and that was lights out for the season. It transpired that he had significant kissing spines and he's had back surgery, which we're hoping can make a difference. He's grown into a fine, big horse, and he's physically improved. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Wind surgery since last time and he has an excellent record at Aintree; key player
runners.spotlight: Tailed off at Cheltenham in January but that's not his track and he's had a wind op since; prior to that he ran well when runner-up to Impose Toi at Newbury and Ascot, and his Aintree form figures read 1212 with his last two visits being in this race (good to soft/good); there can be considerable optimism that he'll be a key player back here; tongue-tie added.

quotes.race: Coral Long Distance Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'd like to take the winner on off level weights, but Strong Leader has run well. He was a lot sharper in cheekpieces and jumped well on the whole. I'm disappointed he's been beaten but it was still a very good run. It's frustrating as we have to go left-handed, but he doesn't like Cheltenham. I need to have a chat with the owners about potentially going to Ireland. Otherwise, the only race I can see is the Rendlesham at Haydock, but it could be very soft there. I can't see us going back for the Long Walk - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Hurdle (Grade 2) (Registered As The West Yorkshire Hurdle) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: There were three brilliant jockeys and that was British jump racing from the back of the last today, a brilliant race, and I'm pleased we came out on top. That was a proper horse race. A truer-run race would suit Strong Leader well and I hope there are more good races in him still - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: Ivy Liverpool Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Strong Leader ran very well. He jumped well on the whole, just probably missed a couple of hurdles at a crucial time. He's backed up his run from last year. He's just a horse who needs to be kept to a flat track now and I think we'll campaign him a bit differently next year. There's another one of these in him. I think he likes nice ground - he's run very well - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Long Distance Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was Strong Leader's first start of the season and I had him as fit as I could get him. We're obviously mindful of the rest of the season, so I left a bit to work with. He's not a flashy horse, he doesn't do anything over-exuberantly, but overall he jumped well. He improved throughout the whole of last season and I'd like to think he'll do the same this term. He's as good a staying three-mile hurdler as we've got on this side of the water by the looks of things, and hopefully he can keep progressing. We'll head for the Long Walk and then potentially look at the Cleeve Hurdle and see if we go for a Stayers' or wait for Aintree. Sometimes in life you've got to have a go. If we go for a Stayers' he'll have to run in a Cleeve and go very close to winning - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: JRL Group Liverpool Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: This is my best day as a trainer. This lad is a home bred and they're just ten minutes down the road from me. I'm adamant Strong Leader doesn't like Cheltenham, he doesn't go up and down hills well enough. I was ballsy enough to leave it alone and save him for this day. He got into a rhythm and jumped and travelled well. He's a very good horse on his day - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: Boylesports Best Odds Guaranteed Novices' Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Series Qual') (GBB)
quotes.quote: It was a smart performance under a penalty. Jumping hasn't come naturally at all and Strong Leader was a lot more professional (than on hurdling debut) and jumped well on the whole, with probably still plenty to brush up on. He's a horse we've always liked. He definitely wouldn't want very heavy ground - Olly Murphy, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He looks fantastic. The plan is that he'll go to Wetherby for Charlie Hall weekend, where he'll run in the West Yorkshire Hurdle. A flat, left-handed track suits him well and we're looking forward to getting him started. He's got no Grade 1 penalty this season either, which is a big help. He picks his own way, but we might consider Leopardstown over Christmas - something a bit different - as he would like that track. It's worth looking at. 23-10-25

We were disappointed with his run in the Welsh Champion Hurdle but he'll step up in trip now. He has a big staying pedigree and has never worked like a two-miler - he has shocked me every time he has gone to the races, including when finishing runner-up in a Grade 1 last season. We'll put a line through Ffos Las as he has come out of the race fine and I still have plenty of faith in him. 01-11-23

runners.comment: Powered up the hill to win the Martin Pipe at Cheltenham; this new trip might suit
runners.spotlight: Won the mares' novice hurdle at last season's Cheltenham Festival (2m1f, good to soft) and returned to form to win the Martin Pipe Handicap there (2m4f, soft) last month; she has something to find now back up in grade, even with the 7lb mares' allowance, but she powered up the hill last time and has an Irish National winner in her pedigree, so the step up in trip might prompt further improvement; not discounted.

quotes.race: Martin Pipe Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I got a flyer of a start; I was a bit closer than I wanted to be, to be honest, I had planned on sitting just in front of mid-division, but when I was up in the van there I thought it was a valuable spot to give up, and I was travelling so easily and jumping well where I was. I got a bit tapped for toe coming down the hill, but we were confident Air Of Entitlement would stay well. Robbie Power, who has been a huge help to me, told me not to panic and to wait to cross until I crossed the road to go for it, and that's what I did. She just idled a bit in front - she was straight as a die when she had a bit of company. She headed the second horse and was just looking for a rail to run, but she was a good winner - Paddy O'Brien, jockey.

quotes.race: Ryanair Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (Registered As The Dawn Run Mares' Novices' Hurdle) (GBB)
quotes.quote: We knew Air Of Entitlement had the stamina and the New Course suits horses with that. We always worry about being too handy in that race, but Rachael was spot on. I thought they went a real good gallop and she gave her some spin. It was a little bit like Telmesomethinggirl a few years ago.  We weren't as far back as we normally are, but she stayed on really well. I thought when we winged the last we had a chance. I knew Keith (Donoghue on Sixandahalf) had been up there the whole way and historically that hasn't worked as we have had a couple that did that. I always say I prefer coming here fresh and happy rather than feeling that I have to justify myself coming here - Henry De Bromhead, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She stayed on really well to win the Mares' Novices' Hurdle at the Cheltenham Festival last season. It was a little disappointing at Fairyhouse, where she finished second in a conditions hurdle, but she ran okay for her first run back. We'll look for something similar and hopefully she can progress and find her form. 11-11-25

runners.comment: Runner-up in the Pertemps Final but today's assignment requires a clear career best
runners.spotlight: Course winner who keeps on improving and was a fine second of 24 in the Pertemps Final (Handicap) at Cheltenham (3m, good) last month; receives 7lb mares' allowance but today's assignment requires a clear career best.

quotes.race: Pertemps Network Final Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: She's runs a blinder. She's unrideable and made Brian's life very difficult out there. We couldn't bury Lavida Adiva down the rail and we were probably right not to. You have to give her some kind of room but she's not easy. She's not even very big, bless her, but she's tough. She's like a terrier. We are stood here [in second] wondering why we are not over there [the winner's spot] but we are still thrilled. Why wouldn't we be? We are second in a big-field handicap with a cracking filly - Ruth Jefferson, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes 'Big-Value You Can Bet On' Mares' Hurdle (Listed Race) (Registered As The Beeswing) (GBB)
quotes.quote: We thought Lavida Adiva would like the longer trip and we thought if she stayed and could cope at this level we could look at a similar race at Ayr.  She never travelled or jumped on the ground last time, it was too tacky for her, and Charlie Maggs didn't give her a hard race, which I loved. As soon as I rode her on the Monday I thought 'you're coming here' - Ruth Jefferson, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Proper Prices Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Mares' Hurdle Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I think that qualifies Lavida Adiva for the Cheltenham race [in April] she finished second in last season. We dropped her in class as we just wanted to get her head back in front. She's not very big and it's quite hard for these horses to carry top weight - Ruth Jefferson, trainer

stable_tour.quote: My little diva and my little pocket rocket. She's a law unto herself at home, she just does her own thing and we tolerate her moods, bless her. In the first two races last season things just didn't go right for her. I made too much use of her at Aintree and she was keen, and then she ran at Haydock on bottomless ground and just didn't like it. Then she went to Aintree on Boxing Day and won and things picked up in the second half of the season, with her Listed win at Kelso in March. She's a hard horse to figure out. You just have to get to where you think she's ready to run and then run her. Whether she takes a run or two, I don't know. The first season I ran her over 2m5f at Kelso and she ended up dropping back in trip and winning over 2m, before working her way back up in trip, so we were just making it up as we went along. Last season we weren't sure how she'd get on as a first-season handicapper but she got there in the end. She was third on her reappearance at Ayr this month. I was pleased with that as it was her best run first time out for us, in her third season. We'll be looking at some of those mares' hurdles and she'll probably go to Doncaster next for a Listed race in December. Most of her winning has been done on sharp tracks, so ideally we'd be looking to go back to Kelso at the end of the season. 19-11-25

runners.comment: Good form in defeat in 3m Grade 2s in November; each-way claims if back on song
runners.spotlight: Not at the top of her game in the Mares' Hurdle at Cheltenham (2m4f, good) last month but this sort of trip may be her optimum; neck second to Strong Leader at Wetherby (3m, good) in November and creditable third behind Impose Toi and Strong Leader in another Grade 2 at Newbury (3m, soft) later that month; ran well here 12 months ago; each-way claims if back on song.

quotes.race: BetMGM Mares' Hurdle (Grade 2) (Registered As The Warfield Mares' Hurdle) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought I was flat out at the home turn but Dan and Harry [Skelton] said Take No Chances would stay really well and to keep after her. I saw Paul Townend's head come upsides me and I thought I might just be in trouble. I suppose he didn't have race fitness on his side and we did - Kielan Woods, jockey.

quotes.race: bet365 Mares' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We dropped back in trip like we did with Molly Ollys Wishes and she's a similar type of horse. Take No Chances has a fabulous attitude and jumps very slickly. I'm going to be adventurous and put her in the Fighting Fifth, just in case Constitution Hill frightens everybody off. There's a few quid on offer and she'll be getting weight. We won't be beating Constitution Hill but we might turn up for a few pennies on offer. She's improving and when mares get confidence they do even more for you - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Download The Rhino.Bet App Mares' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Take No Chances had some really good bumper form without winning, but we have always liked her a lot. We were relatively confident coming here. I'm sure Dan has got something in mind for her. I should think if she goes in again in another race like this then she would be stepped up in class. I do think she is up there with our better mares - Bridget Andrews, stable spokeswoman.

stable_tour.quote: She was third behind Lossiemouth last year, is super-consistent, and we've run her a little less this season to get her there as fresh as possible and give her the best chance. She's certainly no less a horse this year and I'd give her an each-way squeak at least because she'll run her race and be bang there. 17-02-26

racecards.verdict: Honesty Policy is feared but STRONG LEADER has an excellent record at Aintree, including in this race, and he's the selection.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Honesty Policy, 4/1 Strong Leader, 11/2 Jingko Blue, 6/1 Hiddenvalley Lake, 13/2 Impose Toi, 7/1 Home By The Lee, 11/1 Air Of Entitlement, 22/1 Hewick, 25/1 Take No Chances, 28/1 Doddiethegreat, 50/1 Lavida Adiva

racecards.race_name: Randox Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: 1st and 2nd in last two Grand Nationals; penultimate race suggests all his ability remains
runners.spotlight: His only three long-distance events resulted in an Irish National win in 2023, a storming success in this race in 2024 (soft) and a valiant second, from further off the pace, in repeat bid here in 2025 (good to soft); what a record that is, and 50-1 second in a 3m Grade 1 at Leopardstown on penultimate start gives every encouragement that all his ability remains; the return of cheekpieces (tried once in 2022) is interesting but, off 1lb higher than last year, he should be set for another prominent finish.

quotes.race: Randox Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I Am Maximus ran a huge race. He probably took me through the race a bit better last year but he's run with credit again and it's a big result for the team. A bit sickening to get beat though - Paul Townend, rider.

quotes.race: Randox Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I could see all the time that Paul was happy with where he was, just looking for room, looking for daylight, and he eventually got it and set I Am Maximus alight. He made little of his mark, and that means he's going to be a Gold Cup horse. We don't know how good this horse is. Today he showed us that he's better than he has been, anyway. I think he was still just a little bit ahead of the handicapper after what he did in the Bobbyjo Chase and he proved it today.
