He's quirky, he's immature, but he's learning all the time - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Tote.ie Bobbyjo Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: I don't know how good I Am Maximus is, but he's certainly improving with every run. I'd imagine he goes for the Grand National, he would look like a Gold Cup horse in time but I'd imagine Aintree is his objective - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Bar One Racing Drinmore Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: That was a nice bonus on his last day as a novice. I Am Maximus won his maiden in nice circumstances and then to do that on his last day as a novice was good too! He is a total character but he looks a class horse now and not just a handicapper so we might have some different plans for him. We were hoping he might have a chance but it was more in hope, and the fact it was his last run as a novice made us give him his chance. He's clearly improved and showed he has that bit of class when he needs it. We were thinking of the Grand National but maybe we'll stick to Grade 1 races with him, we'll see - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: BoyleSports Irish Grand National Chase (Extended Handicap Chase) (Grade A)
quotes.quote: I must complement Paul for the ride he gave I Am Maximus because if he were listening to me I'd have said pull him up after going a mile. He dug in and stayed very well. It's really special - JP McManus, owner.

quotes.race: Prodec Networks Maiden Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I Am Maximus will be a lovely horse and I wouldn't be surprised if we went two and a half miles at some stage. He's quickened up again at the end, but is a strong galloper who learned a lot at Exeter last time - he'd had just one run in his life before then. He was a different horse today and his jumping was deadly. He looks like he's got a very powerful gallop in him. He'll be a fantastic chaser next season and he's a Graded horse; there's no doubt about that - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Royal Gloucestershire Hussars Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I Am Maximus is lovely and will be very good, but we'll have to discuss plans re another bumper or hurdling - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: You don't need me to tell you where we will be aiming him - all roads will lead back to Aintree for the Grand National. He has run two fabulous races in it and we'll stick to the same sort of plan as last season. 17-11-25

He came to us in the autumn and, although he has yet to get his head in front, he has run well in top company, notably last time behind Mighty Potter. There are several options in the Ultima, Brown Advisory, Turners and Plate. 08-03-23

runners.comment: Won this in 2025 in basically smooth style; up 4lb; this year's preparation is a big worry
runners.spotlight: Final leg of last season's hat-trick was delivered in basically smooth style here in the National, asserting in the final 1f from I Am Maximus and Grangeclare West (good to soft); 4lb higher today but it's far more concerning that his season has hardly got going, with reappearance delayed until last month when he was seriously ring-rusty behind Gerri Colombe; last year's and this year's build-ups could hardly be more contrasting and he's been deserted by Patrick Mullins.

quotes.race: Randox Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We got too good a start and we were too handy. Nick Rockett was jumping brilliant but I was taking him back everywhere. At the Canal Turn second time I was wondering if I'd dropped back too far but then once I've asked him to make up ground he got there easily and I was going to get there too soon. I'd that in mind when we got to the last so I was bopping around until we got to the Elbow and then I said to myself I'm going to go, I'm going to enjoy this - Patrick Mullins, rider.

quotes.race: Follow @ToteRacing On Twitter Bobbyjo Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: I thought it was a nice performance, beating an Irish National winner in the process, and it was a nice trial for Aintree. I'm very pleased with Nick Rockett. It was tough coming back from the Thyestes only four-and-a-bit weeks before this. That was tough and this should leave him spot on for Aintree. He'll probably take a little while to recover from that but he has the time. I was very impressed with how slick he jumped ? his jumping was excellent. We aimed him for the Irish National last year but it didn't work. He's a horse I think has the potential to run well around Aintree. Bobbyjo winners have been lucky around there - Willie Mullions, trainer.

quotes.race: Goffs Thyestes Handicap Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: We'll probably look forward to a National and we'll have a look at the Bobbyjo. That might be too soon but we'll see how Nick Rockett comes out of this - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: McInerney Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Nick Rockett was good. He improve a little bit from his first run, he obviously jumped very well. The first day was a competitive race and the form has been franked - David Casey, assistant trainer

stable_tour.quote: He's now rated 6lb higher than when he won the Grand National last season, so we might try to mind that mark by running him over hurdles on a few occasions. There is also the option of training him for a Gold Cup but he seemed to relish the demands of Aintree, so it would be hard not to head back there for another crack. It would be brilliant to head back to the National with a horse who had a live chance of going back-to-back. He seems to be in particularly good shape. 17-11-25

runners.comment: So nearly won his second King George at Kempton, which doesn't mean this test will suit
runners.spotlight: So nearly won his second King George at Kempton over Christmas but, although he's a class act, excelling over 3m on good ground at that speed track doesn't mean that this test will suit him; his moderate late headway in the extended 2m4f Grade 1 Ryanair at Cheltenham last month isn't that persuasive either.

quotes.race: Ryanair Chase (Registered As The Festival Trophy) (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Banbridge ran a great race but is probably a bit in between trips. He doesn't quite get three miles and two up the hill but he was flat out here over two and a half but stayed on well - Sean Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes King George VI Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a fantastic run and I'm very proud of Banbridge. It is obviously frustrating to get nabbed, but he has turned up and run his race. I'm delighted for Ronnie [Bartlett] and his family, and for Ben and Harry with the winner. Everything happened perfectly for us. He jumped great and travelled great. He got a great jump at the last and was just beaten in a head bob. This was an obvious target for him and today was the day we were building towards and I'm very happy with how he turned up and Sean [Bowen] gave him a great ride. I don't think we will work back from a Gold Cup. I will talk to Ronnie and see. We gave that a crack last season. Aintree and Kempton Park are tracks he has been good at in the past so it might make more sense to go back there (Aintree) - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Boodles Cheltenham Gold Cup Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Banbridge didn't jump well enough - J J Slevin, jockey.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes King George VI Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a special win. Banbridge has been a special horse for a number of years and is such a dream. Speed is emphasised here more than some places and I think that panned out well for him, but I did think Il Est Francais had gone and won. We'll enjoy today and will discuss plans later. After Punchestown last year Ronnie [Bartlett, owner] called me and said let's have a go at the King George and that paid off. We really felt he was ready to run his legs off - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Champion Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: I thought JJ [Slevin, jockey] gave Banbridge a fantastic ride and the tempo of the race wasn't quite what we thought it'd be. He saved a bit and the horse found a lot and I'm delighted for Ronnie [Bartlett, owner] as he's been very patient with this horse, particularly when the ground hasn't been right for him. We weren't sure if we'd go three miles or two, but it became obvious when El Fabiolo went to Sandown. He's pretty versatile, and Ronnie's even mentioned the King George as an early season target next year but he'll be kept on as good ground as we can find for him. He's remarkably consistent when he has his conditions - Joseph O'Brien, trainer, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: Coral Silviniaco Conti Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We've been looking for good ground and we got it today. Banbridge looked a bit rusty at times and made a few mistakes but he's been off the track for a long time, so it's pretty exciting. He's more mature and he was very cool about travelling over here. We've had him bubbling for a while and there have been races that we've been going for and the ground wasn't the way we wanted, but hopefully there's a bit of improvement to come. If the ground is nice he'll go for the Ryanair; it would be nice to take Michael O'Leary's money! - Ronnie Bartlett, owner.

quotes.race: Racehorse Lotto Manifesto Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Banbridge ran in the Drinmore earlier in the season and after that race we knew he's a better horse on better ground so there's no point wasting runs on soft ground. I think we probably saw the result of minding him earlier in the spring here today. I declared him on Saturday just in case, when I saw there was rain coming yesterday I wanted to be sure before I walked the track this morning but he won't run again. We'll look at Punchestown and see how he comes out of this. You'd have to say looking at him today that he could stay further in time. But he's certainly not slow - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: From The Horses Mouth Podcast Arkle Challenge Trophy Trial Novices' Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Banbridge has taken to chasing very well. He's already gone a step ahead of his hurdles campaign and there's a long way to go until the next step but you couldn't be more impressed with what he's done there. He's a hugely exciting horse going forwards. I think we learned today that two miles is another option going forwards, his jumping was what you wanted to see from a two-miler - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Join Gowran Park Racing Club Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Banbridge jumped very well. We had schooled him a bit at home and he has been very good. You'd be hoping he might achieve something similar to what he achieved over hurdles - J.J. Slevin, rider.

quotes.race: Martin Pipe Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The standing start actually suited us. Banbridge was very sharp away, thank God, and I got a lovely position early. They didn't go very quick and he was always in his comfort zone. I wasn't confident that I would win until about ten strides after the last. I was always just conscious that something might get to me, but luckily nothing did - Mark McDonagh, rider.

quotes.race: Dunmoe Rated Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: It was a nice performance for a horse that really wants further. Banbridge will be a three-miler in time. I just thought that they might do him for a bit of toe but he's very tough and he jumped well up the straight. He wouldn't want it any softer than that. Next year he could be an exciting chaser, especially at 2m4f or further. He'll stay 3m. He stays, he's honest and he gallops - Brendan Powell, assistant trainer.

stable_tour.quote: The one thing about him is he needs top of the ground to be at his best at this stage of his career. We'll have a discussion with Ronnie [Bartlett, owner] closer to the time to see if he goes to Cheltenham or waits for Aintree. The ground will be the deciding factor. 19-02-26

A very smart novice chaser who won twice earlier this season, including the Arkle trial at Cheltenham's November meeting. His last run was a fair effort when second to El Fabiolo who has not done the form any harm since. We missed Cheltenham last month with him as the ground was too soft, but he is in very good order and he is going to Aintree on Thursday for the Manifesto Novices' Chase which is a Grade 1 over 2m4f. He will be up against Stage Star amd Saint Roi so it won't be easy. His work has been very encouraging though. 12-04-23

runners.comment: 3l third last year, after diving at the final fence (up 3lb today); won his latest outing
runners.spotlight: Excellent 3l third in last year's renewal, somehow renewing his effort after diving at the final fence cost him plenty of momentum; creditable fifth at Sandown just three weeks later and surging clear from Gerri Colombe at Fairyhouse this February, after another last-fence dive, showed that he's at least as good as ever; 3lb higher than 12 months ago but lots to like.

quotes.race: BAR 1 Betting Bobbyjo Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Grangeclare West is a classy animal. I was getting that feel off him that he was handling that [heavy] ground and on ratings he was entitled to beat them snugly. I tried not to overthink it and went with him. He left a poor run behind him a couple of starts ago and if I wasn't on this lad and he won, how silly would I look. He's been keeping good company in good races and that'll do him the world of good. He's a brilliant jumper and has been keeping top company - Paul Townend, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Randox Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was some spin. Grangeclare West jumped for fun and ran the race of his life. He did something a bit similar in the Gold Cup in Ireland, but repeated that here today with eleven stone eight on his back. Going out on the second circuit I knew he was going to run a big race. I gave him a breather and then he started winging fences down the back. I thought he was going to do the business but he just got into the bottom of the last and that cost him momentum - cost him second place - Brian Hayes, rider.

quotes.race: Neville Hotels Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: I didn't expect that - I was hoping Grangeclare West would run well but that was a top race. Paul was very worried about him pulling too hard and he had some job there. He'd want to be as fit as he is as he just pulled his arms out for the three miles. To do that in that ground and win like that going away, it was a huge performance. His jumping was excellent. He just came out of Paul's hands at the first fence and from then on he was just trying to settle him back. You can't keep jumping like that over three miles. He got him back jumping normally and then when he needed him over the last few fences, especially at the third-last, he was there. He's just a natural chaser. We were looking at it and asking ourselves is he a Brown Advisory horse? But we nominated Fact To File for that. The winner could go for the Brown Advisory and Fact To File might go to the Turners, but we'll see, it's a nice problem to have. We might come back here for the Dublin Racing Festival first - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Mongey Communications Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Grangeclare West has always promised and I would say chasing might just help him to fulfil his promise now, hopefully we can get a good run with him now. The two fences in the straight being taken out was no help to him. I was using his jumping to fill him up, so if I was going to get beat it was the long run-in which was going to do it but his class got him through - Paul Townend, jockey.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: I have to say Grangeclare West impressed me, considering he was so keen early on and jumped a bit big during the race. Then he settled and Paul got him together and balanced. Once he got down to gallop he impressed me. The obvious race for him would be the Lawlors of Naas Novice Hurdle (January 8). He surprised me in the manner he did it there. As I said to the owner before racing, we could run well here and finish fourth or fifth. It looked a good race - Willie Mullins, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We were kind of looking at the Grand National for him, but I spoke to the owners during the week and I said we're going to Cheltenham. Now the dust has settled I think we'll wait and see what weight he gets before deciding where to go next. 5-2-25

runners.comment: 2nd in 2024 Cheltenham Gold Cup and, some positive signs lately, could be on his way back
runners.spotlight: Five Grade 1 wins and runner-up in the 2024 Cheltenham Gold Cup; reappearance at Christmas came after 421 days off and this season's form is well short of his best, but second to Grangeclare West at Fairyhouse was a big step back in the right direction and he comfortably obliged at odds-on for latest outing; cheekpieces last three starts; well handicapped on his old form and could be on his way back.

quotes.race: Bluegrass Racehorse Cube Chase
quotes.quote: It was straightforward enough. Gerri Colombe actually enjoyed that better ground as well.  He'll probably go to Aintree next. I'm not sure if it will be the National or the Bowl ? obviously that will be up to Gordon and connections - Jack Kennedy, trainer.

quotes.race: BAR 1 Betting Bobbyjo Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe has run a cracker. He had a long time off so it's great to see him improve with each run. He seemed to enjoy himself out there today so let's see how he comes out of this. Hopefully we can have a think about Aintree for him - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Bowl Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jack (Kennedy, jockey) said he was never happy with Gerri Colombe the whole way, he said he was slack the whole way, but, look, it shows the goods the horse has. He said he probably ended up in front too soon, but he's a great horse. He only does what he has to do. We're lucky to have him. I actually think he'd be a bit better on better ground, but it will be all systems go for the Gold Cup next year. We'll probably go the same route again and keep dreaming - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Boodles Cheltenham Gold Cup Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe ran a great race and we got a lot closer to the winner this time. The loose horse didn't help us but it didn't make the difference between winning and losing. The winner was very, very good - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Savills Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: We've no excuses, everything went even more smoothly for Gerri Colombe than it did at Down Royal. He jumped and travelled great, but the winner just picked up and went away. The winner was unreal. The gallop was strong the whole way and I was happy. The winner just picked up and went away from me - Jack Kennedy, jockey.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Champion Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: We were delighted with Gerri Colombe as we knew there would be improvement in him today, his first run in open company. He only came back in on September 19, so there's loads of improvement. We'll have one run now and then the Gold Cup. He showed that he is in the mix now for the Gold Cup, he stays very well and that's what you need. Jack [Kennedy] said he was a bit rusty early, but I thought he was pretty much foot-perfect, apart from one, for a novice stepping into open company. The sky is the limit - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Air Charter Service Mildmay Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were happy the whole way. Gerri Colombe is a good horse. We were disappointed we got beaten at Cheltenham, I think we were the best horse in the race. That proved it today. He's a horse to look forward to for next year. We'll look to the future now, Cheltenham is over. You have to dream in this game and he looks to have a whole lot of potential - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Brown Advisory Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (Registered As The Broadway Novices' Chase) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe has been beaten a short-head in a Grade 1 and a stride over the line he is a neck in front, so of course I retain faith in him - he's top class. However, whether he has another run this season is something that will have to be discussed with the owners as he has definitely had a race there - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Scilly Isles Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: If Gordon Ellliott decides he doesn't want to go to Cheltenham (this season) I'd have no issue with that. Next season Gerri Colombe could be a Gold Cup horse. I'm sure there will be ante-post punters going bananas because I've told you he might not go to the festival but we're looking at next year and the Gold Cup for this horse if we can keep him sound. The only thing that has been ruled out today is the National Hunt Chase, because we can't qualify - Brian Acheson, owner.

quotes.race: Guinness Faugheen Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe just keeps winning. He doesn't do anything fancy at home and when he got to the front he pulled himself up again. We're lucky to have him. We'll have a look to see where he might run next - I don't know yet. The National Hunt Chase, or something like that, might suit if the ground was soft. He's a lovely horse who wouldn't like the ground very quick. He was a big baby last season and is coming to himself now - Gordon Elliott, trainer

quotes.race: Irish National Hunt Steeplechase Committee Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe was good I thought. He was having a good blow afterwards and Jack thinks he'll come on for the run. He might go to Limerick at Christmas - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: BetVictor W.T. O'Grady Memorial Irish EBF Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe won in spite of the track, we ran him here because of the lack of races. He needs more ease in the ground and I imagine he'll go straight to the Albert Bartlett - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: I.N.H. Stallion Owners EBF Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe is still very green for a horse who has done so much. He still has a lot to learn. He jumped well and he's a beautiful horse to look forward to. There's a nice bit of class there and he stays well. He's a nice horse - Denis O'Regan, rider.

quotes.race: Paddy Power (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: Gerri Colombe is going to be a lovely horse next year for his owners and we're just delighted with that. Next year is the year for him when he goes jumping and anything he does this year is a bonus. He's won two bumpers now and is exciting - Jamie Codd, rider.

quotes.race: Racing Again January 30th (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: I don't think you'll see a whole lot more of Gerri Colombe this season, he might have one more run. He's probably going to be a big chaser more than anything, a big staying horse down the road - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's back cantering away but you won't see him this side of Christmas. It's all going to be baby steps with him and we definitely won't be rushing him. He has no Grade 1 penalty anymore, so that opens up a few easier options for him. Something like the race at Tramore on New Year's Day could be an option. We'll decide closer to the time. Whether he's still a Gold Cup horse or we need to be looking at the Grand National for him, only time will tell. He's been an incredible horse over the years and owes us nothing. 26-10-25

runners.breeder: Dr V Simon, Mrs V Simon & Mr N Simon
runners.comment: Irish and Welsh National winner; Gold Cup was disappointing but he's bounced back before
runners.spotlight: In the last 13 months he's won Cheltenham's NH Chase (3m6f), the Irish National (3m5f), a hurdle race, Welsh National (near 3m7f; 12lb higher today) and a Newbury Grade 2; no way can he be ruled out, particularly as he finished well on top in those four chases, but there have also been two major blips this season; latest was in the Cheltenham Gold Cup, for which he was just 6-1 and made most but went to nothing turning for home (writing on the wall four out); however, he's bounced back before, the likely tempo of this race can suit him better and the trip looks like doing so as well.

quotes.race: Boodles Cheltenham Gold Cup Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I didn't travel at all, Haiti Couleurs was as flat as a pancake - Sean Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: William Hill Denman Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was delighted with that. I was so nervous coming into this with all the Gold Cup chat and I'm glad it's out the way. I don't think Haiti Couleurs was doing a lot in front and while he's gone through that ground, I don't think he loves it as much as a slightly better surface. It's job done and we can freshen him up [for the Gold Cup now] - Rebecca Curtis, trainer.I was delighted. Haiti Couleurs is a bit cold in front, but from the moment something came to me I took off, and from the back of the last he's waiting [for company] again. That will do me. You could see up the straight how well he jumped. He'll be better around Cheltenham over 3m2½f with a big hill than he will at Newbury, so hopefully there's a bit left - Sean Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: Coral Welsh Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought the weight was going to beat Haiti Couleurs, but he's absolutely amazing. We knew we had him bang-on today, but that was some performance. This is the race we've wanted to win for years. He's run so well all the way round and if he got nabbed on the line I'd have been absolutely gutted. I put a line through what happened at Haydock - even in the parade ring when putting his saddle on, I knew it had come too soon. Rebecca Curtis, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Chase (Grade 1) (Registered As The Lancashire Chase) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I don't put it down to anything to do with grade of race or ability. I think it was just purely that, for whatever reason, Haiti Couleurs didn't show up. I knew from the start. Normally he'd be revving at the bit to try to get to the front and he'd be winging fences, but he didn't do any of that yesterday. It wasn't him at all. You can hear people say, 'he's just a handicapper' but that's absolute nonsense, it was nothing to do with ability yesterday, it just wasn't his day. I'm going to get a vet to do bloods, tracheal washes, back, everything, and maybe something will show up, but that definitely wasn't the normal Haiti Couleurs, so we can't take anything out of that race. We maybe ran him back too soon. We didn't think he had a hard race at Newbury, but he puts everything into his races and he'd had a gallop at Ffos Las not long before that run as well. That's a lot for a horse like him in a month. It's a shame we haven't taken anything out of yesterday as to the ceiling of his ability. We'll freshen him up and see where we go. He'll probably get an entry next week in the Welsh National, but he definitely won't run for a month or six weeks, maybe more, we'll just see how he is - Rebecca Curtis, trainer, speaking the following day.

quotes.race: BoyleSports Irish Grand National Chase (Extended Handicap Chase) (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: I can't quite believe how easy it was all happening. Haiti Couleurs got into such a good rhythm, he jumped amazing and what a job Becky has done this season. He sweated up and it wasn't smooth beforehand but as soon as we jumped he got in such a good rhythm - Sean Bowen, rider. He's just so tough. I was a little bit worried as he likes to jump his way to the front and all the time I hoped he wasn't doing too much. After the second last I got excited and I knew he'd keep going. Could you ever imagine he can become a Gold Cup-type horse? He's not slow, I know he's won over three [miles] five [furlongs] in his last two races but he doesn't need to have that trip. He loves Cheltenham too - Rebecca Curtis, trainer.

quotes.race: Princess Royal National Hunt Challenge Cup Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Haiti Couleurs is such a tough horse. He wouldn't be overly speedy, he'll just gallop all day long. His jumping is so quick and accurate - Rebecca Curtis, trainer.

quotes.race: Josh Wyke Birthday Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Haiti Couleurs had a nice novice season last term before he struck into his leg quite badly, so we had to take our time with him. He's slightly backward for his age but with racing he's just kept improving. I don't know where he'll end up really, I really fancied him for the National Hunt Chase, as he stays all day, but Sean says he's improving that much from his Aintree win to this that you wouldn't know if he would make the Brown Advisory. We'll be looking at both of those. We'll see what the handicapper does for his next race but he's a lovely prospect - Rebecca Curtis, trainer.

quotes.race: BoyleSports Best Odds Guaranteed Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Haiti Couleurs has done that fairly easily, jumping and travelling well. He's a nice horse who's very versatile on the ground. I'd hope he'd be a Welsh National type for next season. It's nice they've changed the National Hunt Chase to a handicap, so maybe we'll look at something like that in the spring. He's relatively inexperienced and we'll see how he progresses - Rebecca Curtis, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: It's been an amazing journey with him ever since he won a maiden hurdle by 18 lengths two years ago. Since then he's won another eight races, including the National Hunt Chase at last year's Cheltenham Festival, the Irish Grand National, the Welsh Grand National and the Denman Chase. His switch to fences last season brought enormous improvement. The Irish National over 3m5f was tailor-made for him and I wasn't afraid of the big Irish stables even though their horses seem to win everything over here. I'd go over there anytime I've got the horse. Apart from anything else it's a great day out for the owners. He didn't show up in the Betfair Chase - I could see that from the very start of the race. But you saw what he can do in the Welsh National, even under all that weight. He didn't particularly like the heavy ground in the Denman at Newbury but won by seven lengths and it will have sharpened him up for the Gold Cup. That's the one we all want to win. 25-02-26

runners.comment: Cheltenham Grade 2 win in January; pulled up here in Thursday's Grade 1
runners.spotlight: Won two Irish Grade 1s in the spring of 2024 as a novice and a Grade 2 at Cheltenham (near 3m2f, soft) this January; probably had something in the tank that day at Cheltenham (he travelled up strongly to take over) but he was pulled up here in Thursday's Grade 1.

quotes.race: Betfair Cotswold Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It means everything to the yard. I only have ten horses in training, I'm on the way down in that sense now, but Spillane's Tower's a quality horse. I'm very grateful to the McManus family for sending him to me. We had everything going for us today. Venetia's horse made the race for us going a good nice gallop and without that it would have been difficult for Jack Kennedy because he's not a horse who can make the running. Venetia's horse didn't throw in the towel. I'd have to say he'd have to improve to win a Gold Cup, but I think there's more in this horse. He wouldn't run on fast ground, but I'll leave that up to Frank [Berry, racing manager] and JP - Jimmy Mangan, trainer.

quotes.race: John Durkan Memorial Punchestown Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: I'm absolutely over the moon with Spillane's Tower. He hasn't been on grass since he won here at the festival. We couldn't, the ground has just been too firm. We have everything to look forward to now. Without a doubt that's the best race I've ever been involved in. You couldn't get any better - Jimmy Mangan, trainer.

quotes.race: Dooley Insurance Group Champion Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Spillane's Tower is a special horse to us. We're dreaming now, he has something special about him. He is the most relaxed and easy horse and got a beautiful and cool ride - Jimmy Mangan, trainer

quotes.race: WillowWarm Gold Cup (Chase) (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted for Jimmy [Mangan, trainer] especially because he hasn't had a good horse in a while. When he gets a good horse like that he's well able to do the job. I was keeping my powder dry as I didn't want to be in front too soon but I had to go with the gallop they were going and, to be fair, Spillane's Tower jumped well. I'm delighted and he's one to look forward to - Mark Walsh, jockey.

quotes.race: Betting Better With SkyBet Novice Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Spillane's Tower was helped by the step up in trip and he stayed well. All of his runs have been good and he is improving all the time - Frank Berry, racing manager to J.P. McManus.

quotes.race: William Hill Ireland Rated Novice Chase
quotes.quote: Spillane's Tower had two great runs and he delivered today. It turned into a sprint, we would have preferred a good gallop, but he has that little bit of class - Jimmy Mangan, trainer.

quotes.race: Cavan Developments Supporting Kill GAA Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Spillane's Tower is a nice horse and he will be better next year. He needed the trip and that ground is probably as quick as he would want it. A Summer's grass will do him the world of good - Jimmy Mangan, trainer

stable_tour.quote: I knew we were going to Cheltenham last time with a very good chance. I never lost faith in him. He acted so well there, although he'll never win by too far. He'll just get upsides and that's it. I wouldn't run him at Cheltenham unless there was juice in the ground. The horse comes first.  19-02-26

runners.comment: Ran on late when fourth in Irish Gold Cup (3m); didn't see out 3m2f so well at Cheltenham
runners.spotlight: Tongue tied on last two starts; Irish Gold Cup at Leopardstown (3m, soft) in February was also the first time he went beyond 2m5f, when 33-1 and spending most of the race out the back but running on into fourth of 12, beaten 14l; some encouragement might be derived from that but he didn't see it out so well when confronted by 3m2f in the Gold Cup at Cheltenham.

quotes.race: Boodles Cheltenham Gold Cup Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Ran well, we're happy with Firefox, jumped well, 3m2f probably just stretched him - Jack Kennedy, jockey.

quotes.race: Kildress Plumbing Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Firefox been competing at the top end the whole time and this was a good performance. I thought Jack [Kennedy] gave him a very, very good ride and just landed him there at the right time - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: WillowWarm Gold Cup (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: That's more like it. Firefox travelled and jumped nicely and that's more like the horse we saw earlier in the season. He's very good on his day and hopefully there's more to come from him next season - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Mongey Communications Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Firefox probably learned more today than in any novice chase with Henry's horse taking him on an jumping as well as him. Sam said he just gave him a squeeze coming down the hill and he picked up. I wouldn't be afraid of coming back in trip - Gordon Elliott, trainer

quotes.race: TrustATrader Top Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought Firefox ran a good race, there was no real excuse. He got the run of the race, he jumped well. He'll go chasing next season and be a proper two-mile chaser. The way he jumps a hurdle, you'd say he wants a fence. He's a good horse. It's always frustrating when you don't win but he ran a very good race so we're proud of him - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Supreme Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm a bit disappointed because I got stopped up the straight. Firefox wouldn't have been far away only for that - Jack Kennedy, jockey.

quotes.race: Kettles Country House Hotel Supporting Fingal Ravens GFC Raceday Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Firefox is a good horse. We thought he needed two and a half miles which is why we made the running. He could still go that trip, but Jack said he has so much boot and is so laidback and relaxed that everything comes very easily to him - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Play Responsibly (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: He's good. We thought Firefox was a fair horse and were disappointed that he got beaten in his first bumper but he came on plenty from that. He's not going to be a horse until next year really. Whatever he does this year is only going to be a bonus. He obviously can't go to the Cheltenham bumper because he ran in a hurdle race. We'll probably go to Fairyhouse or Punchestown. We like him - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I was delighted with him in the Irish Gold Cup. He ran a huge race from off the pace and might have earned himself a crack at the big one. We'll see how he is over the next few weeks, but it's definitely a possibility. 09-02-26

runners.comment: Trying in vain at Grade 1 level; going up markedly in trip in a handicap is mouthwatering
runners.spotlight: Just 1-11 as a chaser, largely because he keeps trying in vain at Grade 1 level; fourth in last year's Cheltenham Gold Cup was one of his peak efforts, as was this season's never-nearer fifth in a Leopardstown Grade 1 at Christmas; he didn't fare so well in the Irish Gold Cup last time but was the only one matching strides with the top-class winner on the home turn; going up markedly in trip today, in a handicap, makes him a mouthwatering proposition.

quotes.race: Boodles Cheltenham Gold Cup Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: In fairness (that mistake) and having to avoid the horse that fell might have cost Monty's Star a place, but that is it. I like that ground for him I must say. He goes on any ground, but I thought it would help him today, but maybe it didn't. We are delighted and he ran a blinder. We will get our lad home now and see how he is before making any plans - Henry De Bromhead, trainer.

quotes.race: Download The New Tote App Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Monty's Star's jumping is his greatest asset. It is tough ground to be jumping out of but he did it well. He stayed and galloped to the line and improved from the last day - Rachael Blackmore, rider.

quotes.race: Surehaul Mercedes-Benz Novice Hurdle (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Monty's Star is a big, big horse and has taken a long time. He ran really well in a maiden hurdle at Navan where he was a bit green, but I'm delighted with him today. The lads just wanted to see would he stay, and he duly did. He is in the Albert Bartlett and I imagine that is where he will go next - Henry de Bromhead, trainer

stable_tour.quote: He's in the Grand National and the Gold Cup and we're in discussions about it at the moment. The Maloneys [owners] love having runners at Cheltenham and they think the Gold Cup looks an open race, while another view would be that he's an out-and-out Grand National horse. When you look at his Brown Advisory run, he looked all over a Gold Cup horse, but I'm not sure whether he'll be as good as we thought he could be. 15-02-26

He made his hurdling debut in January when a good second to a smart rival. I expected him to come on for that, so we ran him in a Grade 3 at Clonmel for his second race. We had the odds-on favourite, Hiddenvalley Lake, but despite the difference in prices I didn't think there was that much between them as he was in receipt of 6lb, so when he swept in late to win it wasn't a surprise. He's a big horse and has taken a long time, but it has been worth the wait. That Clonmel race was the perfect springboard for Minella Indo, who finished second to Allaho in 2019 before going to Cheltenham and winning the Albert Bartlett. Hopefully lightning can strike twice as Monty's Star now heads for Cheltenham and the more testing the ground, the better his chance. 01-03-23

runners.breeder: E A R L Elevage Des Loges
runners.comment: Stays long distances; his revised mark since bold show in the Thyestes is the chief worry
runners.spotlight: Career with Willie Mullins took a long time to catch fire but it's done so this season and he looked set for victory in the Thyestes at Gowran Park (3m1f, heavy) in January when unseating at the final fence; pulled up behind Grangeclare West last time but back catalogue includes a creditable sixth in the Scottish National and fourth in bet365 Cup at Sandown, so he stays long distances; his revised mark since the Thyestes would be the chief worry.

quotes.race: Guinness Kerry National Handicap Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Spanish Harlem wasn't the cheapest horse but he just hasn't been firing. We put cheekpieces on him and he got his jumping right at long last. Danny [Mullins, jockey] came up with a plan which was to jump out, give him plenty of daylight and it worked. He jumped super but made one or two mistakes. He'll iron that out too. We'd love to produce him for the Randox Grand National at Aintree. I suppose we'd have to have a go at the Munster National or the Coral Gold Cup at Newbury and raise it like that. I think he likes nicer ground, that could be the key to him as well as plenty of jumping and longer trips - Willie Mullins, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Jim Ryan Memorial Novice Chase
quotes.quote: Sean [Cleary-Farrell] gave Spanish Harlem a good ride and he kept galloping well. I'd say nicer ground suits him and obviously those extended trips. He ran a real good race at Sandown. I'd say he'll be looking at races like the Kerry National and Munster National - David Casey, trainer's assistant.

stable_tour.quote: Cheekpieces have really helped him and brought him on. He jumped really well when winning the Kerry National and hopefully he could turn into a Grand National horse this season. He's another of mine who holds an entry in the Coral Gold Cup at Newbury. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Won 3m Grade 1 at Cheltenham last March from Stellar Story; no impact in Ireland this term
runners.spotlight: Unraced beyond 3m2f; came into his own as a novice last term, notably in the 3m Grade 1 at Cheltenham Festival which he won by 4l from Stellar Story; no impact at the top level in Ireland this season and he clambered over the final fence on his way to a heavy defeat behind several of today's rivals in a Grade 3 last time, so current prospects don't look so bright.

quotes.race: Brown Advisory Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (Registered As The Broadway Novices' Chase) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: All season Lecky Watson has improved. We just said to Sean [O'Keeffe] maybe go a little bit wider and keep out of trouble. Sean kept it very simple and it was an excellent ride. Was it the plan to have not gone over three miles this season, no, it was a case of getting them ready and running in them in whatever race possible. I hadn't been planning to go the Gold Cup route with this one, but we have to go that way now - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet, For The Fans Novice Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Lecky Watson has a good engine and settled it very quickly. He's probably more mature this season and his jumping is something we can work on - Paul Townend, jockey.

quotes.race: Bar One Racing '100% Acca Boost On Self Service Terminals' Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: He was good. Lecky Watson enjoys being in front, he jumped like a buck, took his breathers when I wanted him to, flew the last and opened up well when asked - Paul Townend, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Lawlor's Of Naas Novice Hurdle (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: The third, Lecky Watson, was unlucky too, he was just too keen the whole way - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Lecky Watson loves jumping. He was fresh and gassy through the race, so to pull out again and hold off the second horse was a good performance for one of ours at this time of the year. He can only improve - Paul Townend, rider

stable_tour.quote: Another who has an entry in the John Durkan at Punchestown, and he could start off in that. He won the Brown Advisory last season, so he's entitled to go down the Gold Cup route on the back of that. If he's not up to that level, the Grand National could also be an option. He just keeps on improving and I have a feeling he'll keep progressing this season. He jumps and gallops, and fences have been the making of him. He's a strong stayer over three miles. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Whether he'll stay 4m2f is a big question but he could outrun his odds for a long way
runners.spotlight: The furthest he's been is 3m1f in Grade 1 novice at Punchestown Festival (good to yielding) last April which he won in good style, showing improved form; went close over 2m in November and although he slipped up next time and met with heavy defeats twice since, he went well enough to the home turn in Irish Gold Cup on latest; whether he'll stay 4m2f is a big question but he could outrun his odds for a long way.

quotes.race: Dooley Insurance Group Champion Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: From halfway down the back I knew I was going to play a big part in the race, from there it was a case of keeping a good jumping rhythm. Champ Kiely put his head down between the last two and a good jump at the last sealed it. It was his first run at that trip and that's probably where you're going to see the best of him - Danny Mulllins, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Flyingbolt Novice Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: I was always going to keep it as simple as I could. Champ Kiely loves jumping fences. To be honest, I thought we built up nicely from leaving the back straight and every time he heard the other horse coming he pulled out loads. I was always in control - Paul Townend, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

quotes.race: Bellshill Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Champ Kiely did everything as it should have been done; he galloped and jumped. Paul [Townend, jockey] was very happy that he was far more relaxed over fences than he had been over hurdles, which will hopefully bring about more improvement. The two miles and five furlongs Grade 1 at the Dublin Racing Festival is a race we will probably look at. He could easily step up in trip now he's much more relaxed - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Lawlor's Of Naas Novice Hurdle (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: The Royal Bond was a bit of a messy race but Champ Kiely was only beaten four-and-a-bit lengths so I believed he had something like that in him - Danny Mullins, rider.

quotes.race: Fitzgerald's Woodlands House Hotel Novice Hurdle (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Champ Kiely was very good, he showed stamina at Galway and he backed that up with speed today. He ticks a lot of boxes and he quickened here off a strong pace. Not many can do that - Danny Mullins, rider.

quotes.race: Tote Always SP Or Better At Galway Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was hoping Champ Kiely would win but didn't think he'd do anything like that. He's moved up a few places in our novice hurdlers for this season. That looked very good. He looks a real jumping sort. I know he is only starting his novice hurdle career, but I'm already looking forward to him going over fences. I think there was a lot of confidence behind the favourite, so to come out and beat a 102-rated Flat horse like that was very good. I'll have a chat with Michael [Masterson, owner] and go through all the rest of the horses for the year before making a plan, but he looks a smart type - Willie Mullins, trainer

quotes.race: Athea INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: Champ Kiely is a big boy for a small girl. He was in my hands the whole way but when I went for him it took him a while to quicken up and he's still a bit green. He was doing all the right things at home and please God he is another nice one - Jody Townend, rider.

stable_tour.quote: You would have to be delighted with the way he ran at Naas over a trip that would have been tight for him and giving plenty of weight to the winner. He's not going to be the easiest to place this season, but he's in the John Durkan and might go there. I'm sure we'll find something for him around Christmas as well. He won a Grade 1 race over three miles, so he's quite versatile with regard to trip. 17-11-25

He's not done a lot wrong since joining us, with four wins from five. The defeat was when fourth to Marine Nationale in the Royal Bond at Fairyhouse and that was a good run, only weakening after the last. He won his Grade 1 last time out when beating Irish Point to take the Lawlor's of Naas in early January. He's improving with every run and at the moment I think he'll be best suited by the Ballymore. 08-03-23

prev_owners.owner: Lord Daresbury, Ecurie Mme Jacques Cypres & E Clayeux

runners.comment: Staying-on fourth in 2025 National off 5lb lower; scoped dirty at Cheltenham last month
runners.spotlight: Staying-on fourth in last season's Grand National (good to soft) off 5lb lower as just a 7yo; a second crack at it has been his main target this term but he looked better than ever when winning from Firefox in a hot, three-runner race at Ascot (2m5f; second run after wind surgery) in December and had an excuse (scoped dirty) at the Cheltenham Festival last month; has to be in serious calculations.

quotes.race: Howden Graduation Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Iroko just needed to go and actually have a race today. I know it was only a three-runner field but they quickened fairly up the hill and he really had to grind it out. He just takes time to get into gear. It was good to see him lengthen and get his head down and he's done well. We might go back to Kelso, where he was second to Grey Dawning last year. It's two miles seven and a nice track and not many runners go there. Then we'll probably miss Cheltenham and go straight to the Grand National. Trainers always say horses have strengthened up, but he seems a lot better this year. Jonjo comes and rides him out and he says so - Oliver Greenall, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Randox Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was very happy with Iroko. He just found everything a bit fast early on and was a bit on his head. He could have done with the ground being slower. I just didn't have the horse after the third-last but he ran on well after the last and with another year on his back I look forward to coming back again - Jonjo O'Neill Jr, rider.

quotes.race: bet365 Premier Chase (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was happy with Iroko. Jonjo thought the track was a little bit sharp for him in that grade. There were no excuses today, he was up against a good horse.  He's run well and he deserves to go for the National. I think the trip is what he wants, he seems always to be doing his best work at the end. He does normally travel a bit better in his races but they were probably going a bit quick - Oliver Greennall, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Exchange Graduation Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted with that and for a first run everything went to plan, bar winning. Iroko jumped brilliantly, travelled really nicely and bar winning, I couldn't have been happier. We'll probably look at something like the Cotswold Chase and maybe once the National weights are out a handicap somewhere - Josh Guerriero, trainer.

quotes.race: Huyton Asphalt Franny Blennerhassett Memorial Mildmay Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: To get two runs out of him after his injury is unbelievable. Iroko just gallops and round here it's probably too sharp for him and we probably bumped into one. Jonjo said he got stuck down the inner and while he probably wouldn't have won, he didn't quite get a clear enough run up the home straight. He tries and stays and jumps so well. When he's flat out he still jumps really well. It was fairly tacky ground out there and he was tired. He could go to Punchestown and there are races like the Coral Gold Cup next season - Oliver Greenall, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Stan Mellor Memorial Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Iroko was pretty much foot perfect, bar a couple of small mistakes. He loved the ground and we thought he would like three miles more, but he has travelled like a dream there over two and a half miles. We will probably stick to two and a half for the time being. At Aintree he looked like he wanted a trip, but maybe he had a hard enough race at Cheltenham and he just ran a bit flat at Aintree. Maybe that wasn't his true reading. Whether you go for a smaller race then go up a level or go straight up a level next we will just have to see. On a tighter track like Kempton on better ground you could go three miles, but we will see how we go. The Kauto Star could be considered. If it is soft ground at Cheltenham he would probably stay at two and a half miles and if it was quick he would go over three miles - Oliver Greenall, joint trainer.

quotes.race: Winners Wear Cavani Sefton Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a very good run and Iroko is a lovely horse. Mark said if he had run over three miles before he might have been a bit more positive with him. It was his first time over three miles and you couldn''t have done that. He was staying all the way to the line and he will be an exciting chaser for next season. We would possibly go back to two and a half to start with over fences at somewhere like Wetherby - Oliver Greenall, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Martin Pipe Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was amazing. We always knew Iroko was nice but we just felt that maybe he might be tapped for toe around here. He held his position, came off the bridle early enough but jumped so well even when he was off the bridle. He's so easy, tough and honest. He shows nothing at home and he's not a good work horse but he's so straightforward. He doesn't take much work and he's a dream. He toughed it out, winged the last and it was great. Absolutely brilliant - Oliver Greenall, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Slingsby Gin Peak Cap & Pearls Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We've always liked Iroko. I was slightly concerned about the ground and he came off the bridle early enough but he battled on well. He's bound to come from that, he's still a big baby - Oliver Greenall, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We're going to take the same route back to the Grand National. We were delighted with his fourth place and there are many reasons to believe he could improve a lot in the race. It was unfortunate it was good ground because he needs it soft. He's not very quick and was run off his feet and struggled with his jumping because of that. He's a year stronger, has more experience and he's had a run in the race. The first thing Jonjo [O'Neill Jr] said when he came in was that it was a year too soon. We're starting him off in the graduation chase at Haydock on Saturday. It looks a stronger race than last year, when he was second, and I suspect he'll need it. He could then go to Ascot again - if he doesn't win at Haydock - and there's Cheltenham Trials day, with Kelso or the Ladbrokes Trophy at Kempton after that. He's only seven, he looks very good and he's improved. 20-11-25

He ran in the Ultima at Cheltenham on Tuesday but was disappointing. I can't say what went wrong but now that he's home we can take a good look at him. He was never travelling, even when he was close up for the first mile. But let's not forget he's an all-round better horse this season. We gave him a wind op at the start of the campaign and he found racing more comfortable. He used to look a bit awkward and hang a bit left, but he doesn't seem to do that now. He's more experienced and looks stronger. All being well with him, he'll go for the Grand National, in which he was a strong-finishing fourth last year. He was right out the back at one stage, but he was the only one out of the first four to come from behind. Jonjo [O'Neill Jr] got off and said it was a year too soon, so it was a massive performance. A bit of soft ground would help massively as it would slow the whole thing down. 13-03-26

runners.comment: 11yo who's having a tremendous season, over Cheltenham cross-country on last two outings
runners.spotlight: Experienced 11yo who's having a tremendous season; 66-1 winner of a top 3m handicap at Leopardstown (made most) over Christmas and took his form to another new level on the 3m5f Cheltenham cross-country course on last two outings, winning easily on first occasion and well clear of the third when he chased home Final Orders at last month's Festival; well handicapped and with the trip likely to suit, he's a leading contender.

quotes.race: Glenfarclas Cross Country Chase (A Limited Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We got a good run round and Favori De Champdou jumped well, but he probably spent a bit too long in the air at the last. He was giving the winner a lot of weight and we know how much that horse is suited by good ground. It was a good run - Jack Kennedy, jockey.

quotes.race: Glenfarclas Cross Country Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Favori De Champdou fell at the water when he ran here in December, but it definitely sweetened him up and he did everything right today, he enjoyed himself. I am delighted. He seems to have a new lease of life and it's great to win another cross country race as these races have been close to us and it's nice to win another one. I didn't actually want Jack to ride him, I wanted Sean Bowen but Jack jocked him off, he said I'm riding him! We'll come back for this race at the Festival and he is also definitely a Grand National type - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Chase (Extended Handicap Chase) (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: To be honest, I thought I got a handy enough lead and Favori De Champdou was game all the way to the line. Dad [Warren] had him as a pointer, so I'm sure he'll be happy at home too. Even as a novice hurdler, he was black type and Saddler Maker is a good sire - Sam Ewing, jockey.

quotes.race: Liam & Valerie Brennan Florida Pearl Novice Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Favori De Champdou came on from the last day and we knew he had, but I thought that would be tougher. Jack said he stayed very well and jumped brilliant. It was a hot enough race and he's a nice horse - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Lyons Of Limerick Jaguar Land Rover Novice Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Favori De Champdou did it well. Jordan was happy the whole way. He jumped well and handled the ground and didn't do a whole lot in front. He's going the right way - Ian Amond, travelling head groom.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Favori De Champdou did everything right and Jack gave him a grand ride. He looked big in the ring but he jumped great. I would imagine he'll go chasing straight away after missing a year - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's come alive of late. He won the Paddy Power Chase at a big price but there was no fluke about it. He won it fair and square. We then took him to Cheltenham for the cross-country race last month and he bolted up. He never missed a beat and you'd like to think he'll go back there next month with a big chance.  09-02-26

runners.comment: Career-best form in the autumn; last year's Grand National and latest start are concerns
runners.spotlight: Career-best form in the autumn this season, including a win at Cheltenham (3m1f) and second to Panic Attack in the Coral Gold Cup at Newbury (3m2f); flopped when favourite in the Grade 3 won by Grangeclare West at Fairyhouse in February, admittedly after 12 weeks off but there's the additional worry of last year's Grand National in which he was 16-1 and raced very prominently but faded steadily from three out.

quotes.race: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was great for Three Card Brag to get his head in front as he's been knocking on the door in those big handicaps for the last couple of years. It's hard to win with him as he's been creeping up the handicap the whole time, but he travelled well today - Gordon Elliott, trainer.Three Card Brag jumped and travelled great throughout the race. We didn't go much of a gallop, but he stayed on well - Jack Kennedy, jockey.

quotes.race: Randox Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Three Card Brag gave me a great spin but he was just doing too much the whole way. He was jumping so well that he was just jumping into the bridle every time. Hopefully he'll be back next year, older and wiser - Sean Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Novice Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Three Card Brag ran well in his own right. He needed that run to qualify for the Grand National - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: QuinnBet Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Three Card Brag has had a few niggly problems, and just a few things didn't work out for him. I imagine we will probably head straight for the English National with him now - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Easter Festival 8-10 April Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Three Card Brag is a nice horse and stays at it well. It wasn't ideal having to make it because he is lazy but the further they went the better he was - Ian Amond, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction Maiden Hurdle (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Three Card Brag looked good. He jumped well apart from one but what impressed me most was the way he went on to the line. I think there is plenty of improvement in him - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I always knew there was a nice staying handicap in him and he put it all together to pick up a nice pot at Cheltenham on Saturday. He had been knocking on the door in those big handicaps for the last couple of years. It's hard to win with him as he's been creeping up the handicap the whole time, but he travelled well on Saturday and he travelled well for a long way in the Grand National, too. He probably did just too much in the first part of the race. 26-10-25

runners.comment: Slow early jumping in 3m1f Grade 1 novice at Cheltenham but he made late inroads into 4th
runners.spotlight: A first-season novice won the 2022 Grand National when unraced beyond 3m1f and this Irish challenger (who's one year older) bids to repeat the feat; hat-trick this season included two small-field Grade 2s and when his winning sequence came to an end it was in the Grade 1 novice at Cheltenham Festival, where some slow jumping in the early stages left him with plenty to do but he made late inroads to finish fourth; he still looks capable of better and the longer trip could suit.

quotes.race: William Hill Racing Bet Builder Ten Up Novice Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: I wasn't going overly quick because of the testing ground. Oscars Brother jumped really well and hit the line well. He's versatile ground-wise although I do think the slower the ground the better, 3m is the key- Daniel King, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.  After the last day, we had this race pencilled in and I suppose we can make more plans now. Oscars Brother takes his racing well, so we will see how he is during the week and go from there. The timing of the Brown Advisory would be good. He keeps improving, so you never know where he could end up. We did the National entry last week and while we would need one more run to qualify, we still have time on our side - Connor King, trainer

quotes.race: Boodles Florida Pearl Novice Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: We've always liked Oscars Brother. He did well over hurdles, but we always hoped he'd be a better chaser. I've been keeping my eye on this race for a long time. I remember watching this race last year just before I rode him out and I thought it'd be a nice race to aim for. It's disappointing for us that they have got rid of the three-mile novice chase at Leopardstown as that would have been ideal. Limerick [the Faugheen Novice Chase] is two mile five and it will probably be heavy ground so that might suit him, and we could travel as well - Connor King, trainer.He's a dream to ride and to train. Oscars Brother was good and tough today, he's improving away. He's such a good attitude, jumps for fun so a nice horse to look forward with - Daniel King, jockey.

runners.comment: Nothing to prove for stamina or this track, but he cracked alarmingly on last two outings
runners.spotlight: Usually goes well in the mud; last season's hat-trick culminated in the 4m2f Midlands National and he rallied to go very close against Twig in the 3m2f Becher over these fences on first outing this term; while there was so much to admire to that point, he's cracked with alarming speed in 3m and 4m1f races on his last two outings.

quotes.race: William Hill Half A Mill Becher Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Mr Vango loved the fences and he's quite bright because he worked out that you don't have to give them too much air. I couldn't be more delighted with him as he wants all of the trip and slightly softer ground, then you've got a big chance. He's such a big horse you can't make definite plans, it's very much where is the ground and how is the horse. The Welsh National is in my mind, it probably won't go heavy enough for the Classic Chase and he loves the ground at Haydock so the Grand National Trial is a possible. We wouldn't come back here on anything that isn't softer than good to soft because they'll go too fast for him - Sara Bradstock, trainer.

quotes.race: JenningsBet Midlands Grand National (Handicap Chase) (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We ran Mr Vango with slight trepidation on slightly quicker ground but they've done a great job at Uttoxeter. He's the biggest thoroughbred I've seen - my measuring stick honestly isn't long enough but he's at least 18 hands - and he is only getting to full strength now. The National is the dream next season. He would need ease in the ground but hopefully he has the right attributes for the race. The way he jumps and everything he does suggests it should suit him. I'd love to be able to run him there - Sara Bradstock, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Peter Marsh Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Mr Vango is such a fantastic horse because he can't go any faster than that, but he just keeps going and jumps beautifully. He's a giant and he has to try very hard. We're hoping and praying that we get the wettest spring ever and we can run him in the National, but I'd only run him on heavy ground. He'll go to the Midlands National if I don't think the ground is going to be soft for the Grand National - Sara Bradstock, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Exchange London National Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Mr Vango is a star for us. He can't go very fast but he never knows when to stop. He's a big gentle giant really and it's a case of the softer the better for him. If all goes well he'll go for the Welsh National now. I wouldn't run him on good going, but if he gets his ground it would be perfect - Sara Bradstock, trainer.

quotes.race: My Pension Expert Devon National Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: If all races were like that, then it would be nice. Sara [Bradstock] said to get into a nice rhythm because Mr Vango has jumped loads of fences at home and staying chases are his game. I felt I went a nice gallop and it wasn't anything major, but down the back straight I slowed it up and expected them to come and get me. I looked round but he just galloped and jumped them into the ground - Ben Jones, jockey.

runners.breeder: Mr & Mrs D Futter & Peel Bloodstock
runners.owner: Sullivan Group Limited & P Crowley & Neill Hughes

prev_owners.owner: Sullivan Group Limited & P Crowley & Neill Hughes
Sullivan Bloodstock Limited & Neill Hughes & P Crowley

runners.comment: Staying-on third over an extended 3m4f at Sandown (good; 5lb higher today) last April
runners.spotlight: One positive is his staying-on third over an extended 3m4f in the bet365 Gold Cup at Sandown (good; 5lb higher today) last April; another is that he's trained by Willie Mullins, who described him in November as likely to be "an ideal type for the Grand National"; after a solid reappearance, he's been pulled up in good handicaps on his last two outings but both were in the mud and he got loose before the latest, which presumably didn't help.

quotes.race: QuinnBet Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: High Class Hero did it nicely. The ground was quite testing as they had a lot of rain before racing. He's in the Brown Advisory and he would look like that type of an animal. We'll probably head that direction. Loughglynn will probably stay at home and we'll find something for him. Overall, I'm very happy with them - Willie Mullins, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: Stamina is his strong suit. The further he goes the better he seems to be and he ran a cracker to finish third in the bet365 Gold Cup at Sandown at the end of last season. I'd imagine he'll be an ideal type for the Grand National this season. That's what's in my head. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Unraced beyond 3m2f but has strongly suggested that he has serious stamina; e-w appeal
runners.spotlight: Second to Lecky Watson in the 3m Grade 1 novice at Cheltenham last March; while comfortably dismissed in the closing stages of his three starts this winter, the first two of those were Grade 1 events and giving 8lb to Grangeclare West and Gerri Colombe at Fairyhouse (blinkers replaced cheekpieces) on latest outing makes that result look a whole lot better; above all, perhaps, while unraced beyond 3m2f, he has strongly suggested on plenty of occasions that he has serious stamina reserves; each-way appeal.

quotes.race: Brown Advisory Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (Registered As The Broadway Novices' Chase) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Stellar Story's jumping is really starting to come together. That was a great performance by him. Hopefully there are better days ahead with him - Danny Gilligan, jockey.

quotes.race: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Novice Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: I was thrilled with Stellar Story. If we could get him just to jump a bit better there is a big day in him. He wasn't as guessy at his fences today, and he could go for the Brown Advisory too - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Boodles Florida Pearl Novice Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Stellar Story didn't want to be in front and the two of them chopped and change. He didn't have the benefit of a run and took a couple of chances. He will probably head for Leopardstown at Christmas - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Albert Bartlett Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (Registered As The Spa Novices' Hurdle) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We didn't think Stellar Story was a 33-1 chance to be honest, but we only made the call at ten to ten on Wednesday to run him. He was going to go to Aintree but another horse had a niggle and I couldn't run him. They went no gallop and Sam was in the right position. He's a quality horse. He's gorgeous and a chaser for next season - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Kilberry Pub & Kitchen Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Stellar Story is a nice horse. Jack said he'd come on from it too as he had a bit of a blow. I was a bit worried in the back straight when the other horse was going with us but he said he'd come on plenty from it and we're delighted. He was bought to be a big staying chaser - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Nursery Of Champions (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: Stellar Story learned a lot from his run last day. All he does is stay. He roamed around a lot last day but was good and straight today and he is a nice horse for the future - Harry Swan, rider

stable_tour.quote: If the ground turned up soft on Gold Cup day, he could outrun his odds. He's an Albert Bartlett winner who likes Cheltenham and he's a proper stayer. 09-02-26

runners.comment: Stays but he was too zestful in this race last year; now tongue tied first time
runners.spotlight: Took well to these fences in last year's renewal but subsided rapidly after three out, which might have been surprising for one who'd won a 4m2f Midlands National (March 2024) but he seemed to race a bit too zestfully in the front rank; 3lb lower today, having run respectably on reappearance but moderately in two hurdle races since (wind surgery before latest); now tongue tied first time; a bit to prove.

quotes.race: Randox Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I couldn't have asked for a better ride. The one mistake I made was that I kicked Beauport out of the gate and he ended up doing way too much. He was really enthusiastic and one thing you can't afford to do here over four and a half miles is race too enthusiastically. I've learned, and there will be another day - Sam Twiston-Davies, jockey.

quotes.race: 1st Class Logistics Berkshire National Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: His jumping was spectacular. Beauport has had a few physical problems but Nigel Twiston-Davies and his team have done brilliantly to get him into that kind of shape. He should be put up enough after that to sneak into the National so that must be a race we've got to think very hard about. We always thought he was a potential National horse and, after a Midlands and Berkshire National, we probably need to go to Liverpool at some stage. There won't be many British runners but I hope he can be one of them - Bryan Burrough, owner.

quotes.race: bet365 Midlands Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Beauport has run one bad race in his life and the owners have shown great loyalty to Jordan. He's such an honest horse and when he gets his conditions he's hard to get past. Bryan and Philippa [Burrough] always buy horses who are National types, so Aintree could be something to consider next season, but this is a big race in its own right and it's great to win it - Carl Llewellyn, stable representative.

quotes.race: Colin Parker Memorial Intermediate Chase (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was nice to jump well first time over fences and to have a good experience. At the weights, Beauport was well-in on his ratings getting the weight from Millers Bank. He was entitled to win and I don't think he's surprised anyone. He might go to Newbury now at the end of November - there's a nice novice chase there - Carl Llewellyn, assistant to Nigel Twiston-Davies. ,

quotes.race: Optimum Pay Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Beauport is a lovely horse. Dropping him back in trip wasn't ideal but we made sure it was a good gallop and he kept going well. I ride him quite a bit at home and he's quite strong - he always runs off with me! It's lovely to ride him regularly and I can't thank his owners enough. Winners on these big days are what you need to get your name out there and I'm closing in on losing the claim - Jordan Nailor, jockey.

quotes.race: European Breeders' Fund Paddy Power 'National Hunt' Novices' Handicap Hurdle Final (Grade 3) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Beauport is my first winner here and my first Graded or Listed win too. The ground really helped him out. I was thinking to myself when I got to the front I was there too soon and I'd have been fuming with myself if he'd have got beaten. But all he does is stay and it was always going to be really hard work for anything coming from behind to get me on the ground - Jordan Nailor, jockey.

runners.owner: Vincent Caldwell & Angela Shamoon & Mrs A Shamoon Ibgi

prev_owners.owner: Vincent Caldwell & Angela Shamoon & Mrs A Shamoon Ibgi

runners.comment: Tremendous response on the run-in to win 4m Scottish National last April; 12lb higher now
runners.spotlight: Leopardstown seventh to Favori De Champdou at Christmas was a glimpse of what he's capable of; the performance which really gets the juices flowing, however, came in the Scottish National at Ayr (4m, good to soft) last April when very confidently ridden and unleashed to find a tremendous response on the run-in, cutting down the leader; it's very hard to rule him out after that, despite the 12lb higher mark.

quotes.race: Coral Scottish Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I just wanted to get Captain Cody settled early and creep him into the race. I followed him at Cheltenham last time and he was too free. He probably unshipped Danny Mullins because he was going so well, he was overracing, so the plan was to get his head dropped early. As soon as he did that he got into a lovely rhythm. I wanted to go wide because he hasn't had that many runs over fences and I wanted to let him see his fences. It couldn't have gone all the better all the way round. I didn't want to get there too soon. I knew I was going to beat Johnny. Even at the last I thought let's just get him over it, and away he went - Harry Cobden, jockey.

quotes.race: Paddy Kehoe Suspended Ceilings Novice Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Jody was very good. She minded her own business and kept Captain Cody balanced and jumping. She's always there riding winners all the time for us. When you consider how light she is, she must have to carry a stone and a half of lead every day - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Ladies Auction Maiden Hurdle (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Captain Cody had a top-class run at Cheltenham last year. His jumping was a bit rusty at times but he was very good at the last two when it counted - Patrick Mullins, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Auction (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Captain Cody has definitely improved. I know Patrick thought his horse would come on for the run at Punchestown but I knew my fellow would too - Jody Townend, rider.

stable_tour.quote: A thorough stayer who would gallop all day long. He showed his stamina when he won the Scottish National at Ayr and I'd imagine he'll have the Grand National on his radar this season. The Irish equivalent might be an option, too, as he's a winner around Fairyhouse over hurdles. 17-11-25

prev_owners.owner: Lord Daresbury, Ecurie Mme Jacques Cypres & Laurent Couetil

runners.comment: Constant improver; went close when upped to 3m1f at Cheltenham after some jumping errors
runners.spotlight: Improved his rating in every one of his eight chases, winning four and that includes the 2m4f Plate at last year's Cheltenham Festival; first venture much beyond 2m5f had to wait until his return to Cheltenham last month, in which he came from out the back to get within half a length of the winner Johnnywho; that showed he stays 3m1f and suggested he's still capable of better, but his jumping contained unnerving moments; wears cheekpieces first time and a half-brother probably stays 4m.

quotes.race: Trustmarque Ultima Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a very good run, but it's so frustrating. Jagwar missed one important jump down the back and I do think this track made a big difference to him. As Mark [Walsh] said, it was so sharp for him and it's a lot sharper than the New course, and it looked like that. Because he wasn't jumping, Mark said he'd go out wide to get a bit more light, which helped, but then he was losing so much ground on the bends. It's just annoying that it hasn't gone our way.
