He's such a big horse, he just struggles to get himself organised. He's got a massive engine and I think we're going to go for the National now. I know he doesn't jump that well, but he's safe and the National course will help his jumping. You run in a straight line and he can use his big stride. With the fences there being a bit different, it might make him concentrate a bit more. We didn't put cheekpieces on him today because I just thought, up in trip, he might have been a bit keen, but he could end up with them now in the National -  Josh Guerriero, joint trainer.Jagwar looked like he stayed but he made the odd mistake. We'll have a look [at the Grand National] -  Oliver Greenall, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Exchange Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I don't think we can go into a Graded race [Ryanair] off the back of that. Jagwar needed to be winning, so we'll see. Jonjo [O'Neill Jr.] said turning in that he felt like he was going to take off and win easy, but in that sticky ground and with the weight it dragged it out of him. He looks so relaxed now that he might want further, and it might help his jumping. I think spring ground will help him. When he won in March, it was wet sort of soft ground, and the only other time he ran on this sticky surface, he was beaten at Uttoxeter. It's frustrating, he's run well with a lot of weight, but the other horse has been tough and outbattled him - Josh Guerriero, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Support The Hunt Family Fund December Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jonjo [O'Neill Jr, jockey] said Jagwar was just a bit rusty having not run for a long time. He got shuffled back a little bit through the race and lost his position. It then turned into a sprint, and they haven't gone quick at all. The winner has got a freebie in front really. Jumping the second last, he looked like he was motoring. He missed the last but wouldn't have won anyway. He will come of for it and we'll stick at two and a half for the moment. He could come back here on New Year's Day or Trials Day - Oliver Greenall, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: TrustATrader Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: First time out over fences Jagwar's jumping wasn't great; last time at Cheltenham he was really good, but I think in a more competitive race his jumping just let him down at a few, but he just kept coming back on the bridle and Jonjo said he had plenty of horse underneath him. He made a mistake at the last but he's won with his ears pricked. He's just a big baby. He's the biggest horse we've ever had, he measures 18hh, so he's still fairly weak and needs to muscle up behind. Once he does I think his jumping will probably improve. You see him drag his back legs through the fences a bit, which isn't ideal - Oliver Greenall, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Timeform Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jagwar's jumping was a lot better today. They went quite steady early which helped him. He was quite keen early in his career but settled well today and it was perfect. It's always hard when you have two in the same race but there weren't many options for them. Both horses needed to come here to see they could handle the track going forward and they have both done that today. I think they have both got improvement to come and have shown they can handle the track. The two-and-a-half-mile novices' handicap should be ideal for them both - Oliver Greenall, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Bobby Renton Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Jagwar was a bit novicey to start with and he became very keen over hurdles so I was anxious to get him switched off. After the last he stuck it out when others probably wouldn't have - Jonjo O'Neill Jr, rider.

quotes.race: Come Racing At Carlisle In 2024 Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jagwar made hard work of it but it's hard work out there and Nicky Richards was very complimentary about the second. We may give him one more quiet run and then look at Aintree but we'll have to see what the owner wants to do - Oliver Greenall, joint trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We took him out of the Paddy Power as we just didn't want to bottom him out on his first run of the season, carrying 12st on heavy ground. We hope he's better than a handicapper, so we need to keep his confidence high. He looks physically stronger and could still be improving. He might go to Newbury on November 28, but we're more likely to wait for the December Gold Cup. It helps that he likes Cheltenham and there are handicaps for him there on New Year's Day or Trials day. To win the Plate how he did was amazing as he missed the last four fences and still won well. He'd have to improve a lot, but the dream could be the Ryanair. 20-11-25

He ran a brilliant race in the Ultima at Cheltenham on Tuesday, beaten only half a length by Johnnywho. It might have been a different result if he had jumped better but he hit one hard and brushed through a few. He was still brave enough to challenge up the straight. The JP [McManus] team is really keen to go for the Grand National and he had to run over 3m to do so, so the Ultima was his last chance. His work over the last few weeks has been amazing. He's got plenty of pace and the Ultima proved that he stays. With the National nowadays, you probably need a strong traveller who has a bit of a kick rather than an out-and-out stayer. It would be a big ask first time over the unique Aintree fences but it might help him concentrate more with his jumping. 13-03-26

prev_owners.owner: Ms Kiva O'Brien & Mrs J M Walker

runners.comment: Joint-third fav for this in 2025 but fell at the ninth; nothing to shout about this winter
runners.spotlight: Won major 3m handicaps at Leopardstown over fences (by 7l, going away) and hurdles before starting joint-third favourite for last year's National, but he fell on the first circuit; it's too early to forget his best performance (Christmas 2024) but with nothing to shout about in his two races this winter, this time he could be an outsider.

quotes.race: Race And Stay At Leopardstown Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Perceval Legallois was very nimble over hurdles. I thought coming here he's a better chaser than he is a hurdler but he was good there. He's in the Grand National so we'll have to consider it - Gavin Cromwell, trainer

quotes.race: Paddy Power Chase (Extended Handicap Chase) (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Perceval Legallois got me out of trouble! It didn't go to plan. I didn't want to be as far back as I was. They kicked on down the back straight and I was a good bit back, further than I wanted to be, but I weaved my way through and he winged the last. I thought coming down to the second-last I had a chance if he kept going the way he was going. I got a great kick out of that because the horse deserved it. He's been unlucky on his last few runs. I knew the ability was there but nothing went right on his last few runs - Mark Walsh, jockey.

quotes.race: P.J. Foley Memorial INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: That was great from Percival Legallois. We've liked him and I was fairly confident he'd handle conditions. Obviously we were very afraid of Willie's horse coming here but I'm not one bit surprised because he has shown us plenty at home - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He did well last season, winning the Paddy Power at Leopardstown over Christmas and then going back there to win over hurdles at the Dublin Racing Festival. He has an entry in the Coral Gold Cup. There's nothing set in stone - he could also go back over hurdles at some stage. 04-11-25

He's been a bit frustrating and the handicapper keeps pushing him up a little bit despite him not winning. He might just not be well handicapped anymore but hopefully he'll have a good chance in one of those staying handicap chases if things fall his way. 13-11-24

runners.comment: 11l fourth off this mark to Panic Attack at Newbury (3m2f) and stuck to his task very well
runners.spotlight: Fourth behind two of these in 3m Grade 1 novice event at Cheltenham last March; ran creditably all three starts this winter, notably 11l fourth of 24 off this mark to Panic Attack at Newbury (3m2f) in November when he stuck to his task very well having been left at the shambolic start; improvement is needed but that race gave encouragement for longer trips and his dam is half-sister to Cappa Bleu who was placed in this race in 2012 and 2013.

quotes.race: Brown Advisory Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (Registered As The Broadway Novices' Chase) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Gorgeous Tom ran a blinder. First run over the trip and he stayed at it really well. Really happy with him - Darragh O'Keefe, jockey.

quotes.race: Louis Fitzgerald Hotel Hurdle
quotes.quote: We've always liked Gorgeous Tom. We gave him a break after Christmas. We hoped on better ground and stepping him up in trip would suit him - Henry de Bromhead, trainer.

quotes.race: Book Your Summer Season BBQ Packages At Naas Racecourse Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Gorgeous Tom deserved that after some good runs. He battled it out and hopefully he will improve on better ground. A step up in trip will suit him - Henry de Bromhead, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We were delighted with his run at Down Royal when second behind Firefox - he looked right back to form. He's entered in the Coral Gold Cup at Newbury, so he could potentially go there, but it's not certain. 11-11-25

runners.comment: Well handicapped on peak efforts but those past glories may now be too distant
runners.spotlight: 11lb below his peak mark and well handicapped judged on best efforts, the most recent of which were over 3m on good ground late in 2024; muted in this three runs this term, only one of which was over fences but he ended up tailed off in that Wetherby race, which he'd won a year earlier; those past glories may now be too distant.

quotes.race: bet365 Charlie Hall Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I never wrote The Real Whacker off. We just had no luck. Every time we went to run him, the sky opened the night before. He got his ground today. I'm delighted to get him back, I had him fairly right going to Listowel and he unfortunately unseated but we were happy with the ground today. The ground is the key to him. He won't go for the Betfair Chase, he'll maybe go for the King George and then the Cotswold Chase, then hopefully the Gold Cup - Paddy Neville, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes King George VI Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The Real Whacker travelled well and jumped well for his first time in open company. He stayed on really well at the end, which I was happy with. He missed the start for some reason today, and we were always chasing after that. I like the way he stayed on at the end and the Gold Cup is still on the agenda. Cheltenham is a place that he likes. I think we might go straight to the Gold Cup - Patrick Neville, trainer.

quotes.race: Brown Advisory Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (Registered As The Broadway Novices' Chase) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was toying with the Gold Cup this year but we made the decision to try to give The Real Whacker a bit more experience and mind him with the view to coming back next year. We'll give him a good summer as he might have done enough now for this year. He could go to Punchestown but we'll see how he comes out of this. He'll probably go to Listowel in the autumn because it's one of my favourite tracks - Patrick Neville, trainer.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Novices' Chase (Registered as The Dipper Novices' Chase) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was thinking in my head that The Real Whacker had improved for his last run and I knew he had improved at home. I took my time with him and I saw this race and said we will go for it and make it a test of jumping. Looking at Monmiral you had to respect him as he is a Grade One winner, but this horse is progressing and is on the up. Hopefully he will be a Grade One winner soon. We will come back for the festival and enter him in a couple of them. We might even go for the Gold Cup! - Patrick Neville, trainer.

quotes.race: mallardjewellers.com Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The Real Whacker is a smashing horse and we've always loved him. Fences are his game. He's gorgeous and would probably be better on softer ground. Gavin Sheehan was brilliant on him and his jumping was outstanding - Patrick Neville, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I might have made a couple of wrong decisions with him last season, but with a horse like him there aren't that many races. People were doubting him but I never lost the faith and I was delighted to win the Charlie Hall last month. We had him right for his return in the Kerry National and he was running a massive race but, unfortunately, he hit a fence and unseated Sam [Twiston-Davies]. The ground dried up at Wetherby and the race came at the right time. He's come out of it really well and we had him in the Betfair Chase but took him out on the day because of the ground. With the form he's in, he could possibly run in the King George after all. We'd have to supplement him but we've looked into it. It would be ground dependent but we'll have a good idea of the ground and weather forecast by then. He finished fourth in it last year and ran very well for a first run in open company. You can run him at any track - it's the ground that's key. There's a race at Wetherby on Boxing Day as well, but we'll look at the King George because it's a wide-open race. We're still thinking of the Cotswold Chase and then the Gold Cup, but it'll depend on the ground. If the Cheltenham Festival came up soft like it did last year, we'd go the Aintree route. There's the Bowl and we'll probably put him in the Grand National as well. Everyone keeps telling me that's a good race for him, so we'll see. 11-12-24

runners.comment: Third in the 3m5f Irish National last April but completed only four of his eight chases
runners.spotlight: Third in the 3m5f Irish National last April, despite an indifferent round of jumping, and third of 16 with cheekpieces at Leopardstown on latest outing was his best form, despite just the 2m5f; kept jumping out to his right in the latter and although a case can be made for him, it would have to gloss over that he's completed only four of his eight chases.

quotes.race: Munster Hurdle
quotes.quote: Quai De Bourbon is a good jumper but the hurdles are a bit small for him. It turned into a bit of a staying race on the testing ground. He is going to be a stayer - Paul Townend, rider.

quotes.race: ALTO EQUINE Building Solutions Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Quai De Bourbon lacked a bit of concentration, when I gave him a slap and left him on to the last it was the best hurdle he jumped. He's a staying type - Paul Townend, rider

stable_tour.quote: He got very tired in the Troytown at Navan and was disappointing. We'll get him home and see how is he before making any future plans. I would like to think there is a nice handicap in him at some stage this season. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Faded in a 3m7f race; clearly his best five ratings were registered on soft or heavy going
runners.spotlight: Faded into sixth at Punchestown (3m7f) last May on his only attempt at a marathon trip; worth another go, having rallied so well to win a major 3m handicap at Navan in November, but it's a little hard to ignore that clearly his best five ratings have been registered on soft or heavy going, as have all his four wins.

quotes.race: Clinton Higgins Chartered Accountants Novice Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: It shows how good those beginners' chases are with Willie's horses. They can be closer to Grade 1 chases than beginners' chases. Answer To Kayf appreciated the drop in class and that soft ground is a big help to him. I'm thrilled with the way he did it. Handicap company is his level for now, but with more experience he might take on better company by the end of the season. We would love to go back to Cheltenham. The pnly race he can run in is the novice handicap chase, so we might go there and hopefully it will rain for the week leading up to it - Terence O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction Novice Hurdle (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Answer To Kayf is twice the horse he was. He jumped really well and he saw it out well. The final of this series at Punchestown is the main aim, but he has an entry in the Albert Bartlett and he will probably get one in the Martin Pipe - Terence O'Brien, trainer

stable_tour.quote: He had a nice mark at Naas and did it well. He's not qualified for any other race other than the novice handicap so that's the aim and he's in good form. He ran a cracker in the Martin Pipe last season and we're hoping he's a better chaser than hurdler. He's not spectacular over a fence, but he's quick and efficient. 20-2-25

runners.comment: Second in the 3m1f Grade 1 novice chase at this meeting last year; below form since
runners.spotlight: Twice second in Grade 1 novice events last season, most notably when upped substantially in trip to 3m1f at this meeting; possibilities judged on that performance (unraced over further) and although he's been nowhere near that form since, his closest finish this term came when a staying-on fifth of 18 over 2m7f as a hurdler; just a 7yo but not totally dismissed.

quotes.race: Guinness 00 Faugheen Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: That was a great run. We didn't go quick and it developed into a bit of a sprint, but Jordans came home well. I thought I had a chance at the second-last but he was just beaten by a very good horse - Richie Deegan, jockey.

quotes.race: BetVictor Novice Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: I thought Jordans would go away and win at the second-last, but he just pricked his ears a bit in front. I was in front a bit soon. He popped the last and it just gave the other horse a chance to come back to us, but I never felt like I was going to be headed. He jumped well and will improve again - Richard Deegan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: I'm not totally sure where he's going to start off yet, but it will be in a staying chase somewhere and it will be interesting to see where he eventually fits in. He could potentially run in the Grand National, but there's a good bit to happen between then and now. He's a staying chaser and he's in that rating zone. 23-11-25

runners.comment: Has taken so well to Cheltenham cross-country; best performances away from soft ground
runners.spotlight: 10yo who's had 70 races (only one of today's rivals has managed even half that) and won 11; latest was the 3m5f cross-country at Cheltenham Festival, comfortably holding off Favori De Champdou for career-best form off the same mark as today; having taken so well to that discipline (he also won there in December) and produced his best performances away from soft ground, he has to be considered seriously.

quotes.race: Glenfarclas Cross Country Chase (A Limited Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I knew conditions would really suit Final Orders and Conor [Stone-Walsh] was very good on him. He ran really well on Trials Day but his wind isn't so good on soft ground and we actually gave him a little wind surgery after that and it really worked for him. I was confident he was in great form and Conor gave him a brilliant ride. The more the ground dried I thought it would play to Final Orders' strengths, but at the same time Stumptown is so good around here, although the ground drying up was a negative for him. I thought at the last though that Favori du Champdou was cantering upsides us - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.I had no real plan, just get a good start and go wherever Final Orders was happy, but I was conscious that I wanted to cover the least ground as possible, so I let him rock down to the Canal Turn, and he jumped that well and ended up on the inside, and I was happy where I was and he was taking me everywhere. He jumped from fence to fence and he kept going the whole way. He's a small horse and when the ground is quick he really enjoys it - Conor Stone-Walsh, jockey.

quotes.race: Glenfarclas Crystal Cup Cross Country Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Keith [Donoghue, jockey] is unbelievable around here and I'm sure he's worth at least a stone on any horse. He loves it so much and gets a tune out of the horses, he gives them confidence and they jump brilliantly for him. Final Orders just really enjoyed it, he is so nimble and quick, and really took to it today. We will now look at the Festival - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

quotes.race: Prizm Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: Final Orders had a break since the jumps season and that was a nice pipe-opener for Galway. I thought he might be vulnerable over the trip but he did it well. He'll go for the Galway Plate - Gavin Cromwell, trainer

quotes.race: Paddy Power Cheltenham Fanzone Handicap Chase (Registered As The Sandyford Handicap Chase) (Grade B)
quotes.quote: Final Orders has massive scope, they are big fences around here but he just has so much scope. He loves it and is just thriving off it. He was off 140 there today and he's only 102 over hurdles so it's been a massive transformation - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

quotes.race: "Bet Through The Free Racing Post App" Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Final Orders has been a revelation since he went chasing. He's only a small horse but loves jumping. He needs every yard of three miles over hurdles and but his jumping is so good over fences that he can operate at this trip. The Dan Moore Handicap Chase could be a race we might look at for him - Gavin Cromwell, trainer

quotes.race: Start Your Free Trial Now At racingtv.com Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Final Orders is just so good and quick to jump. He wasn't in love with that ground, he might sneak into a good handicap off a low weight - Gacvin Cromwell, trainer

quotes.race: Follow Us On Social Media Rated Novice Chase
quotes.quote: I wanted to make use of Final Orders because he stays well. I left him bowl away, used his jumping and he jumped well on the whole - they're probably the biggest fences he's jumped but he has loads of scope. The ground looks worse than it is and I wouldn't call it soft, it's only yielding - Keith Donoghue, rider.

quotes.race: tote Guarantee On All Irish & UK Races Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Final Orders jumped really well for his second run over fences, exceptionally good. He's really suited to the summer tracks. It wasn't a strong race - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

quotes.race: Reddans Of Bettystown Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Final Orders tends to hit a flat spot in his races but he stuck at it very well here. We might look for something at Listowel or he could go back on the Flat - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He ran some good races last season, making the frame at Leopardstown and in the Ulster National. He was a good third over the banks at Punchestown in May and the plan is to go to the cross-country race at Cheltenham this month. He looks like he's taking to it well and could be a nice horse in that sphere. 04-11-25
He had a busy summer, so we let him off on a break and we'll probably bring him back in shortly. 13-11-24

runners.breeder: G Codre & Mrs A & K Kepa
runners.owner: DL Adams, JA Adams & G McPherson
runners.comment: A strong-staying winner at Cheltenham (near 3m4f, soft; 5lb higher today) in November
runners.spotlight: Negotiated these fences safely in the 2m5f Topham one year ago, albeit fading into 12th; a strong-staying display to win at Cheltenham (near 3m4f, soft; 5lb higher today) in November hints at untapped potential over long distances.

quotes.race: Oddschecker Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's feels unbelievable to have a winner here, it really does feel good. I'm thrilled for his owners, David and Jackie [Adams], who are massive supporters of the yard, as they've been dying to have a winner at Cheltenham for so long.Marble Sands had a bit of a question mark about the stamina, but we didn't need it. I was happy enough with how he was going and Kielan's given him a great ride. I'm delighted. We'll get him home and have a think about where to go next. We had been thinking about the Rehearsal Chase, but we'll see. Fair play to the team, they're doing a great job. We've had a slow start to the season but this makes it a lot better - David Killahena, joint trainer.

quotes.race: Colin Parker Memorial Intermediate Chase (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Aintree was the plan [last week's Old Roan] but this was the second option. The ground probably wasn't ideal as it was on the slower side of good and Marble Sands likes a sounder surface, but he's done it nicely. He had his two runs on the Flat to get him ready for it. This was the target and he won't be running on too soft ground and we'll have a look at what's about. The owners are very patient and if there's nothing for him the next few weeks they're happy to give him a break - David Killahena, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: M1 Agency Sidney Banks Memorial Novices' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We will go back and have a look but Marble Sands has done plenty this season to deserve a go at the Ballymore probably so fingers crossed. We will go back and speak to Graeme, David and Jackie )owners) and see what they want to do - Fergal O'Brien, trainer.

runners.comment: 8lb higher than for her big-race win at Newbury (3m2f) but her dominance is hard to forget
runners.spotlight: 10yo who is better than ever this term, including with a big handicap double in November in the Paddy Power Gold Cup at Cheltenham (2m4f, soft) and Coral Gold Cup at Newbury (3m2f, good to soft); dropping back to 2m4f, however, was probably not ideal when creditable third in mares' race at Cheltenham last month; 8lb higher than in the Newbury race but her dominance that day is hard to forget.

quotes.race: Mrs Paddy Power Mares' Chase (Registered As The Liberthine Mares' Chase) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Panic Attack has run a beautiful Grand National trial over two and a half miles. She jumped immaculately. She's a phenomenal jumper and I'm very proud of her. She couldn't quite win today on decent ground but that's sometimes how the cookie crumbles. We'd love to see her jump like that round Aintree wouldn't we. It would be some sight and the dream's alive. It's a possibility. It's not a probability, but it's a possibility - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Alder Demain & Akers Mares' Chase (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: On the numbers, Panic Attack ought to have done that, but it was fantastic she did. She's in the form of her life, and when you see her run like that, you think you've got to have a go at the Mares' Chase. The National is definitely the plan, but there are four weeks between them this year. You've got a chance to do both, but she's good enough to run in a Mares' Chase - Bryan Drew, owner.

quotes.race: Coral Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Panic Attack is brilliant. She's a credit to herself to do that fourteen days later [after Paddy Power win]. When they're getting on you have to race them when they're in form and she's clearly in the form of her life. Harry [Skelton, jockey] said to run her and it's worked out. Tristan [Durrell] gave her a phenomenal ride, he's the most improved rider I've ever had anything to do with in a short space of time - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Gold Cup Handicap Chase (In Memory Of Edward O'Grady) (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: To some degree these wins are satisfying, but I'm a paid professional and like Roy Keane says, 'I'm just doing my job'. When Panic Attack missed the Plate in March we made this race her target. We've been second in this race a couple of times and I remember with Spiritofthegames I've never been more disappointed after a race. His owner Norman Lake was one of our first supporters and he died a couple of years ago. I love running horses. I don't shy away from it. I'll run them if they're right and sometimes I get it wrong. She won't come back for December and we will most likely go to Doncaster in December for a mares' race over the Christmas period. I'd like to bring her back here for the Mares' Chase.? - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Catesby Estates PLC Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race) (NHMOPS Bonus Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought it was going to be easier than that. I thought this was tailormade for Panic Attack, she didn't finish as strongly as we hoped at Uttoxeter so we put the blinkers on and she travelled sweetly. Tom gave her a great ride, she was brave and battled up the run-in. She'll probably end up a three-miler and she goes on the better ground. She'll go over a fence too - David Pipe, trainer.

quotes.race: MansionBet Cheers To 2021 Mares' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We were hoping Panic Attack might do something like that at Cheltenham last time, but she made a mistake at the first and was beaten after that. Nothing came to light, so we freshened her up and this was the ideal race for her - it's possible she's better on a flat track. It was a confidence booster for the trainer, owner and horse and we bought her to be a graded performer, which is hopefully what she'll end up being. She's always worked nicely at home and we've always had high hopes for her, so it's nice to get her back on track but there are no plans, although she'll get further. - David Pipe, trainer

quotes.race: Alan Swinbank Mares' Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Panic Attack knew her job and it was a good performance. She took me there with ease and it took me a while to pull her up, which is always a good sign. We were getting a lot of weight but hopefully she's got a bright future - Paul Townend, rider.

stable_tour.quote: She has an entry in the Ryanair just in case, but I think we'll go for the Mares' Chase. She's had a phenomenal season and I can hardly believe where we've ended up with her, with three wins on the bounce and a rating of 147. She's a credit to herself, flying around at home, and can't wait to get her out again. She'll get 3lb from the favourite, Dinoblue, so I think she'll go very close. 17-02-96

A very smart mare who was a winner at Cheltenham last April when taking the Listed mares' handicap hurdle. She added to that at Huntingdon in November when a 13-length winner over fences. Last time out we sent her to Cheltenham with hopes of a good show in the Timeform Novices' Handicap Chase, but she ran the oddest of races, as having made a bad mistake down the far side when going well I thought Scu would pull her up but she got it together again and ran on well to take fourth. She seems in grand order and the plan is to head to Warwick with her next for a three-mile handicap chase. I think she wants that trip now, and if she does then it opens up many more options for us. We will see how she does in that race before looking any further ahead. 22-02-23

runners.comment: An excellent, rallying second at Haydock (extended 3m4f) but this is a much stronger race
runners.spotlight: One of several who are now in the veteran stage but also in the form of their lives; 7l winner at Haydock (extended 3m1f) in November and returned there with an excellent, rallying second in the Grand National Trial (extended 3m4f, again good to soft) in February; ridden last three starts by Toby McCain-Mitchell; back up 2lb and an interesting prospect for 4m2f but this is a much stronger race.

quotes.race: Amroth Bay Caravan Park "West Wales National" Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I think Top Of The Bill's class has shown there. His jumping has always been a big asset - Jordan Nailor, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Bella Coulson's 50th Birthday Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Last time was my fault. We weren't going to run Top Of The Bill but Nigel rang and said there were only three runners - I knew it was wrong. The ground was so bad that day, he's a great jumper but he wasn't getting any real advantage. I don't know whether we'll run him again this season but we want to win a good long-distance race with him next season. The owner would love to win the Welsh National and I told him we won't run over further than 3m this season so we keep that up our sleeve. He'll stay forever - Jim Old, trainer's representative.

runners.comment: 2nd and 1st over 3m2f/3m1f at Cheltenham Festivals and wasn't stopping; up 6lb in future
runners.spotlight: Fine over these fences in November; laboured from before three out when a well-beaten fifth to Haiti Couleurs in Irish National last April; that was in the mud, though, and his top efforts have been on good to soft; they include his neck second in the 3m2f Kim Muir at Cheltenham last March and, equipped with first-time cheekpieces after wind surgery, a 3m1f win from Jagwar at this year's Festival; able to race here off the same mark as last time (due to go up 6lb) and he wasn't stopping in either of those big races at Cheltenham; seriously considered.

quotes.race: Trustmarque Ultima Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Absolutely fantastic. Richie [McLernon] gave Johnnywho a great ride, he was in the right place all the time. It's just great to see it all work out. He just missed out on winning last year in the Kim Muir and it's great to come back and set that straight - A J O'Neill, joint-trainer.Johnnywho jumped and travelled well, the ground was dry enough I thought. We went a nice gallop and he was very unlucky here last year, he missed the last a bit and this time I just took aim at the last and it helped him. He just made one mistake - he was a bit slow at the third-last, but he was economical - he's not the biggest horse in the world. The cheekpieces, the tongue-tie and the wind op have definitely helped - Richie McLernon, jockey.

quotes.race: Fulke Walwyn Kim Muir Challenge Cup Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Chase (Spon By Thames Materials) (GBB)
quotes.quote: You're always disappointed not to win but Johnnywho ran very well. He pulled two shoes off, which might not have helped, but that's the way it goes - Jonjo O'Neill, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Lakes Estates Property Sales And Lettings Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Johnnywho warmed up to the task nicely. I think over two and a half [miles], he'd probably appreciate a bit slower ground. He'll hopefully have plenty of options - Jonjo O'Neill Jr, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: Beaumont Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Johnnywho is a nice horse, he's done everything right so far. The second and third are probably decent yardsticks and it was a nice way to go about it - Jonjo O'Neill Jr, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He ran a great race in defeat in the Kim Muir last season, before putting in another respectable run when finishing fifth in the Irish National. We were very happy with his comeback in the Grand Sefton. It was a positive performance over the National fences and we've put him in the Becher Chase off the back of that, where stepping up to three miles two furlongs would be in his favour. He's still got to improve if he's going to become a National horse, but he's certainly one for those long-distance handicap chases, and being able to jump those fences might be a useful string to his bow in time. 18-11-25

runners.comment: A doughty 3m2f win over these fences in the Becher but remote 10th in last year's National
runners.spotlight: Second at the 2024 Cheltenham Festival and started this season with two wins, notably by a short head from Mr Vango in the 3m2f Becher over these fences (wore cheekpieces second time); warmed up for this over hurdles after three months off; the Becher performance was doughty stuff but his only go at a marathon trip was last year's National in which he finished a remote tenth, always behind.

quotes.race: William Hill Half A Mill Becher Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Twig's run a blinder, Beau gave him a lovely ride and he jumped for fun. He just got lonely in front. He didn't get involved in the National, he plugged on and ran well, but you can't run like that in a National these days. He'll go up enough to get in again, so we'll see as I was thinking about the veterans final - Ben Pauling, trainer.

quotes.race: Oddschecker Veterans' Handicap Chase (Leg 8 Of The Stayers' Veterans' Chase Series)
quotes.quote: Twig is class; all last season was about trying to get him in the National, we got him in and he never really got into the race but finished beautifully to be tenth. We were delighted with him there and it's great to see him back. It was quite a hilarious race to watch; it changed complexion at least five times, but it's great. Hopefully, we can pop about in some of those sorts of races, maybe try him at the cross-country as well - Ben Pauling, trainer.

quotes.race: Ultima Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: This morning we were debating even running Twig, he wants better ground. But we thought we could go here and prep him for Aintree and he's run like that. I'm absolutely delighted - Beau Morgan, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: bet365 Summer Cup Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: When I originally trained Twig for his previous owners, who bred him, he just wasn't physically ready. I didn't think he was going to be a racehorse and that's why I sent him off into the point-to-point field, and he's just improved and improved - Ben Pauling, trainer.

quotes.race: Download The BetVictor App "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Twig is very consistent at a decent level and is possibly a better chaser than he is a hurdler, but we're trying to give Beau some good experience on a nice horse. The horse is going the right way and we might chuck him in something better towards the end of the season; he's a flat track, better-ground type - Ben Pauling, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's going to go for some veterans' chases and we'll possibly look at the Becher. I was delighted with his run in the National considering they went a million miles an hour from the start and he was struggling. He's not done with yet - he's got plenty to give in his own grade. 07-11-25

He joined us earlier this autumn and his three runs have been very encouraging. He finished second to Found On at Worcester first time out for us. We then went to Warwick this month where he got his head in front in a 3m novice handicap chase. He reverted to hurdles at Cheltenham on Friday and ran well to finish second to Shearer in a novice (well clear of the third). He would not want the ground too soft and I would anticipate a small break over the Christmas/New Year period. He will be an interesting runner when he returns in early spring. 26-10-22

runners.owner: Mrs M Roden & Mrs R Nolan
runners.comment: Outbattled over 3m1f in October; it's doubtful whether he's got what it takes for this
runners.spotlight: Gained all three chase wins in small-field novice events last April-June (one over 2m7f) but fell in three of his nine races since, including the last two; placed over 2m1f as a hurdler at three Cheltenham Festivals and runner-up in a 2m2f Cesarewitch on Flat, but he was outbattled over 3m1f at Cheltenham in October; it's doubtful whether he's got what it takes for this.

quotes.race: Fibrus Gallop At Gigabit Speeds Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Pied Piper was a bit sketchy throughout, but has lots of class and will come on mentally for that, so I'm very happy. He was entitled to go through it very easily, but hopefully his jumping will sharpen up a lot. I was full of horse, and getting his head in front will do his confidence the world of good - Danny Gilligan, jockey.

quotes.race: WKD Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Pied Piper idles in front and we didn't want to make the running, but he just cantered around like it was a piece of work. We'll probably wait till Christmas now - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Masterson Holdings Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was a nice way to start Pied Piper off and it was great. He's got a lot stronger since last season and I love the way he put his head down and galloped to the line. He's a nice horse. We're going to dream for another while but it's a hot division and he'll have to keep improving. We'll go to Down Royal now for the WKD [Hurdle] in two weeks time then onto Christmas from here. He'll be trained as a Champion Hurdle horse but it's a very hot division and he's going to have to improve but if you're not in, you can't win. As an individual he's way stronger. Even going round the ring he looked more like a chaser than a juvenile. With them juveniles you want that scope to keep improving. It's as strong as a division as there is out there. We can go to bed dreaming tonight anyway - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: JCB Triumph Trial Juvenile Hurdle (Grade 2) (Registered As The Finesse) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We thought we'd come over, have a feel and see where we are. We thought Pied Piper was a nice horse and if he was settled and behaved he's go close. We thought he was nice, but I was surprised a little bit by that. He jumped like a man. When he got close to one he learned how to settle. We bought him as a horse to mix on the Flat and over jumps, so he'll be a nice horse for those staying Flat races as well this year. He looks nice. They've (Fil Dor) got the same owners so we may try and split them up, we might run the two of them in the Triumph Hurdle. They're both in the Supreme Novices', I'd say this is the speedier horse than the other one and the Friday track might suit Fil Dor better. If one of them is going to go for the Supreme then it'd be this lad. There's always Aintree and plenty of other options. I wouldn't rule the Supreme out for him - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Join Tote.ie 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Pied Piper is a nice horse and I think there is an awful amount of improvement in him. I couldn't see him winning today and he hasn't even been away from home. He jumped well and probably travelled a bit too well early. He loved the ground and is one to look forward to. He's a big baby - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Kube - Leicester's Premier Event Hire Venue Handicap
quotes.quote: Pied Piper has been travelling a lot better in his races recently and been caught too far back off a slow pace the last twice. We went an even gallop considering the conditions and he kept at it well. He won in similar conditions at Newmarket at the back end of last year and has replicated the timing again this year - Rab Havlin, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's a hard horse to place, but he travelled brilliantly at Cheltenham on Saturday. He probably just found a strongly run 3m1f at Cheltenham a bit too far and the winner outstayed him. I was thrilled with how he ran, though, and it might open up a few doors for him. 26-10-25

runners.comment: 3 wins over conventional fences here; 3m1f win this January but this trip is a big unknown
runners.spotlight: Novice campaign last season went well, notably over the conventional fences here where he registered three handicap wins (2m/2m4f) and was second at this meeting (3m1f); resumed progress with a win at Haydock (3m1f) this January but badly hampered at the Cheltenham Festival; this trip is a big step into the unknown but he needs a second look.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Peter Marsh Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Imperial Saint has got form on the ground and I thought it would play to our advantage, and possibly disadvantage one of two of the others. I had no worries about the trip on that ground. I thought we'd potentially have more of a turn of foot than some of the opposition. I think there's still improvement to come. He's run four fantastic races at Aintree and I'd certainly be heading that way rather than Cheltenham. I think he'd definitely be worth an entry in the National - Johnson White, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Handicap Chase (Registered As The Freebooter Handicap Chase) (Premier Handicap) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Imperial Saint has been progressive all year, winning three here, and that was another step in the right direction. Hopefully there will be more to come again next season. He has to go left handed and he might start in the Paddy Power, as he's effective over two and a half - Philip Hobbs, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Betting Done Properly Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Imperial Saint definitely seems to enjoy it round here and it was the obvious race for him. We knew he'd get further and he's bounced back. We were a little bit disappointed at Newbury but maybe two miles round there was a bit too sharp for him. He's jumped, travelled and done it really well. He's going to go up in the handicap again and it's not going to be easy for him, but it's lovely to have a horse of his quality for our syndicate - Richard Johnson, syndicate manager.

quotes.race: Jason Salleh Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I didn't see what happened to the other horse, but I felt I was just getting back on top coming to the last. I was very comfortable the whole way and Imperial Saint jumped really well. He's had the point-to-point experience and he's a forward-going type, so we used that experience. He stays really well - Micheal Nolan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He ran okay the other day in the Old Roan at Aintree. They went off pretty quick and he just never really got into a rhythm. We've put it down to the fact it was his first run of the season and he might have just needed it. I think two and a half miles is his right trip, although he'll get further, as he proved at the Grand National meeting. We're looking at the December Gold Cup next. 20-11-25

He did well for us over hurdles last season, winning twice, at Ludlow and Ffos Llas, and finished in the first three in all of his five runs.  We were over the moon with his win at Aintree on Sunday in his first run over fences when he jumped very well throughout. He's owned by the Richard Johnson Racing Club and he gave his owners a great day. We think he'll get further in time but we'll stick with 2m with him at the moment and try and find another race for him in a couple of weeks' time. He's one we're looking forward to. 30-10-24

runners.comment: A fluent fourth in the Topham over these fences last April; ran creditably once at 3m4f
runners.spotlight: A fluent fourth in the 2m5f Topham over these fences was the first of three big runs in good handicaps last April-July; ran creditably in one (Sandown in April 2024) of his three attempts at 3m4f-3m5f and excuses might be made for his latest two outings (first cross-country, then the mud) but other candidates are more persuasive.

quotes.race: KilbegganRaces.com Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: I expected Amrite to win last time but I'm not convinced he loves real heavy ground. We waited for better ground after giving him a break. He looked really well today. The plan was to leave him in the field but we may look to a novice hurdle.

stable_tour.quote: He won the Midlands National at Kilbeggan and was fourth in the Galway Plate this summer. He was meant to go for the cross-country chase at Cheltenham this week but that has been cancelled, so he'll probably now go for the one in December. The aim is to run in the Cross Country Chase at the festival and then hopefully on to the Aintree Grand National. He's in great form. 11-11-25

He made a winning debut over fences at Fairyhouse this season from stablemate Secret She Keeps before making the frame in two Graded races. He has entries in the Brown Advisory Novices' Chase and the Kim Muir Handicap Chase and will go for one of those. 01-03-23

racecards.verdict: This is the day for MONTY'S STAR (nap) to shine, from Favori De Champdou, Grangeclare West and Stellar Story.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/1 I Am Maximus, 15/2 Panic Attack, 9/1 Grangeclare West, 10/1 Jagwar, 12/1 Johnnywho, 14/1 Monty's Star,  Iroko, 16/1 Captain Cody,  Haiti Couleurs,  Oscars Brother, 22/1 Gorgeous Tom, 25/1 Gerri Colombe,  Final Orders,  Quai De Bourbon, 28/1 Stellar Story,  Champ Kiely, 33/1 Perceval Legallois,  Spanish Harlem,  Lecky Watson,  Jordans, 40/1 Twig,  Favori De Champdou, 50/1 Imperial Saint,  Three Card Brag,  Marble Sands,  Banbridge,  Top Of The Bill,  Firefox,  High Class Hero, 66/1 The Real Whacker,  Answer To Kayf,  Mr Vango, 80/1 Amirite, 100/1 Beauport

racecards.race_name: Weatherbys nhstallions.co.uk Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (Grade 2) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Some improvement when runner-up at Taunton last month but looks out of his depth
runners.spotlight: A little more improvement when runner-up at Taunton (good) last month, on first outing after wind surgery; now fitted with a hood and a tongue-strap but he looks out of his depth in this grade.

runners.breeder: S Gesbert, J Lacouture & C Moreau
runners.comment: Followed wins at Newbury and Ascot with excellent third at Cheltenham; the one to beat
runners.spotlight: Assembling an impressive CV in bumpers, following all-the-way wins at Newbury (good to soft) and Ascot (soft) with an excellent third at the Cheltenham Festival (good) where he stuck to his task gamely after being headed over 1f out; that's the best form on offer and he's the one to beat.

quotes.race: King Edward VII Ascot Membership Open National Hunt Flat Race (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's brilliant. I ride Bass Hunter every day, and in my 18 years of training he's the best I've sat on at home, and I think he showed that to an extent. Cheltenham and Aintree will be considered, but for him to win at those sorts of tracks, he'll need to settle down - Chris Gordon, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: Before his first run for us at Newbury I said to  my wife Jenny that in the 18 years we've been training I've never sat on a horse like him. Then you get to the track and start curling up inside, but as it was he took the experience really well and bolted up. We're going to go to Ascot next for the Listed bumper just before Christmas and we'll see how we go. He looks like a special horse and feels like a beast. 23-11-25

At the moment he's the most exciting horse I've had in 18 years of training. I said to my wife two days before he ran at Newbury that I was very nervy and excited about running him. I was just hoping he was what he feels like at home. He's one of my rides and gives you an awesome feeling. I took him to one gallop in Lambourn, which is a tough gallop, and he scooted up there very easily. Anyway he backed it up at Newbury, which was great. He's by Authorized and they can be a bit buzzy but he took all the preliminaries very well, and when he got out on the racetrack he did it very comfortably. The plan is to keep him to bumpers at the moment - he's a big, gangly five-year-old and, if you're trying to make a career out of horses, there's no point in rushing them. He's a slow burner as far as I'm concerned this season, but we'll look at a Listed race at Ascot over Christmas and see if he can back up his Newbury run. If he does, we might aim at the stars after that, but we'll see. He's my trainer's pick. 01-12-25

runners.comment: Well beaten behind Bass Hunter at the Cheltenham Festival; difficult to recommend
runners.spotlight: Successful in his first two races (on good ground) but has come unstuck in a higher grade since, well beaten behind Bass Hunter at the Cheltenham Festival last month; difficult to recommend.

runners.comment: Workmanlike winner at Fakenham; remains unexposed but has plenty to find on the figures
runners.spotlight: Favourite in both his bumpers, taking second at Chepstow (good) before going one better at Fakenham (soft); remains open to improvement but has plenty to find on the figures and Harry Skelton rides stablemate Risky Obsession.

runners.comment: Hexham winner before fifth to Bass Hunter at Ascot; may not have reached ceiling just yet
runners.spotlight: Ridden by Heidi Palin on both outings for current yard, winning at Hexham (good to soft) before finishing a creditable fifth to Bass Hunter at Ascot (soft) when he faded late on; may not have reached his ceiling just yet; one of three contenders for Dan Skelton.

stable_tour.quote: A bumper winner for Tom Weston, he won his second bumper at Hexham under a tidy ride from Heidi Palin. He took off from turning in and I was very impressed with what I saw. He'll go to Ascot over Christmas for a Listed bumper. 10-11-25

runners.owner: Gummerson, Martin, W T Walsh & Williams
runners.comment: Two wins in Ireland but ran badly on British debut and this is even more competitive
runners.spotlight: Progressive in three outings in Ireland, winning under a penalty at Ballinrobe (soft) and subsequently changing hands for £100,000; however, he ran no sort of race in a Listed event at Newbury (heavy; 12-1) on his debut for current yard and this contest is even more competitive.

runners.comment: Wide-margin Sandown win has not worked out well; only midfield at Kempton next time
runners.spotlight: Overcame greenness to win at Sandown (good to soft) in November with plenty in hand, but that race has not worked out well and he could finish only midfield at Kempton next time; others appeal more.

quotes.race: Oddschecker Premium Tipsters Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We've always loved Le Roi Remi but he's still a shell so it'll be one or two more runs and put him away. "When he physically forms he's going to be a fair horse - Tom Ellis, trainer.

runners.breeder: G A E C De L'Ombre
runners.comment: Smart prospect; followed close second with a cosy win, both at Fairyhouse; major chance
runners.spotlight: Has a compelling profile, having gone close on debut at the 2025 Irish Grand National meeting (soft to heavy) before making a winning start for Willie Mullins back at Fairyhouse (heavy) in February; has to prove his effectiveness on less testing ground, but he looks a smart prospect and this owner/trainer combination were successful in this event 12 months ago.

runners.comment: Put firmly in place in Listed race at Cheltenham in November; needs a great leap forward
runners.spotlight: Runner-up at Newton Abbot and Lingfield but put firmly in his place in Listed race at Cheltenham in between; needs a great leap forward.

runners.comment: Dug deep when making all at Warwick on rules debut; unexposed and cannot be discounted
runners.spotlight: Changed hands for £72,000 after finishing third in an Irish point in November, and he dug deep when making all in bumper at Warwick (good to soft) five weeks ago on debut for current yard; Ben Jones jumps ship to ride Rices Pool, but this one is unexposed and cannot be discounted.

runners.comment: Steady improvement but he's 0-3 and this is his sternest assignment to date; tongue-tie on
runners.spotlight: Steady improvement with each of his three runs, beaten off only late on when second at Chepstow (soft) on debut for this yard last month; may have more in the tank but he's still a maiden and this is his sternest assignment to date; fitted with a tongue-strap for the first time.

runners.comment: 2-2 since joining Emma Lavelle; well up the pecking order on ratings; should have a say
runners.spotlight: 2-2 since joining Emma Lavelle; easily saw off eight rivals at Hereford (good ground) last month after a long layoff; well up the pecking order on ratings and should be in the thick of things again.

stable_tour.quote: He took time to wake up at home and then it clicked into place. He was really impressive when winning a bumper in a good time at Southwell and the second has won since. It wasn't the end of the world that he scoped dirty and couldn't run at Windsor as he doesn't want the ground too soft. He'll have one more run in a bumper, then we'll gear him up to go straight over hurdles next season. 29-01-25

runners.comment: Justified favouritism at Taunton with something in hand; improvement required but possible
runners.spotlight: His second in an Irish point has substance and he justified favouritism in bumper at Taunton (good to soft) with more in hand than the relatively short winning margin suggests; Ben Pauling runs four and stable jockey Ben Jones rides this one; improvement required but certainly possible.

runners.comment: Well beaten on heavy last time but previous wins were full of promise; interesting
runners.spotlight: Might have been unsuited by heavy ground when tailed off in Listed race at Newbury (100-30) in February, and he'd previously made an excellent impression when winning an Irish point (good to yielding) and a bumper at Warwick (good to soft); surely still has untapped potential and jockey bookings suggest he's the pick of Dan Skelton's three.

stable_tour.quote: An Irish point-to-point winner, he possibly didn't quite stay the three miles that day but travelled really well through the race and will win a bumper this year. I like him. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Significant improvement with each run, winning twice at Newcastle; each-way claims
runners.spotlight: Significant improvement with each of his three runs, winning at Newcastle in December and January (both good to soft); not hard pressed to pull 11l clear in a big field on latest; solid candidate with each-way claims.

runners.comment: Two good runs in defeat since his Hereford win but others have stronger claims
runners.spotlight: Made all at Hereford (good) in November and has run well in defeat twice since, albeit finishing behind Risky Obsession at Warwick and Merlin Allen at Kempton; others have stronger claims.

runners.comment: Off to the perfect start at Kelso in February; open to improvement but in much deeper here
runners.spotlight: Half-brother to the stable's smart 1m7f-2m4f hurdle/chase winner Notlongtillmay; off to the perfect start at Kelso (heavy; 7-1) in February, leading inside the final 1f and beating eight opponents; open to improvement but he's in much deeper here.

runners.comment: Favourite when making winning debut at Fontwell; could be anything but this is much harder
runners.spotlight: A fourth runner for the Ben Pauling yard, and like two of the others he's 1-1 under rules; well-backed favourite when comfortably accounting for four rivals at Fontwell (soft) four weeks ago; could be anything but this is a much stiffer task.

runners.comment: C&D winner of junior event before running well against older rivals at Kempton; respected
runners.spotlight: Beat his 11 opponents handsomely in junior event over C&D in November and ran well under a penalty against older rivals at Kempton (again good to soft) seven weeks ago; in good hands and remains open to progress.

quotes.race: William Hill "Junior" National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was exciting. Merlin Allen is a really nice horse - a proper three-mile chasing type - so I didn't think he'd win like that. This was his first day at school and we never run our horses again for six weeks. We'll see what we do - Jane Williams, trainer.

runners.comment: Only fourth at Warwick 16 days ago and has much more on his plate here
runners.spotlight: Made a winning start for a different yard at Catterick (soft) in January, but his limitations seem to have been exposed since; only fourth at Warwick 16 days ago and he has much more on his plate here.

racecards.verdict: Willie Mullins' Look Me is respected but the form pick is Cheltenham Festival third BASS HUNTER, who can regain the winning thread.
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/4 Bass Hunter, 7/2 Look Me, 9/1 The Perfect Poet, 10/1 One Knight, 11/1 Rices Pool, 12/1 Ronnie Russet,  Risky Obsession, 18/1 Smile John Boy, 20/1 Moments Away,  Le Roi Remi, 25/1 Thelastmanfrompenr,  Cooltobecareless, 28/1 Forthfactor, 33/1 Merry Away,  Governors Rock,  Chicker,  Merlin Allen, 66/1 Nightflyer,  Makingplansfor, 100/1 Barachiel

racecards.race_name: Tiptop Thunder Throne / EBF Junior 'National Hunt' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Record of 2-2 and he was impressive when scoring at Bangor 11 days ago; major player again
runners.spotlight: Made a good start when beating a clear second at Hereford (2m, good) in November and he built on that with an impressive win in similar conditions at Bangor 11 days ago; has a double penalty but he looks a useful prospect and is a major player again.

runners.comment: Promising third on Exeter debut (2m, good) last month and he should know more this time
runners.spotlight: First foal; dam placed in point/2m3f hurdle, half-sister to 3m chase winner Presenting Belle; weak 11-1 shot at Exeter (2m, good) last month but he rallied in the closing stages and did well to snatch third; that was an encouraging debut and he should improve for the experience.

runners.comment: Well-held ninth in two bumpers and he's best watched on hurdling debut
runners.spotlight: Big prices and he's finished a well-held ninth in two bumpers, with latest at Wincanton last month; best watched on hurdling debut.

runners.comment: Fell on debut and he unseated in the race won by Planters Punch at Bangor last time
runners.spotlight: In contention before falling heavily at penultimate flight on debut at Newbury (2m, good to soft) in February, and was unlucky to come to grief four out at Bangor (hampered and unseated rider) 11 days ago; seems to have ability but he was 20-1 last time and that was in the race Planters Punch won by 15l.

runners.comment: Made a low-key start over C&D last month and he needs to leave that form a long way behind
runners.spotlight: Half-sister to bumper/hurdle winner Hillfinch; 6-1 for a novice over C&D (good to soft) last month but she got outpaced before finishing a well-held fifth of seven; should know more this time but she needs to leave that initial form a long way behind.

runners.comment: Runner-up in both hurdle runs and latest was at Market Rasen last month; in the mix
runners.spotlight: Fell in her only point, but she's finished second in both hurdle runs; was no match for an odds-on rival at Market Rasen (2m, good to soft) last month but she gave it a decent shot from the front and was clear of the third; should go well again and she's in the mix.

runners.comment: Showed promise in first two runs but was pulled up in her final start for Dan Skelton
runners.spotlight: Built on her debut third at Warwick when runner-up behind a 4-11 shot at Ludlow (2m, good to soft) in December; that was promising but she was pulled up at Hereford in February and left Dan Skelton for £8,500 since; now returns after another break and has something to prove for new yard.

racecards.verdict: This can go to Nicky Henderson's unbeaten gelding PLANTERS PUNCH who was impressive at Bangor 11 days ago and looks a useful prospect.
racecards.betting_forecast: 1/2 Planters Punch, 5/1 Guts And Glory, 11/2 Longmoor, 10/1 Evening Tess, 14/1 Whitletts, 33/1 Mistral St Georges, 100/1 Look Don't Stare

racecards.race_name: Tiptop Duel Flush Mares' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Quite useful on the Flat and she won by 14l over hurdles at Kempton last time; respected
runners.spotlight: Quite a useful handicapper at up to 2m for William Haggas on the Flat; well-held fifth of 13 on hurdling debut at Hereford in February but she left that form well behind when justifying favouritism with a 14l win at Kempton (2m, good) last month; has a penalty but that was an impressive win and she could have a lot more to offer in this sphere; strongly respected.

quotes.race: Scots Association Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: She's still quite inexperienced. We thought the track might be a touch on the sharp side so were keen to get Molten Sea into her stride and her rhythm and she's done that and showed a good attitude in the later stages. She gets that trip well and I think going up in trip will be a big help. The second horse quickened by her while she was still a bit green and she's really gone through the line well and galloped out nicely afterwards - Callum Rodriguez, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

runners.owner: S T Racing Burnt Ends Partnership
runners.comment: Still early days but she's struggled in both hurdle runs and needs a transformation
runners.spotlight: Getaway mare who wasn't beaten far in her sole bumper but she's finished tailed off in two runs over hurdles (2m, good) since; with top yard and still unexposed but needs major improvement; stablemate of Jollie Dame.

runners.comment: Tailed off in both hurdle runs during the winter and can only be watched
runners.spotlight: Tailed off on Wetherby debut (2m3f, soft) in December and same story when dropped to 2m at Hereford (300-1) the following month.

runners.comment: Showed promise in both bumpers runs and she looks interesting now switched to hurdling
runners.spotlight: From a good family and she showed promise in two bumpers during the winter, more recently when third of ten at Huntingdon (2m, soft) in January; looks interesting now switched to hurdling and she needs watching in market.

runners.comment: Failed to beat a rival in sole bumper and was tailed off on hurdling debut last month
runners.spotlight: Failed to beat a rival in her sole bumper and was tailed off on hurdling debut at Stratford (2m, good) last month; one of two runners for the yard.

runners.comment: Form figures may look encouraging but she's been beaten 16l or more in her last four runs
runners.spotlight: Form figures may look encouraging but she's been beaten between 16l and 23l in her last four races, including two runs over hurdles (2m, good); still has potential but she has quite a lot to find here and others are preferred.

runners.comment: Struggled in both her bumpers and needs a transformation on this switch to hurdling
runners.spotlight: Half-sister to useful jumper Midnight It Is but she struggled in both her bumpers and needs a transformation on this switch to hurdling.

runners.comment: Well held in both bumpers and was a remote third on hurdling debut at Stratford
runners.spotlight: Well-held seventh in both bumpers and remote third at a big price on hurdling debut at Stratford (2m, good) last month; remains best watched for now.

runners.breeder: Haras De L'Hotellerie, Meridian Int, Seb
runners.comment: Won Grade 2 over C&D in December; tough task in Triumph latest and she sets standard here
runners.spotlight: Won smoothly on good to soft at Exeter and Chepstow (Grade 2) on first two hurdle starts; has found things tough at Cheltenham in last two runs but the first was behind Maestro Conti and latest was in the Triumph last month; sets the standard back in much calmer waters and she's a key player back at the scene of her last win.

quotes.race: Coral Finale Juvenile Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I can't believe the improvement Tenter Le Tout has made. She won a little race at Exeter last time, and her work at home since has been excellent. You have to have a crack at these races, and to win a Grade 2 so early in my career is very satisfying. I can't believe how well it's gone, and thanks to the team at home. You'd have to think about the Mares Novice or the Triumph at the festival after that. She's a staying type rather than a speed horse - Chester Williams, trainer.

racecards.verdict: The vote goes to TENTER LE TOUT who had a tough task in the Triumph last month and sets a clear standard back in much calmer waters.
racecards.betting_forecast: 8/11 Tenter Le Tout, 7/4 Molten Sea, 8/1 Jollie Dame, 9/1 Elated, 33/1 Burning Embers, 40/1 Nowherenearmilan, 66/1 Lakeview Lass, 100/1 Ciao Bellisima,  Footage Detectives

racecards.race_name: Tiptop Riders Restroom Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.owner: Jamie Rock, A Lewis, M Howell & Partner
runners.comment: Back on his winning chase mark and would be interesting if the ground is good
runners.spotlight: Needs to improve on his third-place finishes (modest/remote) this term but would be interesting if the ground is good; won off current mark at Market Rasen (2m3f) the last time he raced on such going.

quotes.race: Breed Buy And Race In Ireland Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a nice performance. It's been an up-and-down season for Ostend. He ran very well in a very competitive race behind Jagwar at Bangor in November and we thought he'd have a big season in front of him, but it's been one thing after another. We're pleased to see the horse we thought we had. Better ground has been a big thing for him and he had a tongue-tie on today. I'm really pleased with him and the way he jumped. I'm going to keep him busy because he's missed time ? we might look at Ayr in a couple of weeks - Alastair Ralph, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was third last time at Southwell on his first run since April. He had his wind done and had a few foot issues too. It was nice to see him jump well and Toby [McCain-Mitchell] gave him a lovely ride. He'll go to Bangor next at the end of the month. 12-02-26

runners.breeder: S C E A Haras Du Hoguenet
runners.comment: Had a solid record until pulled up in last two starts; turnaround is required
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 6yo who had a solid record until pulled up in last two starts, effectively failing to back up the sound effort he posted at Uttoxeter (2m, good) on chase/seasonal debut; turnaround is required.

stable_tour.quote: He was always going to be a better chaser than hurdler, and he jumped really nicely on his chase debut last month. He's a two-miler with loads of scope and we might look at something at the Coral Gold Cup meeting. He's off 119 and I'd be very surprised if he's not well above that come the end of the season. Physically, he's not the finished article and, if we mind him, he should be progressive. 23-11-25

A winning hurdler who has gone chasing this season. Unfortunately, he had to be pulled up at Newbury and needed some physio afterwards, but he'll be back in the spring, if not before. He's an athletic sort, the type to improve significantly. I'm expecting him to come to the fore next season. 07-01-26

runners.comment: Record of 2-2 over C&D includes a win off 1lb higher last April; respected
runners.spotlight: Record of 2-2 over C&D (good) includes a neck success off 1lb higher last April; failed to get home over 2m3f on soft ground here last month on return from a break; respected back down in trip.

runners.comment: This drop back in trip is likely to suit on second chase start; may progress
runners.spotlight: Good-ground hurdles scorer for previous yard; no match for the winner at Doncaster (2m3f) on chase/stable debut and return from absence but shaped as if this drop back in trip will suit; may progress.

runners.comment: Record of 5-12 for current yard; ran well on return from break last time
runners.spotlight: Record of 5-12 for current yard; campaigned mostly at longer trips but the way he shaped over a sharp 2m2f last time (ran well on return from break) suggests this galloping 2m may not be a problem; in the mix.

quotes.race: Position Payout At bet365 Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Pep Talking is absolutely amazing, he loves good ground. He bounced off it in front - Billy Aprahamian, trainer.

quotes.race: Join Southwell Golf Club Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Pep Talking has been a fantastic horse for us and has become a bit of a handicapper's nightmare as he only just does enough. He loves his jumping and hopefully has more to come next season. That will be him for this campaign - Billy Aprahamian, trainer.

runners.comment: Second in this race last year; has a record of 2-4 since wearing cheekpieces
runners.spotlight: Close second in this race last year; prevailed at Bangor (2m1f, good to soft) most recently, bouncing back from a poor effort and taking record since wearing cheekpieces to 2-4; likely player in the retained headgear.

racecards.verdict: The return to this C&D swings the vote in favour of BALLYBREEZE, ahead of last year's runner-up Dj Pete.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 Pep Talking, 7/2 Ballybreeze,  Dj Pete, 11/2 Koapey,  Whatyouwaitingfor, 13/2 Ostend

runners.comment: Failed to complete in last two starts but he needs checking in market back from a break
runners.spotlight: Failed to complete over hurdles (pulled up) and fences (fell) in his last two starts but this lightly raced 7yo is still unexposed in handicaps and he won twice during his novice hurdle campaign; returns after 157 days off and he needs checking in market back in this sphere.

quotes.race: Amazing Sri Lanka EBF "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The Kemble Brewery has always been a good horse. He won his two bumpers but he sliced into the back of his tendon when he ran at Cheltenham and was within millimetres of not being with us. His owners run a pub in Cheltenham and they've been very patient - Kim Bailey, trainer.

quotes.race: Cheltenham & South West Racing Club Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The Kemble Brewery has won a decent bumper today and that's all that matters. I think we'll probably go over hurdles, but we will see how takes this race. He is very unfazed by anything, and he has already schooled and jumped well - Kim Bailey, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a very nice horse and we've always liked him. He's so laid-back it's ridiculous- if he was a human he would drive you demented because he's got so much talent and ability, but you'd want to kick him before he actually did anything. We'll definitely take a step up in grade now and his form is working out very well. He's a very talented individual with plenty of speed. 19-11-24

He's the biggest talking horse we've trained in a long time as his form had worked out so well. We didn't know whether to go hurdling or chasing but, after schooling him at the back end of last season he was brilliant, so we thought we'd let him do what he's bred for. All his work and schooling through the spring had been very good, but he got a very bad fall at Chepstow in November. He didn't have a cut at his fences like we thought he would. He's had a break since then and you'll see him back over hurdles towards the end of January. You'd hope there's an awful lot of progress to come from him. 24-12-25

runners.comment: Made it 2-2 over hurdles with a win at Uttoxeter in December; up 11lb but she's respected
runners.spotlight: 1m2f/1m4f wins in France and then bought for 33,000euros; won on hurdling/stable debut at Leicester (1m7f, heavy) in December 2024 and she returned from a year off with a dominant display in a handicap at Uttoxeter (2m, soft); 11lb higher after another break but that was a big step forward last time and she's open to more progress; interesting contender.

stable_tour.quote: Her legs fly in every direction when she gallops and she's not the easiest to train, but she's going nicely at the moment and hopefully she gets the chance to show her ability. I don't know how strong the race she won at Leicester was, and she raced quite keenly, but so far so good and she's likely to start back over hurdles at some point next month. 22-10-25

runners.comment: Won on hurdling debut before a clear second under penalty; respected on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Irish point winner who scored on his hurdling/stable debut at Warwick last month and was a clear second under a penalty over C&D (good to soft) last week; looks on a workable mark now switched to a handicap and this unexposed 5yo is respected.

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late J P Carrington

runners.comment: Hit a personal best when winning at Taunton in January but he's struggled since
runners.spotlight: Six-time hurdle winner who hit a personal best when scoring at Taunton (2m3f, good to soft) in January but his form has slumped in two subsequent runs; has bit to prove again and this is competitive on this drop back in trip.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I wasn't sure after Celtic Art's his first run but he's definitely been getting better at home. He coped with this soft ground which is nice, he never runs well on quick ground so maybe this is the answer. He was very green at the backend of the race, so we'll need to get that sorted if he's going to progress. He's a lovely horse - Jeremy Scott, trainer.

quotes.race: Betway Handicap
quotes.quote: Celtic Mill has a big heart and needed it to get past Living Legend - Hollie Doyle, jockey.

quotes.race: Matchbook EBF Peter Willett Future Stayers' Maiden Stakes (Plus 10 Race) (Sire/Dam-Restricted Race)
quotes.quote: Celtic Art is a big baby and the ground was way too quick for him. He'll be a lovely horse next year - PJ McDonald, jockey.

runners.comment: Three chase wins in second half of last year; needs watching in market back over hurdles
runners.spotlight: Five-time hurdle winner who did well over fences in the second half of last year, with three wins and two seconds; returns after six months off but he's only 2lb higher than for his last success and he has won when fresh in the past; needs close look back over hurdles.

quotes.race: BetVictor Proud Sponsors Of Newbury Juvenile Hurdle (Nov' Championship Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We hoped In The Air would win and hopefully he'll improve for the run. He's still a baby, but his next run will be at Aintree in the Grade 1 juvenile. I shouldn't think he'd want extremes of ground and I think he can improve a bit. He's a horse for the future, a bit like Porticello, although he wouldn't be as big as him and I don't think he's quite up to that level yet. Gary Moore, trainer

stable_tour.quote: We got him from Adam West this summer and he's started the campaign very well. He won easily on his first run for us at Southwell and got put up 11lb. He won with a 7lb penalty the following week at Exeter and might run again over the weekend. I'm looking forward to seeing what we achieve with him in the future. 22-10-24

Another recent purchase out of Nicky Henderson's from the Olly Harris dispersal. He's a five-time winner and might be a bit of fun and one we aim at the Summer Plate. He's got bits of good form and was a cheap purchase at £15,000 - he might have slipped through the radar. 19-02-25

runners.comment: Flopped in hat-trick bid at Newbury and has bit to prove for new trainer; new blinkers
runners.spotlight: Won back-to-back handicaps at Taunton (2m3f, good) and Warwick (2m, heavy) during the winter but he flopped at Newbury in final run for Stuart Kittow; new headgear is now tried and he has a bit to prove on first run for new trainer.

quotes.race: Oddschecker Cheltenham Free Bets Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Cornish Storm is a straightforward horse who enjoyed it out front and will jump a fence one day - Ben Jones, jockey.

runners.comment: Four chase wins in France but this looks a tough assignment on his British debut
runners.spotlight: Four chase wins in France including three in a row at around 2m2f (soft/heavy) last autumn; unexposed over hurdles but he's hard to weigh up from a handicapping point of view and this looks a tough assignment on his British debut; blinkers are removed and market should guide after 164 days off.

runners.comment: On workable mark but he's finished down the field in last two starts; others preferred
