runners.spotlight: Won a C&D novice (soft) in November and was a good second in a Newbury handicap (2m, good to soft) in January; looks interesting on that form but he's taken backward steps on his last two starts and is now 1-8 over hurdles.

stable_tour.quote: He was third in a good race at Chepstow before he unseated at Fontwell last time. It was unfortunate but it happened too far from home to know if he was going to run well at the time. He could still be a nice horse this season and we'll keep him at two miles for now. He goes to Chepstow on Friday. 20-11-25

runners.comment: Triple C&D winner but he's struggled in last two starts and overall record is 4-48
runners.spotlight: All three hurdle wins have come over C&D but he failed to beat a rival here in December and was tailed off again at Ffos Las in January; overall record is now 4-48 and others are preferred.

racecards.verdict: Top of the list is AUTHODIDACTE (nap) who is 2-2 over hurdles and put in a dominant display at Uttoxeter on her comeback in December.
racecards.betting_forecast: 2/1 Cosmic Connection, 4/1 Authodidacte, 6/1 The Kemble Brewery,  Doctors Hill, 7/1 Lacrima, 8/1 In The Air, 14/1 Celtic Art, 16/1 Cornish Storm,  Zambezi Fix

racecards.race_name: Tiptop Lavish Latrine Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.breeder: Mrs P Souverain & Mr A De Boisbrunet
runners.owner: L Cross, S Cross & J Fitzpatrick

prev_owners.owner: T Acott, L Cross, S Cross

runners.comment: Won at Warwick in December but he's failed to complete in three runs since; risks attached
runners.spotlight: Scored at Warwick (3m, good to soft) in December but he's failed to complete in three subsequent runs and didn't get very far at Stratford (unseated at first) two weeks ago; only 2lb lower than for his last success but he comes with risks attached.

quotes.race: Betfred 'Hot Shots' Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Chasing was always going to be his game. He jumped brilliantly, especially out of that ground. Happy And Fine is going the right way - the question is whether we keep nudging our way up or go and have a pop at something - Alex Hales, trainer.

quotes.race: Summer Plate Day 22nd July 2023 Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We liked Happy And Fine last year but he lost his way a bit as he was a bit weak. He had a really good summer. He's quite a nice horse in this grade and he wants a fence in time - Alex Hales, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a lovely horse bought for us by Charlie Mann out of France. His first run was a very encouraging one when third to Bombs Away at Sandown in November, and I fancied him to open his account back at the Esher track earlier this month, but he ran very flat and hung. He came back lame, but he is fine now and ran a good race at Catterick on Tuesday, when third. He has a rating of 108 which is very workable, and I am keen to get a win into him as he has new owners, and it would be great for them. 30-12-21

runners.comment: Had excuse over 3m7f last time and has claims if he can bounce back; new headgear
runners.spotlight: Veteran who is hard to predict but he may have had stamina issues when pulled up in the Devon National (3m7f) and he ran well over an inadequate 2m3f (good to soft) on his penultimate run; this trip is a much better fit and he's well handicapped on old form; not ruled out in new headgear.

quotes.race: Matchbook Better Way To Bet Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: It was quite windy out there so it's a tough ask to stay in front the whole way. Jepeck did get in front of us but I felt I could have one more go at him at the back of the last, I felt I had something left and I'm glad we got there. Sizable Sam did it well by the time he got to the line. He races like a three miler, very relaxed and straightforward. He jumped well on the whole, bar one - Nick Scholfield, jockey.

quotes.race: Follow @MansionBet On Twitter Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Sizable Sam had to work hard for that. He was very green and it was the hardest race he's had - he did very well to get back. He was bought as a three-mile chaser and that's exactly what he is. We'll see how he comes out of the race and go from there, it might be of interest to go for a Graded hurdle or something like that. It's all learning with him, front-running isn't the ideal way to run him but in order to win a race you've got to make use of his stride. Hopefully in a slightly better race they'd go more of a gallop and he'd learn more sitting in. We don't want to spoil him for next year. I haven't looked beyond this but, having had a hard race, he won't run until February. If we thought he'd improved we could aim for one of the Spring festivals, I think the Sefton would suit him - Jeremy Scott, trainer.

quotes.race: Watch On Racing TV Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I think Sizeable Sam has got ability. He struggled with the ground and Matt [Griffths] said he felt better the last day because of the going. I don't think we rode him positively enough, he's not a speed horse. He jumped well. We'll see what's around in January, hopefully on better ground, probably something like a Class 3. This season we're very much looking after him with the future in mind - Jeremy Scott, trainer.

runners.comment: Two wins at Hereford late last year but he's struggled in last two runs; cheekpieces added
runners.spotlight: Acts on good and soft ground; won two chase handicaps at Hereford (3m1f) late in 2025 but he's struggled in his last two starts; still has potential in this sphere but he needs to get back on track with cheekpieces added.

stable_tour.quote: He switched from hurdling to chasing this season and the results were almost instantaneous, although he returned with cuts on his legs on his chasing debut. However, he won his next two, the second one at Hereford by ten lengths. This is a big horse, far from the finished article, and he'll be a great staying chaser in time. 07-01-26

runners.breeder: G F A Du Pont Rouge
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Brian Davies
runners.comment: In-form 9yo who should go well again and it would be a positive if the ground dries out
runners.spotlight: Triple hurdle winner who made the breakthrough over fences in a Ludlow handicap (2m4f, good to firm) in October; that was a four-runner race but he's been placed in three runs since including over 3m at Taunton; should go well again and it would be a positive if the ground dries out.

quotes.race: Great Outdoors INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: He has settled into the routine very well and his work had been very good at home. He won a point-to-point at Fairyhouse and for this time of the year he is a bit better than them. I imagine he will go on a bit softer ground - rider Jamie Codd.

runners.comment: 11yo who is hard to predict and he's lost his way again in last two starts; down the list
runners.spotlight: 11yo who was runner-up at Warwick (3m, good to soft) on New Year's Eve but he's had a heavy defeat and a fall in two subsequent runs; new headgear is now tried but he's hard to predict and has not won since October 2024; down the list.

runners.comment: Won this race by 12l last year and was a good fourth at Newbury last month; respected
runners.spotlight: Record of 5-16 over fences and he defied today's mark with a 12l win in this race (good) last year; has not seen much action since but he returned after four months off with a creditable fourth at Newbury (2m6f, good to soft) last month; should benefit from that run and he's an interesting contender back at this track.

quotes.race: BetVictor A Run For Your Money At Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The keys to The Boola Boss are a flat track and good ground and, like Becky [Curtis, trainer] said, two [miles] six [furlongs] is probably his perfect trip. Three miles probably stretches him and two and a half [miles] is probably a bit too short so ideal conditions really - Sean Bowen, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports.

quotes.race: William Hill Extra Place Races Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: The Boola Boss has been going really well at home and he's just come into himself. He did it nicely and I'm very pleased. He's quite versatile on ground but I'm not sure I'll keep him going now because he's a big horse and he might not want to be summer racing. He may go out on his break next week  - Rebecca Curtis, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a stable favourite who has won five chases, including two at Worcester. He's never fallen in all the years he's been here. He's had a break since December and is getting ready for some veterans' events. There's one at Doncaster on Friday. 25-02-26

runners.comment: Made it 3-8 over fences when completing a hat-trick on comeback at Wincanton; key player
runners.spotlight: Won his final two starts last season and he made it 3-8 over fences when completing a hat-trick over 3m1f at Wincanton (the vet reported he was treated for post-race ataxia) on his comeback in February; up another 4lb but he seems versatile ground-wise and is open to more progress as a staying chaser; key player.

runners.comment: Lightly raced 6yo but he needs a transformation at this new trip on chase debut
runners.spotlight: Showed promise in novice hurdles but he's been well held in three handicaps in that sphere; still has low-mileage but this is his first attempt beyond 2m4f and he needs a transformation on chase debut.

stable_tour.quote: He was first of the unraced horses in what looked a good Chepstow bumper. We'll find him something similar and make him into the best horse he can be long term. 12-11-24

racecards.verdict: Camulus is strongly respected in his bid for a four-timer but slight preference is for last year's winner THE BOOLA BOSS.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Camulus, 11/4 The Boola Boss, 5/1 Gris Majeur, 7/1 Sizable Sam, 8/1 The Newest One, 10/1 Buckna, 12/1 Happy And Fine,  Choice Runner

racecards.race_name: Tiptop Sensational Shower Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: By no means disgraced last time and the opposition have their own questions to answer
runners.spotlight: Suffered her first reverse under rules when pulled up on reappearance (2m7f; reportedly made a respiratory noise); off three months (wind surgery) before Market Rasen (extended 2m4f, soft) in February when by no means disgraced in form terms, although that 10l ninth of 12 shows that improvement is needed if others give their running; dropped 2lb, 7lb claimer is recruited and the opposition have their own questions to answer.

stable_tour.quote: She's a big mare who's going over fences. She looks all over a chaser and has jumped well in a couple of schooling sessions. She won on bottomless ground at Lingfield last season on pure ability, rather than because she wants those conditions, and she probably wants good to soft or soft. 05-11-25

runners.comment: Won at Doncaster (2m3f, soft); ran badly at Ludlow (3m but not because of the trip) latest
runners.spotlight: Chasing didn't go to plan before she won readily when back over hurdles at Doncaster (2m3f, soft) in February; ran badly, however, at Ludlow (3m but not because of the trip) three weeks later; ran respectably at 3m on final start last term.

runners.owner: M Songer, C Bailey & M Dodd
runners.comment: Staying-on 2nd on handicap debut at Lingfield (2m7f, soft); flop at Newbury (3m1f, soft)
runners.spotlight: Staying-on second on handicap debut at Lingfield (2m7f, soft) in December; flopped in five-runner race at Newbury (3m1f, soft) two months later but had first-time cheekpieces which are now absent; seriously considered on the Lingfield effort but return to better ground asks a question.

runners.comment: Handicap debut under 7lb claimer at Newbury (3m1f, soft; favourite) was disappointing
runners.spotlight: Point and bumper winner; four runs over hurdles, best when third at Wincanton (extended 2m5f, heavy) in January; handicap debut under 7lb claimer at Newbury (3m1f, soft; favourite) last time was disappointing but these are early days and she could bounce back.

runners.comment: Well beaten when upped to an extended 2m3f three weeks ago; goes even further today
runners.spotlight: Won a 2m handicap in 2024 for Henry de Bromhead; back to form in November on first run for this yard and not discredited next time but, with tongue-tie fitted after wind surgery, she pulled up lame on chase debut in January and was well beaten when upped to an extended 2m3f three weeks ago; this trip is a big step into unknown territory.

runners.comment: Back from chasing but with stamina unproven and she is now 0-16 under rules
runners.spotlight: Sent chasing on last four starts, with two minor honours over the extended 2m3f at Ffos Las; however, moving up to this trip here with cheekpieces restored (she tried them twice in 2020) on latest outing did not work out and she is now 0-16 under rules.

racecards.verdict: This is a headscratcher because all of the runners were well beaten last time out. The tentative choice is PRESENTING DOY.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Presenting Doy,  Katie's Melody, 11/4 Harmony Heights, 4/1 I Am The Moon, 10/1 Benignitas, 25/1 Love Me

runners.breeder: S A S Rouge Et Gris Racing & S C E A D
runners.comment: Two good efforts in handicaps including a close fourth over C&D; respected
runners.spotlight: Unexposed 5yo who was a good second on handicap debut at Uttoxeter (2m4f, soft) in January and he backed that up with a close fourth over C&D the following month; up another 2lb but he travelled strongly for a long way last time and is open to more progress; strongly respected with tongue-tie added.

runners.comment: Didn't fire at Sedgefield but has claims if he can get back near best; cheekpieces added
runners.spotlight: 0-9 over hurdles but he went close in a Southwell handicap (2m, good to soft) in December; was never really travelling when a well-held third at Sedgefield (2m4f, good) last month but that was after a short break and cheekpieces are now added; dangerous if he can get back near best.

runners.comment: Unexposed 6yo and he needs a close look in the market on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Placed in both bumpers and he showed some promise in the first two of his three hurdle runs (2m4f/2m) during the winter; returns after a short break and he needs a close look in the market on handicap debut.

stable_tour.quote: He finished second in a bumper at Chepstow, then went to Fontwell and things just didn't click for him that day. It took him a while to get over that, but he's back going well and showed with that good first run that he's got the ability. He's a big horse who'll probably go straight hurdling - he knows how to gallop and jump. 12-11-25

runners.owner: Ben Pauling Racing & Dr Suzannah Turk
runners.comment: Pulled up on handicap debut at Huntingdon and he needs a transformation back up in trip
runners.spotlight: Tailed off in his two competed starts in novice events and was pulled up on handicap debut at Huntingdon (2m, soft; 12-1) in February; still early days but he needs a transformation back up in trip.

runners.comment: Has won over C&D in two of her last three runs and she remains feasibly treated; respected
runners.spotlight: 9yo who is exposed over hurdles but she scored over C&D (soft/good to soft) in two of her last three starts; 3lb higher than for her last win two weeks ago but she remains feasibly treated and should get a decent tow into this race; shortlisted.

runners.comment: Has lost his way since his win at Leicester and he needs a major revival in new headgear
runners.spotlight: Won by a nose at Leicester in November (1m7f, soft) but she's struggled in three subsequent runs and was pulled up at Ffos Las last month; had another wind operation since but she needs a major revival back up in trip; hood and tongue-tie are removed and cheekpieces are now tried.

runners.comment: Low-mileage 6yo but he's untried at this trip and others are more convincing
runners.spotlight: Promising second in a Huntingdon handicap (2m, heavy) in February but he failed to back that up at Stratford (2m, good) last month; still has low mileage but he's untried at this trip and others are more convincing.

runners.breeder: A J & Mrs J Ward &  G Wragg
runners.comment: Has achieved very little under rules and he fell on handicap debut last month; opposable
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in a point but has achieved very little over hurdles (2m-2m3f) and he fell on handicap debut at Ludlow (2m5f, good; 100-1) last month; can only be watched until he shows some promising signs.

runners.comment: 0-9 over hurdles and well held in handicaps in his last four runs; cheekpieces added
runners.spotlight: Flat winner but he's 0-9 over hurdles and has been beaten 17l or more in four handicaps (2m1f-3m) since November; mark continues to fall but he needs the cheekpieces to make a difference on this drop back in trip.

quotes.race: Conference & Banqueting Facilities At Limerick Racecourse Handicap
quotes.quote: Rapid Mission was very free in the blinkers. I had to get him to switch off but the pace was on racing down the back straight and I sneaked into it. He won snug at the line - Declan McDonogh, rider.

runners.comment: Non-runner
runners.spotlight: Non-runner.

runners.breeder: Earl De Cordelles & Mr Robert Brard
runners.comment: Inconsistent ten-race maiden and he's best watched back from a year off
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent ten-race maiden who was well held in a Huntingdon handicap (2m4f, good) last April and has been on the sidelines since; best watched back from a year off.

runners.comment: Has struggled in all five runs including when pulled up on handicap debut at Warwick
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 6yo but he struggled in his qualifying runs and was pulled up at another big price on handicap debut at Warwick (2m3f, good to soft) in January.

runners.comment: No form claims after eight hurdle races and it's not hard to look elsewhere
runners.spotlight: No form claims after eight hurdle races, five in handicaps; tongue tied on latest and tried cheekpieces before that; 1lb out of the weights

runners.comment: 19-race maiden and he's struggled in his last five starts; 4lb out of the weights
runners.spotlight: 21-race maiden; big prices and well beaten in four starts since November including in a hurdle handicap at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) last month; out of the weights again and can only be watched.

racecards.verdict: Top of the list is the unexposed 5yo THORGATH who has gone close in both his handicaps including over C&D last time.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Thorgath, 11/4 Inion Tiogair, 3/1 Hillwalk, 5/1 Shan't Wait, 10/1 Bushstreet Bowman,  Peace In The Park, 20/1 Rapid Mission, 25/1 D'Gesteevo, 33/1 Sophie Power,  Saint Vic, 66/1 Triple Haych, 100/1 Ifan Full Pelt,  Raindance Queen

racecards.race_name: QuinnBet Conditional Jockeys' Training Series Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Part Of The Racing Excellence)

runners.comment: Lightly raced; may still do better on her yard/handicap debut here after 13 months off
runners.spotlight: Hurdling debut fourth at Market Rasen in November 2024 but she failed to build on it in two subsequent runs for Dr Richard Newland and Jamie Insole; remains very lightly raced so she may still do better on her yard/handicap debut after 13 months off.

runners.owner: Ursa Major Racing, S Knowles & Partners
runners.comment: Best effort when second here 11 days ago; this longer trip promises to suit now h'capping
runners.spotlight: A two-time points scorer who posted easily her best effort in this sphere when second of eight in 2m4f novice here 11 days ago; this longer trip promises to suit now going handicapping.

runners.comment: Good third at Sedgefield 23 days ago; bold showing is on the cards off the same mark here
runners.spotlight: On a losing sequence but she is holding her form well, third of seven in 3m3f Sedgefield handicap hurdle 23 days ago; a bold showing is on the cards off the same mark.

quotes.race: Racingtv.com Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Go North Lady Buttons Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: It's Maisy is a typical of one of the trainer's horses, they jump and they gallop - Nick Scholfield, rider.

runners.comment: Scored over fences at Market Rasen in November but has failed to go on; reverts to hurdles
runners.spotlight: Scored over fences at Market Rasen (3m) in November but she's failed to go on and underwent breathing surgery (also fitted with cheekpieces) before coming in a well-held third of five at Exeter (3m) 20 days ago; reverts to hurdles with plenty to prove.

quotes.race: Mick And Linda Jackson Mares' Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
quotes.quote: Seasmoke showed today she had a gutsy attitude and the family has multiple winners because of that. James [Bowen, jockey] gave her a well judged ride and he said if he rode her again then he'd go that little bit quicker - Billy Aprahamian, trainer.

runners.owner: M Waterton, D Amos, G Rutherford
runners.comment: Seems of very limited ability and she was pulled up in Hexham novice hurdle 17 days ago
runners.spotlight: Seems of very limited ability and she was pulled up in 2m4f Hexham novice hurdle 17 days ago; handicap debutante.

racecards.verdict: This looks an excellent opportunity for IT'S MAISY (nap) to gain a deserved first success of the current campaign.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/4 It's Maisy, 3/1 Royal Maggs, 100/30 Pepite De Saphir, 9/2 Seasmoke, 66/1 Strathcatcha

racecards.race_name: QuinnBet Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Chase

runners.comment: Respectable on recent rules chase debut at Wetherby (3m; fourth); 2lb lower; back in trip.
runners.spotlight: Failed to win over hurdles (0-7), going closest when runner-up in a Hexham maiden (2m4f) 13 months ago; respectable on recent chase debut at Wetherby (3m; fourth of nine); 2lb lower, and back in trip with cheekpieces retained.

runners.comment: Shaped well initially over fences, prior to Musselburgh blip; forecast conditions to suit.
runners.spotlight: Made all over hurdles at Bangor (2m4f, good) last September; shaped well initially over fences, only run down late at Worcester (2m4f; 7-2) prior to finishing third at Market Rasen; disappointing over 2m at Musselburgh (85-40 favourite) when last seen; forecast conditions should suit.

runners.owner: M Blades, S Morrell, K Hathaway
runners.comment: Recent Wetherby efforts were modest but C&D form figures 212; competitively handicapped.
runners.spotlight: Usually goes well over C&D - form figures 212 - that win gained from a 2lb higher mark (favourite) over a year ago; recent Wetherby efforts were not so good but there was plenty to admire about the manner in which he rallied behind Always A Reason over C&D (good to soft) in January.

quotes.race: William Hill Offers Top Price Guarantees Novices' Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: We always thought Empty Nest was quite a decent horse and he never quite put it together on the track. He's been frustrating and we thought about retirement but we took him to Malton and he worked really well. I'm not sure what's made the difference but something has definitely worked - Mark Walford, trainer.

prev_owners.owner: Mrs D Walton & D G Pryde

runners.comment: C&D winner (from 2lb lower) three starts back; Danny McMenanmin returns to the saddle.
runners.spotlight: Made it 12th-time lucky over fences when scoring over C&D (good to soft; from 2lb lower) three starts back; excuses since - fell, and then out of depth in a valuable Class 2 Series Final at Carlisle; could bounce back with Danny McMenamin returning to the saddle.

quotes.race: Mini Golf At High Gosforth Park Novices' Handicap Chase (Go North Forgive 'N Forget Series Qual')
quotes.quote: The ground was in Hawkseye View's favour and he was clever. It's taken a little bit to figure him out but he was good today and that's the first race we've won with him so it's good to get his head in front - Joel Parkinson, joint-trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: He's not the easiest to win with. He's very ground dependent, he's got to have it good. He's a good jumper but doesn't have the most scope. He's been placed a few times and has bumped into some nice horses. I'm sure we'll win with him but the race has got to fall right. 28-01-26

runners.comment: Won at Doncaster (2m3f; from 9lb lower) in February; likely to face competition for lead.
runners.spotlight: Seized the initiative, already having the race in safe keeping when left clear at the second last, at Doncaster (2m3f, good; from 9lb lower) in February; well beaten at Southwell subsequently and likely to face competition for the lead here; close to a career best required.

stable_tour.quote: He's been amazing because he's had two tendon injuries and he bled a couple of seasons ago, but he's come back better than ever. His body is coping really well now and he was impressive when winning at Doncaster last month. He wants decent ground and can definitely win again this spring. 13-03-26

runners.comment: Signs of ability over hurdles in 2022; has failed to complete in two attempts over fences.
runners.spotlight: Signs of ability over hurdles for Rebecca Menzies in 2022; lightly raced since, failing to complete in two attempts over fences (PF) for this trainer; monitor only for time being.

runners.owner: J L And Mrs H R Gledson
runners.comment: 0-19; bit better, a never-nearer fourth over C&D (good to soft; 28-1) latest; 3lb wrong.
runners.spotlight: 0-19; form figures PPP4 since November are hardly a ringing endorsement; problematic at the start, but did shape a bit better when a never-nearer fourth to Ceowulf over C&D (good to soft; 28-1) 11 days ago; 3lb out of weights; others preferred.

racecards.verdict: Bravethewaves may offer competition for the lead but C&D regular EMPTY NEST gets the vote. The Clonmel Kid is second choice.
racecards.betting_forecast: 15/8 Empty Nest, 11/4 Hawkseye View, 4/1 The Clonmel Kid, 5/1 Bravethewaves, 10/1 Kingston Rock, 20/1 Quickasican

racecards.race_name: John Hanley Forever Lucky Number 7 Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Winless since May 2024 and he's not proving easy to catch right this season
runners.spotlight: Winless since May 2024 and he's not proving easy to catch right this season, a below-par sixth in 2m3f Carlisle handicap hurdle 20 days ago.

runners.comment: Runner-up on at Catterick but pulled up at Musselburgh last time; has something to prove
runners.spotlight: A fairly useful debut bumper winner; matched that form in this sphere when runner-up on his handicap debut at Catterick (2m3f) in January but he was pulled up at Musselburgh (2m4f) last time; has something to prove.

runners.comment: Failed to fire this term and beat just two at Sedgefield ten days ago; others appeal more
runners.spotlight: Scored twice over hurdles (at about 2m4f) in 2024-25 but has failed to fire this term and beat just two in 2m4f Sedgefield handicap hurdle ten days ago; others appeal more.

runners.comment: C&D winner; back from seven months off with very good C&D third latest; can go very well
runners.spotlight: Scored at Market Rasen (on good ground) last June and she returned from a seven-month absence with a very good third of nine over C&D 11 days ago; this C&D winner can go very well off an unchanged mark.

quotes.race: Racing TV Go North Lady Buttons Mares' Hurdle Series Final (A Handicap Hurdle) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We've not overworked Lone Star because she's been a bit keen and she's getting better all the time. I don't know where the end of it is. I don't know how good she might be - Phil Kirby, trainer.

quotes.race: quinnbet.com Mares' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Lone Star was quite keen and gassy when we got her and we tried a few different ways of riding her. She's only just learnt to be a racehorse and see her races out - Joe Williamson, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Pulled up on at Bangor three weeks ago; he could still do better for good yard
runners.spotlight: Twice a runner-up in bumpers; failed to build on earlier promise in this sphere when pulled up on his handicap debut at Bangor (2m4f) three weeks ago; cheekpieces are retained and he could still do better for good yard.

runners.comment: Debut bumper second for Stuart Crawford but he's failed to kick on for his current yard
runners.spotlight: Debut bumper second (for Stuart Crawford) in Ireland but he's failed to kick on for current yard in four runs over hurdles, undergoing wind surgery before falling two out (well held) in 2m4f Ayr handicap last month.

runners.comment: In good form until sixth at Musselburgh 22 days ago; can bounce back off a slipping mark
runners.spotlight: On a losing sequence but in good form for her current yard until coming in a never-dangerous sixth in 2m4f Musselburgh handicap 22 days ago; she can bounce back off a slipping mark.

runners.comment: Back on the up with success at Carlisle latest; this course winner is a likely player
runners.spotlight: Got back on the up with a third success of the season in 2m1f handicap at Carlisle 20 days ago; up another 4lb but this course winner is a likely player once more for his in-form yard.

quotes.race: Ocean Outdoor Big Screen Classified Stakes
quotes.quote: National Question might have limited ability, but really tries hard - Adam Nicol, trainer.

runners.comment: Winning pointer; brought along steadily and capable of better up in trip for h'cap debut
runners.spotlight: A winning Irish pointer; has been brought along steadily in this sphere, coming in a never-dangerous seventh in 2m1f novice here four weeks ago; goes up in trip now handicapping and is capable of better.

runners.comment: Still to win but good Wetherby second latest; can make presence felt back up in trip
runners.spotlight: Still to register a victory but he comes here after a good second of eight in 2m Wetherby handicap hurdle 44 days ago; he can make his presence felt again reverted to a longer trip.

runners.owner: 8 Amigos, J Grindal, W Hamilton, J Burns
runners.comment: Yet to offer much in his four runs over hurdles; cheekpieces go on for his handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Yet to offer much in his four runs over hurdles, pulled up in C&D novice in January; cheekpieces go on for his handicap debut after a break.

runners.comment: Best run this term (in cheekpieces) when Sedgefield fourth latest; needs to build on it
runners.spotlight: A point bumper winner in 2024; only poor form shown over hurdles but he posted his best run of the season (in first-time cheekpieces) when fourth of 11 in 2m4f Sedgefield handicap 23 days ago; needs to build on it in retained headgear.

runners.comment: Offered little for Dianne Sayer this term; tongue tied for new yard with lots to prove
runners.spotlight: Has offered little in a handful of runs for Dianne Sayer this term, pulled up over C&D in January; tongue tied for his new yard with lots to prove after a break.

racecards.verdict: Philip Kirby's C&D scorer LONE STAR goes well under these ground conditions and teed herself up well with a very good recent C&D third
racecards.betting_forecast: 100/30 National Question, 9/2 Valtteri Its James, 5/1 Abbey Scope, 6/1 Camarrate,  Lone Star, 7/1 Toby Two Scoops, 14/1 Cher Tara, 16/1 Long Time Listener, 25/1 Achnamara,  Noble George,  The Final Brig, 33/1 Largy Meadow, 40/1 Diamond Trilogy

racecards.race_name: Acorn Catering Equipment Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Left alone to make winning chasing debut at Wetherby (2m4f); may strip fitter for Kelso.
runners.spotlight: Capable hurdler, placed in the 2025 Morebattle; left alone to make winning chasing debut at Wetherby (2m4f, good; 7-4) in October; was returning from a four-month break when last of four (beaten around 7l) in a Class 3 at Kelso six weeks ago; best hurdles form on a sound surface.

quotes.race: Every Race Live On Racing TV Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Two Mile Hurdle Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: That was a good performance. Old Gregorian got a lot of confidence from his last win and he'll be better again when he steps up to two and a half miles. He jumps hurdles quickly and well - Alan Doyle, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: Who knows if he'd have still won at Wetherby on his chasing debut if his rival hadn't unseated, but his jumping was very slick. He definitely wants two and a half miles and will improve going up in trip. 29-10-25

runners.breeder: S C E A Haras De Peyre
runners.owner: Mrs I C Sellars And Miss D C Sellars

prev_owners.owner: Mrs I C Sellars & Major Philip Arkwright

runners.comment: Authoritative winner of 2024 Perth Silver Cup; lacklustre since but stable in hot form
runners.spotlight: 21 months since his last win, an authoritative one in the Perth Silver Cup (2m4f, good to firm; from 5lb higher); beaten 26l, 16l and 14l respectively in three runs since April 2025; good ground is ideal, so probably worth considering with his trainer in such fine form.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Parisencore was consistent last season and deserved to win his two races. He relaxes well in front and pops away well. I don't think he can go up too much for that so hopefully there's a bit more to come - Nicky Richards, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A good, consistent handicap hurdler who's nearly top class. He ran a cracker when fourth in the Scottish Champion Hurdle at Ayr, having run well through the season. We've started schooling him over fences and we're looking towards 2m chases with him. He's a strong-running galloper and he'll be pretty exciting if he takes to fences. 25-10-23

runners.comment: Carlisle specialist (close to a career-high); "never travelling and jumped poorly" latest.
runners.spotlight: Carlisle specialist; sits close to a career-high mark following a gritty win there (2m, good to soft) in February; "never travelling and jumped poorly" in the Monet's Garden Series Final there three weeks ago; bit to prove for the time being, even acknowledging a 2024 C&D win.

quotes.race: Racing Post North Monet's Garden Series Final Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Hello Judge is is a lovely big, strong horse. He ran over three miles last time here but he's a two-and-a-half miler. It's a nice prize and this is the first time we've won one of the finals. We declared him for Hexham on Tuesday, thinking the ground here would be too quick - he'll not go there now! - Ian Hamilton, owner and trainer's husband.

quotes.race: Watch Racing TV Now Handicap Chase (Go North Monet's Garden Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I just had to try and get Hello Judge in a rhythm and it was good to see him get back to form. The stable has been a bit quiet lately but hopefully that's them turning the corner - Danny McMenamin, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Wetherby winner (2m4f) penultimate start; respectable third since; no issue with Newcastle
runners.spotlight: 7-52; enjoyed the run of the race, making all, at Wetherby (2m4f, soft; 18-1; from 6lb lower) on penultimate start; ran to a similar level (third) behind the newly blinkered Rath Gaul Hill back there subsequently; no issue with Newcastle; player with Alice Stevens claiming 3lb.

quotes.race: William Hill B.O.G Is Back Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: He likes it here. Geryville jumped well and travelled and it was our day today - Micky Hammond, trainer

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap Chase (Challenger Middle Distance Chase Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: We were just hoping for a nice run from Geryville. The ground has been so firm he hasn't been schooled over fences, he's just been over French-style hurdles on the all-weather. He jumped a bit big early on but hopefully he can win again-Micky Hammond, trainer.

runners.comment: In frame three times (Musselburgh) for H. Burns; competes from easing mark, needing more.
runners.spotlight: With Phil Kirby when left alone in a match at Kelso (3m, soft) in February 2024, that being his fourth (and most recent) win over fences; runner-up in this last year (beaten 11l) for Lizzie Quinlan; in the frame three times (Musselburgh) for Hugh Burns; competes from an easing mark, needing more.

quotes.race: Vickers.Bet Independent Family Owned Bookmaker Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Special Rate jumped brilliant. I let him run to the front down the back, I thought he'll stay anyway and he's kept galloping - Ross Chapman, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Won off this mark at Hexham (2m, good; in blinkers) last June; fortunes have dipped since.
runners.spotlight: Won off this mark at Hexham (2m, good; in added blinkers) last June; that was in a lower-grade contest (Class 4) and his productivity ebbed away thereafter (0-5; hurdles and fences); bit to prove off a 190-day absence; likely to draw benefit from this comeback run.

quotes.race: Living North Handicap Chase (Go North Monet's Garden Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Glory And Honour is a lovely horse and a joy to ride. He needs a really good gallop as he's such a strong traveller and doesn't find as much as you think he would. Today was an ideal scenario and it played into his hands. It was a nice opportunity to get his head back in front - Jonathan England, jockey.

quotes.race: bet365 Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought Glory And Honour would appreciate the good ground. He was 3lb better off with the favourite so I couldn't see why he started the price he did - Sam England, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's been on the go for a long time, mixing Flat and jumping, so he's having a holiday to freshen him up for the spring. The first-time blinkers helped him when he won a chase at Hexham in June. After he won over 2m2f at Pontefract, we ran him in the Durham National at Sedgefield as we thought he should stay a trip over jumps, but he doesn't. All his best jumps form is over 2m and 2m4f. 29-10-25

racecards.verdict: With the ground to suit and his trainer in fine form, it's possible that PARISENCORE can return to better form from this easing mark.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Geryville, 11/4 Parisencore, 4/1 Hello Judge,  Special Rate, 5/1 Glory And Honour

runners.comment: C&D winner on handicap debut (4lb lower) in Feb 2025; no luck since (0-2); merits respect.
runners.spotlight: Justified market support to make winning handicap debut over C&D (good to soft; from 4lb lower) in February 2025; failed to excel in a hood at Wetherby or Huntingdon (November/December); returns from a four-month break on better ground, which holds few fears; merits respect.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We're going to go to Cheltenham if we get in. I think we're good for 7lb or 8lb, which will probably put Bust A Move in the handicap. It's going to be touch and go. He was a very nice Flat horse and he's going to be a very nice hurdler - David Easterby, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Betfred "Hot Shots" Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: It's riding very soft today and that's probably suited Bust A Move as he's by Ribchester and is out of a dam that was placed in soft ground in France so I was always confident he would handle the ground. The trip was a bit of a worry as he can be a little bit keen, but there he was very settled after half a furlong and he just worked into it. He has picked up well and done it well - Billy Garritty, jockey.

runners.comment: Third in this last year; the winning run came to an abrupt end at Ayr (2m5f, soft) latest.
runners.spotlight: Weakened when third of five (13-8 favourite) in this last year; back to form, completing a February hat-trick (Sedgefield twice and Ludlow, rising steadily in the weights); reportedly "ran flat" when pulling up at Ayr (2m5f, soft; from 5lb lower) latest; needs to bounce back.

quotes.race: JTC Pizzalicious Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Thank You Blue jumped really well. He'll probably be better over a little bit further, I was just forcing him for the last half a mile. He was good over the last two and galloped to the line - Sean Quinlan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: Like Constitution Hill he's a son of Blue Bresil and it's incredible how jumping issues came to the fore with this guy - not over hurdles but over fences. He fell twice and was pulled up three times over fences but he's done very well this season back over hurdles, winning his last three. He'll run again under a penalty this week - he has two entries at Ayr on Friday, one over fences and one over hurdles. 04-03-26

runners.comment: Runner-up over fences at Sedgefield (2m) in February; slightly lower mark over hurdles.
runners.spotlight: Justified favouritism at Sedgefield (2m; second chase start) in February but no excuses when runner-up there (beaten 19l) a few weeks later; returns to hurdles (2-7) from a slightly lower mark, possessing C&D experience (beaten a nose in a maiden here in March 2025); possible.

runners.comment: Struggled since winning hurdles/stable debut at Kelso (2m) in March 2025; tongue-tie on.
runners.spotlight: Hasn't kicked on since making winning hurdles/stable debut at Kelso (2m, juvenile) in March 2025, failing to see out races at Doncaster, Kelso, and Ludlow; hopes are pinned on a revival with an added tongue-tie; trainer is 5-11 (45%) over jumps here in the last five years.

stable_tour.quote: He ran really well at Bangor on his reappearance. He jumped great and just had a blow from the second-last. He'll run in another novice hurdle in a fortnight before he loses his novice status on December 1. I think he can make into a decent horse and might be a Challenger Series Final horse for Haydock in the spring. I don't think we've seen the best of him and he can be progressive. 19-11-25

prev_owners.owner: One More For The Road II

runners.comment: Twice runner-up on the Flat here this winter; well beaten over hurdles at Fakenham latest.
runners.spotlight: Won a 2m juvenile contest here in November 2024, and added to his tally in a Series Final at Musselburgh (Class 2) the following spring; twice runner-up on the Flat here (1m2f) this winter, but well beaten over hurdles at Fakenham (2m) one month ago; others more obvious.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Go North Grey Bomber Juvenile Hurdle Series Final (Handicap Hurdle) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's been a real team effort to get Inappropriate here. This has been the plan for a while - his first run was excellent then we felt his subsequent two runs were ground-related and we needed to wait for better going so this race was the obvious one.  But we've had two scares. He stood on a nail with a hind foot and took a while to get over that. Then more recently he got cast and bashed a front leg and back leg. The vets and all the staff have been working so hard, he's been standing in buckets of ice for hours, and they've got him here. There was a worry for a time he wouldn't make it. It's worked out really well - Jedd O'Keeffe, trainer.

quotes.race: Paul Ferguson's Jumpers To Follow 'Introductory' Juvenile Hurdle (Go North Grey Bomber Qual') (GBB)
quotes.quote: We decided to have a punt at this race because we won this with a horse we bought off the Flat at the sales too. Even if we didn't win, it was a nice place to introduce Inappropriate. We've always liked him a lot at home and his jumping has been exceptional. Jumps trainers generally cannot compete buying the ones of the Flat anymore, with Australia and the Middle East getting them. We managed to find him though, and we'll let him learn his new job. It'd be nice if we can find another race with good prize-money like this - Jedd O'Keeffe, trainer.

runners.comment: Consistent for T. Davidson (366233); close third at Musselburgh (2m1f) latest; 2lb higher.
runners.spotlight: Ready Kempton winner (2m novices' handicap, good) for Daisy Hitchins last October; consistent for Tristan Davidson (366233), giving her best when a close third in the Sea Pigeon Series Final at Musselburgh (2m1f, good to soft) recently; 2lb higher but bang there with repeat.

racecards.verdict: The safest option is AS FAST AS WIND, who did her level best when a close third in a competitive series final at Musselburgh recently.

We'll try to find a weak maiden or novice hurdle and he'll also run back on the Flat once we get an official rating. He's shown plenty of speed. 04-03-26

runners.comment: Made breakthrough at Doncaster (2m4f, Class 5) in February; beaten since; back in a novice

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Go North Cab On Target Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I wouldn't call Diamond Koda ungenuine. He's been a bit unlucky, his jumping has let him down mainly, he's fluffed a hurdle at crucial parts of races. He wasn't right last time, he scoped dirty after that and we thought we'd got him right for today. We were pretty hopeful - Nick Kent, trainer.

prev_owners.owner: Miss J Bedi, J Bell And Partners

runners.comment: Well held in two bumpers (Musselburgh and Haydock); needs to settle better; hurdles debut.

runners.comment: Sets the benchmark; out of his depth in The French Furze here (Class 2; 2m6f) in November.
runners.spotlight: Hexham bumper winner for Stuart Coltherd; sets the benchmark, runner-up at Wetherby and Kelso (both 2m) in late 2024; marginally out of depth in The French Furze here (Class 2; 2m6f) in November; returns to a more appropriate level and is tongue-tied on first start for Sam England.

runners.comment: Lacked for pace when third in C&D maiden (beaten approximately 10l) in January; possible.
runners.spotlight: Fair bumper form and has shaped okay since introduced to hurdles (323); lacked the pace to stake a claim when third to Lewisham Grove in a C&D maiden (beaten approximately 10l) in January; is one to consider in this winnable novice.

runners.owner: Castle View Racing & W F Corbett
runners.comment: Kelso bumper winner (2m; 13-8 fav) last September; well beaten both attempts over hurdles.
runners.spotlight: Justified market support, making all in a Kelso bumper (2m, good; 13-8 favourite) last September; jumped poorly on hurdles debut at Catterick (2m) on New Year's Day, and well beaten back there (2m4f) a few weeks later; difficult to retain the faith.

runners.breeder: J C Haimet, Mme E Petit, Mme H Pet
runners.comment: Tailed off on hurdles debut at Wetherby (2m maiden; 250-1) a fortnight ago; discounted.
runners.spotlight: Regressive form in bumpers; fitted with a hood and tailed off on hurdles debut at Wetherby (2m maiden, good; 250-1) a fortnight ago; early days but she's still the first to discount.

racecards.verdict: A winnable novice. LOST FREQUENCIES has shown the most ability, so hopefully can make a winning debut for Sam England.

racecards.race_name: High Gosforth Park Golf Club Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 2 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners.breeder: Mrs A L Merry & Mr Brett Merry

runners.owner: Mrs I C Sellars And Miss D C Sellars

runners.comment: Bought for 60,000 euros after runner-up in Irish point; not discounted on his Rules debut
runners.spotlight: Bought for 60,000 euros after finishing runner-up in an Irish point last May; this son of Berkshire can't be discounted on his Rules debut for good yard.

runners.comment: Cut little ice in a pair of C&D bumpers either side of Christmas for Rebecca Menzies
runners.spotlight: Cut little ice in a pair of C&D bumpers either side of Christmas for Rebecca Menzies; lots more required for his new yard after a break.

runners.comment: Rare runner for yard and not out of things, particularly if betting speaks in his favour
runners.spotlight: 7,000euros 3yo; Son of Sea The Moon who is a brother to 1m6f-2m Flat (RPR 97) and 2m4f/2m7f hurdle winner Moon King and also a half-brother to French 1m4f-2m winner Marelie; unraced dam is closely related to Group-placed 1m winner Maid to Remember; a rare bumper runner for this yard and not out of things, particularly if the betting speaks in his favour.

runners.comment: Walk In The Park gelding; placed in Irish points either side of Christmas; possibilities
runners.spotlight: Walk In The Park gelding who fetched 45,000 gns as a 3yo and was placed in Irish points either side of Christmas; possibilities on his Rules debut.

runners.comment: The market can guide for this Lauro debutant
runners.spotlight: Lauro gelding; dam, unraced sister to 2m4f-2m7f hurdle/chase winner Shesupincourt, is a half-sister to useful winners First Drift (bumper and 2m-2m4f hurdle/chase) and Destroyer Deployed (bumper/2m4f hurdle/3m chase); the market can guide.

runners.comment: Jet Away mare who landed Irish point in January; a noteworthy newcomer for good yard
runners.spotlight: Jet Away mare who was purchased for £50,000 after landing Irish point on her debut in January; a noteworthy newcomer for good yard.

runners.breeder: M L And Mrs V P Enticott
runners.comment: Sans Frontieres mare; others appeal more on this occasion
runners.spotlight: Sans Frontieres mare; dam, 9.4f Flat winner (RPR 64), is a half-sister to useful 1m/1m1f winner Treasurer; others appeal more on this occasion.

runners.breeder: Mrs D M Ewart & Mr M Niven
runners.owner: Clova Farms And P D Niven
runners.comment: Arrigo gelding; the betting can guide for this newcomer

runners.comment: Last of nine in bumper at Hereford; son of Massaat needs to take a major step forward

quotes.race: British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBplus Race)
quotes.quote: Galilean Quality has been very coltish. He was in the preliminaries today and at the start, I had to keep him away from the other horses. He has definitely got better with each run, and the step up in trip has definitely helped - Clifford Lee, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Big step forward on handicap/seasonal debut when scoring at Wolverhampton; big player
runners.spotlight: Brought along steadily before taking a big step forward on his handicap debut when scoring at Wolverhampton (1m4f) on his return last month; up 4lb this progressive colt remains on a workable mark and rates a big player.

runners.comment: Completed AW hat-trick over C&D 46 days ago; well in the mix despite a further 6lb rise
runners.spotlight: Firmly on the up since sent handicapping and he completed a quick AW hat-trick over C&D 46 days ago; well in the mix despite a further 6lb rise.

racecards.verdict: Preference is for the improving MAGNETUDE, who still looks ahead of his mark despite being raised 4lb for his Wolverhampton win.

stable_tour.quote: He's been training nicely. He was placed over six furlongs last season but we'll look to run him over seven soon. He's definitely shown enough to think he can win races. 17-04-24

runners.comment: Continued in form since C&D win off 2lb lower; this is less competitive; she needs a look

quotes.race: Mutasaabeq At The National Stud Handicap
quotes.quote: Bint Al Daar wasn't travelling that well early doors but she crept into it and I got a lovely split when I needed it. Kevin Phillippart de Foy's horses are in good form and she enjoyed the ground - Jack Mitchell, jockey.

runners.comment: C&D winner for George Wood (only time he's ridden him) last July off 3lb lower; chance
runners.spotlight: C&D winner for George Wood (only time he's ridden him) last July off a 3lb lower mark; entitled to have come on for last month's comeback here and is one to consider.

runners.comment: Hard to win with and on the downgrade but remains consistent; should go well again
runners.spotlight: Hard to win with and on the downgrade but remains consistent; nudged up a couple of pounds following two near-misses last month but will be happier back up in trip and should go well once more.

quotes.race: Follow @AtTheRaces On Twitter Handicap
quotes.quote: Adam Kirby gave Pleasant Man a great ride and rode exactly to instructions. He is quite a lazy type and I don't think any other jockey would have won on him - Grant Pritchard-Gordon, representing owners Brook Farm Bloodstock.

stable_tour.quote: Formerly a good staying handicapper on the Flat, he was found to have bled when pulled up in the Adonis Hurdle at Kempton and had a breathing operation straight afterwards. He's a good horse and will leave that form well behind when resuming over hurdles in five or six weeks. 31-10-22

runners.breeder: Lofts Hall Stud, B Sangster, New England

prev_owners.owner: David Spratt & Sean Jones & Mrs Lynne Lyons

runners.comment: Three wins from five C&D starts; continues in good form and his claims are strong
runners.spotlight: C&D record is currently three wins and two seconds from five starts; most of his career wins have come in the winter but he continues in good form and has strong claims.

quotes.race: Unibet More Extra Place Races Handicap
quotes.quote: Tony [Carroll, trainer] said to take my time as Tortured Soul is an easy ride and to ride him with confidence as he's the best horse in the race. The key for him is getting him to relax and when they sprinted into the straight I knew I had plenty of horse to coax and to get there as late as possible. He's done it well and is racking up a few wins - Neil Callan, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.comment: His only below-par effort on Tapeta came over 1m6f; handicapper has given him every chance
runners.spotlight: Dual Newcastle winner who's generally struggled since returning from more than a year off; his only below-par effort on Tapeta came when not seeing out 1m6f, however, and the handicapper's given him every chance.

runners.comment: May not have seen out 2m last time but he's had plenty of chances over various trips now
runners.spotlight: 0-8 for Charlie Fellowes; three runs for current yard, best of them on second occasion when wearing second-time cheekpieces (1m5f, Polytrack) in February; may not have seen out 2m last time but he's had plenty of chances over various trips now.

runners.owner: The Ridgeway Racing For Fun Partnership
runners.comment: This is more realistic now handicapping in headgear but others have more pressing claims
runners.spotlight: Went close in a couple of ordinary small-field bumpers late last summer but has struggled on the Flat and over hurdles since; this is more realistic now handicapping in headgear for the first time but others have more pressing claims.

racecards.verdict: The vote goes to the consistent TORTURED SOUL, whose record over C&D currently stands at 11221. Pleasant Man is second choice.

runners.comment: Soundly beaten in C&D event last month on belated debut
runners.spotlight: Soundly beaten in C&D event last month on belated debut; best watched.

runners.comment: Bumper winner; has achieved nothing in two Flat runs
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner for previous yard; has achieved nothing in two AW Flat contests for new stable, latest over C&D.

stable_tour.quote: He's got a very good Flat pedigree, as a half-brother to this year's French 1,000 Guineas  second Kathmandu, and was beaten only two and a half lengths when third in a bumper at Sedgefield. He's well up to winning one before going hurdling. 16-10-24

runners.comment: Record of 222 since being gelded; ran well with blinkers fitted latest; solid chance
runners.spotlight: Has looked quirky but he ran well in first-time blinkers at Lingfield (1m2f; handicap debut) most recently, taking record since being gelded to 222; helps to set the form standard, with headgear retained.

runners.comment: 1,500,000gns yearling; by Dubawi; wears headgear on debut; heed the market signals
runners.spotlight: 1,500,000gns yearling; Dubawi half-brother to three winners, notably Morgan Le Faye (1m2f-1m4f including Group 2; RPR 111); dam French 1m3f-2m4f scorer (including Group 1; 112); perhaps not straightforward as he's already gelded and wears headgear on debut but his purchase price and pedigree are notable; powerful yard also runs Sailor Song; heed the market signals.

runners.comment: Already a big player on his Doncaster effort and could well take another step forward
runners.spotlight: Seemed to need the outing/experience in C&D event on debut; fared better at Doncaster (1m2f) since, finishing second of nine; already a big player on form and could well take another step forward; respected.

runners.comment: 20,000gns 2yo; by Camelot; one of two newcomers in the field; check the betting
runners.spotlight: 20,000gns 2yo; Camelot half-brother to five winners, notably Bolshoi Ballet (1m-1m4f including US Grade 1; RPR 119); dam unraced; one of two newcomers in the field; check the betting.

runners.comment: Fared better last time but needs further progress for today's additional distance
runners.spotlight: Ran below market expectations at Newcastle (7f) in sole 2yo start; rather belied his bigger odds with second of four at Wolverhampton (9.5f) on reappearance but needs further progress for today's additional distance.

racecards.verdict: Al Azd's seconditis may well continue, with fellow major form contender SAILOR SONG likely to show further progress.
racecards.betting_forecast: 2/1 Al Azd,  Sailor Song, 9/4 King Of Thebes, 10/1 Stepanov, 16/1 Sir Griflet, 100/1 Guthrum,  Masterpiece

runners.comment: Won first two handicaps, over C&D and at Wolverhampton; may have had stiff task since
runners.spotlight: Progressive 2yo who was involved in tight finishes for all three 5f Tapeta handicaps, winning over C&D and at Wolverhampton before having what may have been a difficult task at the weights at Newcastle in December; can be dangerous off the same mark.

runners.comment: Benefited from the drop to 5f when C&D winner latest; may improve on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Early ability at 6f and 7f but she benefited from the drop to 5f when winning over C&D in February; that wasn't particularly competitive but as an unexposed improver she needs considering on her handicap debut.

runners.owner: Nick Bradley Racing 16 And Jmr Partners
runners.comment: Good early 5f form as 2yo; has share of weight but creditable 4th at Wolverhampton latest
runners.spotlight: Ready to go early as a 2yo, winning on second start and close up in a 5f Listed race last May; her handicapping goose appeared to be cooked as a result but she was a bit better than the bare result at Wolverhampton (5f) recently and she shouldn't be far away.

quotes.race: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For horses In Band D) (EBF Rest' Qual') (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Saucy Jane had a poor draw at Pontefract and she ran respectably but her homework had been showing us she'd improved. I'm delighted for all of my team, especially Harriett [Bryce], who rides her every day and broke her in as well. She looks like a filly on the up and a nice prospect. We'll see how she gets on when she gets home but we could look at the Hilary Needler Trophy back here [May 24] or the Marygate at York next Friday. We can always dream of Ascot. She looks a nice filly and if she continues to progress there's no reason why we can't look at it - Jack Morland, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She's a nice filly. She ran very well in the Listed Marygate at York behind Secret Hideaway and arguably would have finished closer if she'd had a bit of cover. We're hopefully going to see the Marygate form franked because there are horses who ran in that race running at Royal Ascot this week. Last time out she went to Chantilly for a Listed race but found it all a bit too much in the preliminaries and boiled over a bit. She's had a bit of a holiday now and was back trotting on Monday. There's a Listed race in Deauville over five furlongs that I'm going to target with her and I think she's a stakes-class filly. 18-06-25

runners.comment: Front-running 2yo promise; showed resolution when C&D winner on return; set to go well
runners.spotlight: Front-running 2yo promise although Beverley's stiff 5f proved too much on two occasions; gelded in the close season and was seen to advantage on C&D comeback, showing resolution to hold off his rivals, the first two well clear; back up 3lb; set to go well.

runners.comment: Beat Saucy Jane on 5f debut; lesser effort on sole AW start; off since September
runners.spotlight: Weights chance on defeat of Saucy Jane on Pontefract form (5f) last spring, when they finished first and second, but some water under the bridge since then and he ran one of his lesser races on sole AW start, at Newcastle in June; needs to have improved during his break to win today.

quotes.race: Racing TV Sky Channel 424 EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C/D) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: We fancied Ice Cold Alex a bit. He didn't cost much and his sire Soldier's Call isn't the most fashionable. He has a fantastic pedigree and has always worked nicely. He did the job well - Ollie Pears, trainer.

runners.comment: Busy 2yo; in good form over 5f and 6f on heavy/soft turf in the autumn; unraced on AW
runners.spotlight: Busy 2yo who came into his own in the autumn, wide-margin 5f winner at Ffos Las (heavy) and creditable shows over 6f (soft and heavy) on final two starts; unraced on AW and prolific winning sibling Spoof was 0-11 on sand for this yard so has some questions to answer.

runners.comment: Won 6f Chelmsford novice for the Crisfords; 8th of 11 on handicap debut; new yard
runners.spotlight: Tongue tied in three AW starts for the Crisfords, winning a 6f Chelmsford novice in August but only eighth of 11 on handicap debut at Lingfield in September; sold 15,000gns since; no tongue-tie on first 5f run; too many questions this time.

racecards.verdict: Comic Strip can be dangerous but AMBISHIO was suited by this C&D when making his AW debut and he could be hard to peg back.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Ambishio, 3/1 Comic Strip, 7/2 Hayynah, 5/1 Saucy Jane, 8/1 Proof, 12/1 Ice Cold Alex, 20/1 Riffa Spirit

runners.spotlight: A three-time winner early in 2026, including over C&D, for Ian Williams; not discredited on just her second run for current yard when fifth in 1m handicap here two weeks ago; in the mix off a slipping mark.

quotes.quote: Pink Socks had a good campaign last year without winning. This mare runs very well for Amy Jo. They went good and fast and came back to her, but she's a smashing mare and stronger this year - Tim Doyle, trainer

runners.comment: Good second at Kempton latest, not enjoying smooth run; can go well despite a 2lb rise
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 4yo who got off the mark here in January and posted a good second of nine to Aim For The Bull in 1m Kempton handicap 17 days ago, not enjoying the smoothest of passages under 2f out; enjoys a 1lb weights pull here and can go well.

runners.comment: Winless since August 2024 but comes here in decent nick; place prospects off easing mark
runners.spotlight: Winless since August 2024 but he comes here in decent nick, fifth of nine in 7f Lingfield handicap 17 days ago; place prospects off an easing mark.

runners.comment: C&D winner but below par of late; it's now 13 starts since that victory
runners.spotlight: C&D winner but below par of late, beating one in 1m handicap here two weeks ago; it's now 13 starts since that victory too.

stable_tour.quote: We've always thought he has a lot more ability than he's shown. He's got a low rating of 55 having been 0-5. He ran poorly on his last run 04-09-25

runners.comment: Made it two wins in last three starts at Chelmsford 16 days ago; not taken lightly
runners.spotlight: Made it two wins in his last three starts in 7f handicap at Chelmsford 16 days ago; up 4lb but he's not taken lightly in his current mood.

runners.comment: Course scorer; good Wolverhampton second final run for Thomas Faulkner; not out of things
runners.spotlight: Course scorer who returned to form in a headgear change when second of eight in 7f Wolverhampton handicap 29 days ago on his final run for Thomas Faulkner; not out of things for his new handler.

runners.comment: In good form, third in 1m classified event here last time; ought to be thereabouts again
runners.spotlight: Kickstarted 2026 with C&D victory (third one) and has continued in good form, fading late on when third of 11 in 1m classified event here last time; ought to be thereabouts again.

Not long after that he developed a foot problem, which means he hasn't raced since May of last year. I hope he's back in June but I'm not rushing him. You know what they say, ‘No foot, no horse'. 09-04-25

runners.comment: Best effort of season when third at Wolverhampton latest; can make her presence felt
runners.spotlight: Without a victory since 2024 but she posted her best effort of the season when third of nine in 7f Wolverhampton handicap 19 days ago; she can make her presence felt off an unchanged mark.

runners.comment: Last of seven in Wolverhampton classified event latest; cheekpieces go on now
runners.spotlight: Poor maiden and she came in last of seven in 9.5f classified event at Wolverhampton 25 days ago; cheekpieces are reached for.

runners.comment: Three-time C&D winner; off 12 months off before well-held fifth at Newcastle last month
runners.spotlight: Veteran three-time C&D winner; off 12 months before a well-held fifth of seven in 6f Newcastle handicap last month; needs to take a big step forward.

runners.comment: It's 18 starts since last victory and only ninth of 12 in 6f Kempton handicap last month
runners.spotlight: It's now 18 starts since his last victory and he came in only ninth of 12 in 6f Kempton handicap last month; others are preferred.

runners.comment: C&D winner; not disgraced when fifth over C&D last time; no forlorn hope
runners.spotlight: Ended a losing run in classified event over C&D in February and not disgraced back in handicap company when fifth over C&D following month; no forlorn hope.

runners.comment: Solid third at Newcastle last time; this course winner needs considering
runners.spotlight: Started 2026 with 1m classified success at Newcastle and posted a solid third of 11 in similar event there (7f) last time; this course winner needs considering.

runners.comment: On a lengthy losing sequence but solid third at Wolverhampton latest; not dismissed
runners.spotlight: On a lengthy losing sequence but she fared better than of late when third of 11 in 6f classified event at Wolverhampton 18 days ago; this C&D winner needs considering.

runners.comment: Largely in good form in 2025; back from eight months off in a change of headgear
runners.spotlight: Yet to register a victory but she was largely in good form in 2025; returns from eight months off in a change of headgear.

stable_tour.quote: She's ready to run and has had a few entries. She was only small when she came to us. The owners had her in a field down the road. She's done nothing wrong whatsoever and she's improved after each gallop, so she's going to be the type to improve after a run or two. She could be okay. 21-06-24

runners.breeder: Highclere Stud & Mr Ilyas Emir Karadag
runners.comment: Without a victory since 2023 and he has yet to make the frame in seven starts in 2026
runners.spotlight: Without a victory since 2023 and he has yet to make the frame in seven starts in 2026; hard to warm to.

racecards.verdict: This can go to CAPTAIN PICKLES (nap), who did well to score at Wolverhampton last time given he challenged wide.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Captain Pickles, 5/1 Heretic,  I Can Boogy, 7/1 Autumn Angel, 8/1 Fort Augustus, 10/1 Turbo Command, 12/1 Drafted,  Thomas Equinas, 16/1 Mickey Mongoose, 20/1 Mavetheforcebewivu, 33/1 Barney's Bay

runners.comment: String of consistent efforts on Tapeta in headgear; no surprise to see him defy a 5lb rise
runners.spotlight: String of consistent efforts on Tapeta since sporting headgear, culminating in last weekend's Wolverhampton win off 5lb lower; not a lot of luck round Newcastle prior to that and it would come as no surprise to see him follow up.

prev_owners.owner: Ms Sara Hattersley And Miss Tracey Mann

runners.comment: Surprise winner over C&D off 3lb lower in February; not convinced over 7f twice since
runners.spotlight: Stable yet to get rolling for the year but he was a bright spot when springing a surprise over C&D off 3lb lower in February; not entirely convinced over 7f a couple of times since and holds each-way claims.

quotes.race: Titanium Racing Club EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB)
quotes.quote: That was brilliant. The steering wheel seemed to fall off Thankuappreicate last time and he couldn't be got under control, but he was straightforward today. I don't know what the level of that form is, but you couldn't ask for more than what he did today - Nigel Tinkler, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was unlucky not to win at Ayr last time. He didn't get the best of passages and had to be switched, and he couldn't quite quicken up for that level of experience. We've got to run him once more to get a handicap mark for nurseries. I'm sure he'll win races. 27-07-22

runners.comment: Returns to handicap company on a workable mark and confidence will have been boosted
runners.spotlight: Plenty of short-priced defeats before finally off the mark on his seventeenth start in a Newcastle maiden a few weeks ago; hard to know the merits of that but he returns to handicap company on a workable mark and confidence will have been boosted.

stable_tour.quote: A nice horse who's been very unlucky to still be a maiden. We've probably placed him badly a couple of times and he's bumped into one or two. He's talented and can win off his mark. He could go for the Ayr Bronze Cup but I have a theory 5f on soft ground is going to be his bag. There might be a weak maiden to win with him and he'll strengthen up over the winter again. 04-09-25

runners.comment: Another 3lb higher tonight; happiest in front; lot will hinge on how things play out early
runners.spotlight: Made all when winning at Kempton early last month (said to have appreciated being able to dominate); unable to get to the front down to 5f here next time and is another 3lb higher tonight; a lot will hinge on how things play out early.

quotes.race: Sporting Times/Sri Lanka Awaits You Handicap (London Sprint Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Early Release has been unlucky with draws and a few things haven't gone right in his previous runs this year, but it was nice to see him put it all together today. He's a horse who has to relax. I felt like I had plenty left going into the final two furlongs and I thought it would take a good one to come and get me  - Billy Loughnane, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Three wins, two seconds and a third to his name from 11 starts over C&D; shortlisted
runners.spotlight: Three wins, two seconds and a third to his name from 11 starts over C&D; beaten as favourite (behind Farandaway) here a month ago but is on a workable mark now and one to consider back under Rossa Ryan.

runners.owner: L Bond/Sheikh Aymen Jawad Al Hamandi/Ptr
runners.comment: Shown enough of late to suggest he can be a factor tonight in first-time headgear
runners.spotlight: C&D winner last autumn who's been showing enough round Newcastle of late to suggest he can be a factor tonight, especially if first-time headgear ekes out a little more.

prev_owners.owner: S Bulmer, P Hebdon & R Taylor

runners.comment: This his time of year but arrives off the back of a string of modest efforts
runners.spotlight: This his time of year, with two May wins in 2024 and a hat-trick last spring; arrives off the back of a string of modest efforts, though, the returning visor not making much difference last time.

prev_owners.owner: Scott McMillan, Frank Reay & J P McKeown

runners.comment: Interesting to see how he goes in the market back from five months off upped 3lb
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish gelding who closed out last season with a narrow beating of Kirkdale off 3lb lower at Newcastle (first-time blinkers; goes in first-time cheekpieces here); interesting to see how he goes in the market back from five months off.

runners.comment: Hampered and eased off when a beaten-favourite last time; unexposed as a sprinter
runners.spotlight: Hampered and eased off when a beaten-favourite last time, having previously got off the mark on his first run in a sprint (5f) off 6lb lower; unexposed as a sprinter.

racecards.verdict: Kirkdale is second choice behind JESSE LUC, who boasts a good record both over C&D and for Rossa Ryan (three wins from four starts)
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Kirkdale,  Farandaway, 4/1 Jesse Luc, 5/1 Sherlock, 10/1 Thankuappreciate, 12/1 Early Release,  Wish This, 20/1 Northcliff

racecards.race_name: Come Racing For Free 18th June Handicap

runners.comment: Back in 0-55 company and holds claims especially if he settles better in a first-time hood
runners.spotlight: Often fluffs the start and is always reliant on luck given his run style; not had the breaks since a Wolverhampton win in January but is back into 0-55 company for the first time since and holds claims, especially if he settles better in a first-time hood.

runners.comment: Well supported ahead of his C&D comeback in February; one to consider for a yard in form
runners.spotlight: Lost his way last year after a spring win for Eve Johnson Houghton off 13lb higher; well supported ahead of his C&D comeback in February, when faring much better off this mark, and is one to consider in a first-time tongue-tie for a yard going well of late.

runners.comment: Landed a sixth victory on Tapeta three weeks ago; never won off a mark quite this high
runners.spotlight: Landed a sixth victory on Tapeta when going in at Wolverhampton off 3lb lower three weeks ago; never won off a mark quite this high but gives his trainer, who also run He's An Angel, a decent hand.

runners.comment: Prolific winner on Tapeta but never here; arrives in good form but high in the weights
runners.spotlight: Prolific winner on Tapeta but never round here; arrives in good form after two Wolverhampton victories last month, latterly off 3lb lower, but has never won on the AW off a mark quite this high; trainer also runs East Tyrone.

runners.comment: Does most racing now over 5f; typically consistent of late off a sliding mark
runners.spotlight: Does most racing now over 5f and hasn't won over this trip in three years; typically consistent of late, off a sliding mark, but he's only finished placed once from ten starts round here.

quotes.race: Watch Racing Free Online At Coral Handicap
quotes.quote: We've always liked Buraback but he's had issues with the bend here in the past and I told John Egan to get something on his outer this time. He got a nice run up the straight and maybe we'll run him on a straighter track next time - John Best, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's new to the yard from Jessica Macey and has had just one run for us when down the field at Wolverhampton. He had a few small issues, which we have ironed out, and the plan is to go down the turf route now. Hopefully when he gets on the grass he'll start to find some improvement. 22-03-23

runners.comment: Goes well here, has slid to a fair mark and been offering more of late; player
runners.spotlight: Most wins come on Polytrack but goes well here, has slid to a fair mark and been offering more of late; won twice before for headgear coming off (cheekpieces removed tonight) and is a player in an open handicap.

runners.owner: Alan And David Fairhurst And P Kirby
runners.comment: Will always come with risks attached given his run style; expensive to follow this year
runners.spotlight: Odds-on to miss the break and an even shorter price to pull hard; will always come with risks attached given his run style and has been expensive to follow this year; goes back to blinkers from a visor tonight for a yard also responsible for Fircombe Hall.

quotes.race: John Smith's Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: East Tyrone ran a great race on debut. Beverley was a run too quick after that but he's shown what he's capable of. We've always liked him. There's more to come and he'll improve with racing - Adam Ryan, assistant trainer.

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late Earl Cadogan

runners.comment: Hard to win with; essentially regressive and is some way down the pecking order
runners.spotlight: Hard to win with and made it 0-12 on the AW when well held at Wolverhampton last time; essentially regressive and is some way down the pecking order.

runners.comment: Better run in the tongue-tie, without seeing out 7f, latest gave her something to build on
runners.spotlight: Won three nurseries for George Scott two summers ago but has regressed sharply since, coming 26lb down the weights for her current yard; a better effort in a first-time tongue-tie, without seeing out 7f, last time gave her something to build on.

stable_tour.quote: She's tall, imposing and covers a lot of ground, she looks a really smart prospect for the yard. It's hard to know quite when she'll get started but she's showing us enough at home to suggest she'll be able to run over six furlongs. 29-03-24

runners.comment: Regressive maiden who's finished well held in two runs back in 0-50 classified company
runners.spotlight: Regressive maiden who's finished well held in two runs back in 0-50 classified company; would be a surprise winner switching from cheekpieces to a first-time visor.

runners.comment: Non-runner
runners.spotlight: Non-runner.

racecards.verdict: Kamekist holds claims for an in-form yard but HE'S AN ANGEL is preferred now he's back down to 0-55 company and fitted with a hood.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Piperstown, 4/1 Kamekist, 5/1 Fircombe Hall, 7/1 Buraback, 8/1 He's An Angel, 10/1 Man On A Mission,  East Tyrone, 12/1 Port Hedland,  Griselda, 20/1 Beautiful Things

runners.comment: Torrid run up the home straight when only eighth on handicap debut (7f, AW); can do better
runners.spotlight: Unable to justify joint-favouritism on her handicap debut at Southwell (7f) two weeks ago but that run can easily be excused as she ran into plenty of trouble in the home straight; capable of better.

runners.comment: Two AW wins over shorter this winter; placed over 1m latest; should be in the shake up
runners.spotlight: Two wins over shorter on AW this winter; solid third at Lingfield (1m) two weeks ago; promise on turf early in his career and another good run should be forthcoming.

runners.comment: Ten-race maiden; had wind op since last seen; returns in a competitive event
runners.spotlight: Ten-race maiden who ended 2025 with two heavy defeats; subsequent wind operation could help but he returns in a competitive race for the grade.

runners.comment: C&D winner; fair mark on 2025 best; should make a bold bid from the front
runners.spotlight: Front-runner; won twice at Newmarket (1m, good to soft) last summer; only 2lb higher than for the second success and he is fully effective at this track; considered.

runners.comment: Strong at the finish when 2nd on Monday's handicap debut (8.6f, AW); unexposed; key player
runners.spotlight: Close second at Wolverhampton on Monday's handicap debut (8.6f), finishing off his race well; the front two drew clear on that occasion and rates a major player with Hector Crouch taking over in the saddle; turf debut.

runners.comment: Absent 540 days; makes stable debut over a trip that may be on the sharp side
runners.spotlight: Failed to win in seven runs for Ed Walker but she finished second in three of them; sold for 7,000gns in October 2024; returns from a 540-day absence and dropping back to 1m far from certain to suit; on the plus side, she has been dropped 6lb during her absence.

runners.comment: Regressing but drops into a 0-60 and last month's return should have sharpened him up
runners.spotlight: Struggled in 2025 and fared little better on last month's return to action (after wind surgery); tumbling down the weights but comes with risks attached.
